text: The verges in this picture are part of the public road.
explanation: LESSON 1 – ‘The public road’.The grass verges are part of a public road.The open road runs until a canal or a private property.

text: Has this car driver his hands correctly on the wheel?
explanation: LESSON 1 - 'The public road'.Put your hands in the position ' 10 to 2 ' or also ("quarter to three").

text: What traffic sign will the driver see on this road?
explanation: LESSON 1 - 'The public road'.Sign 1: steep hill down wards.Sign 2: steep hill upwards.

text: What is the name of the part of the public road marked yellow?
explanation: LESSON 1 - 'The public road'.The road is a part of the public road.

text: Do you commit a violation if you set the navigation app of your mobile phone while driving?

options.text: No, if you have a hands-free kit.
No, because you don't talk to anyone on the mobile phone.

explanation: LESSON 1 - 'The public road'.You must keep your hands correctly on the steering wheel while driving.When setting up an app, your attention goes to something completely different than to the traffic on the roadway.

text: What does this sign mean?
explanation: LESSON 1 - 'The public road'.Meaning: No trough road (for all users).It is a positive instruction sign.

text: This combination of signs indicates a potential hazard when there is snow or ice on the roadway.
explanation: LESSON 1 - 'The public road'.

text: You have a provisional licence B. From what time are you not allowed to drive a car anymore on a Friday evening?
explanation: LESSON 1 – ‘The public road’.From Friday night 22:00h till Saturday morning 06:00h.From Saturday night 22:00h till Sunday morning 06:00h.From Sunday night 22:00 till Monday morning 06:00h.From the night before a legal holiday 22:00 till the next day 06:00h.From the evening of a legal holiday 22:00 till the next day 06:00h.

text: How should you react if you approach a horse with a rider and the horse rears up in fear?
explanation: LESSON 1If a horse on the road gets scared by a car and rears up, the driver must stop the vehicle and avoid any sudden movements, so that the rider can calm the horse and regain control of the situation before it escalates.

text: You have a provisional licence B. It is the 2nd January. What time are you allowed to drive a car?
explanation: LESSON 1 – ‘The public road’.From Friday night 22:00h till Saturday morning 06:00h.From Saturday night 22:00h till Sunday morning 06:00h.From Sunday night 22:00 till Monday morning 06:00h.From the night before a legal holiday 22:00 till the next day 06:00h.From the evening of a legal holiday 22:00 till the next day 06:00h.

text: This road sign means: dead end ...
explanation: LESSON 1 - 'The public road'.

text: You drive 105kph on a regular road with a maximum speed limit of 90kph. What are the consequences?

options.text: Your driving licence will be suspended for a certain period.
You have to do a theoretical and practical examination again.

explanation: LESSON 1 - 'The public road'.When you drive more than 40 km/h faster than the maximum speed limit on regular roads, a judge will decline you the right to drive a motor vehicle for the duration of at least 8 days or up to maximum 5 years.Tip exam: Read very well the text of chapter 12 in your book.

text: When a dirt track is hardened in concrete or tarmac only the last meters before to join the other public road, then it is no longer considered a track but a road.
explanation: LESSON 1 - 'The public road'.Also, if the last meters are hardened, it remains a dirt road.

text: This combination of signs indicate a slippery road within a distance of 7.5km because of ice or snow.
explanation: LESSON 1 – ‘The public road’.Two arrow up is, over a distance of ...

text: What does this warning sign mean?
explanation: LESSON 1 - 'The public road'.Meaning: two or more bends, the first to the right.Warning signs are placed 150 meter for a danger.

text: This driver feels safe when driving in the middle of the road. But is he allowed to do that?
explanation: LESSON 1Drivers must drive on the right side of the road when possible.Driving in the middle or on the left without reason is a traffic violation.

text: Do the traffic regulations apply to a private road?
explanation: LESSON 1 - 'The public road'.Roads with a sign ‘private property’ are not public roads.The traffic regulations don’t apply there. Except when the owner gives permission to be used by everyone.

text: What does this road sign mean?
explanation: LESSON 1 - 'The public road'.

text: What does this warning sign mean?
explanation: LESSON 1 - 'The public road'.Meaning: slippery road.Warning or danger signs are placed 150 meter for a danger.

text: This warning sign means 'danger'. But where is the danger?

options.text: From here and over the next 100 metres.

explanation: LESSON 1Warning signs have a triangular shape with a red border.They are normally placed about 150 metres before the danger. (In built-up areas, this distance may be shorter.)

text: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Take a ferry to the other side.
Deep canal next to the road.

explanation: LESSON 1 - 'The public road'.This road sign is a warning or danger sign.Meaning: way out on a quay or a bank.

text: You are medically unable to drive. Within how many working days you have to go with your driver's license to the Town Hall?
explanation: LESSON 1 - 'The public road'.Within four days after the day (Saturday-Sunday-public holidays not included) that you know about it, you have to report it to the municipality.

text: You drive on this public road. You want to set up your GPS. Where can you stop?

options.text: You are not allowed to stop.

explanation: You are not allowed to stop on the roadway and on the side lane

text: Do the traffic regulations apply to the rail vehicles using the public road?
explanation: LESSON 1 - 'The public road'.Tram drivers do not have to follow the traffic regulations, except the orders of an authorized person and the traffic lights.

text: At what speed limit can you drive on a central carriageway in the Walloon region?
explanation: 70 km/h throughout the country.

text: What kind of traffic sign is this?
explanation: LESSON 1 - 'The public road'.Almost all rectangular signs with a red border are warning or danger signs (not all of them). Warning signs are placed 150 meter for a danger.Meaning: road narrows on both sides.

text: What is the name of the part of the public road with the yellow marked question mark?
explanation: LESSON 1 - 'The public road'.It is the road of a motorway.

text: Do the traffic regulations apply to rail vehicles using the public road?
explanation: LESSON 1 - 'The public road'.Tram drivers do not have to follow the traffic regulations, except the orders of an authorized person and the traffic lights.

text: Which one of the signs indicates a speed hump?
explanation: LESSON 1 - 'The public road'.Both signs are warning signs.The meaning of A = uneven road.

text: What does this warning sign mean?
explanation: LESSON 1 - 'The public road'.Meaning: loose chippings (= fly-away stone)Warning signs are placed 150 meter for a danger.

text: You have a provisional driving licence B. Are you allowed to drive a car on Christmas during the day?
explanation: LESSON 1 – ‘The public road’.From Friday night 22:00h till Saturday morning 06:00h.From Saturday night 22:00h till Sunday morning 06:00h.From Sunday night 22:00 till Monday morning 06:00h.From the night before a legal holiday 22:00 till the next day 06:00h.From the evening of a legal holiday 22:00 till the next day 06:00h.

text: Is the yellow marked part part of the public road?
explanation: LESSON 1 - 'The public road'.The grass verges are part of a public road.The public road runs until a canal or a private property.

text: What kind of a sign is this?
explanation: LESSON 1 – ‘The public road’.It is an information sign.Meaning: No through road (for all road users).

text: Can someone with epileptic seizures drive a car?

options.text: Never, because they can always have another seizure.
Only after a seizure-free period can a doctor grant permission to drive.

explanation: Explanation:A person with epileptic seizures is generally not allowed to drive.After a first seizure, there is a driving ban of 6 months.Someone with chronic epilepsy who, after treatment, has been seizure-free for 1 year may, with approval from a specialist doctor, be allowed to drive again.After a new seizure, there is again a driving ban of 1 year.

text: What is the part of the public road with the question mark called?
explanation: LESSON 1 - 'The public road'.The road is a part of the public road.

text: What warning sign indicates a steep hill?
explanation: LESSON 1 - 'The public road'.% character up = steep hill upward.% character down = steep hill down wards

text: You have a provisional driving licence B. Are you allowed to drive a car on a Sunday evening after 10pm?
explanation: LESSON 1 – ‘The public road’.From Friday night 22:00h till Saturday morning 06:00h.From Saturday night 22:00h till Sunday morning 06:00h.From Sunday night 22:00 till Monday morning 06:00h.From the night before a legal holiday 22:00 till the next day 06:00h.From the evening of a legal holiday 22:00 till the next day 06:00h.

text: What does this traffic sign mean?

options.text: You are approaching a tram stop.
Tram tracks are located on the roadway.

explanation: LESSON 1This is a warning/danger sign.Watch out for trams, which always have priority.

text: What is the maximum speed limit on an ordinary road In Flanders?
explanation: LESSON 1 - 'The public road'.On ordinary roads in Flanders: up to 70 km/h.Unless traffic signs or rules impose a different speed limit.(In Wallonia and Brussels region: 90 km/hour).

text: This combination of signs means that the lane...

options.text: May be slippery due to snow or ice.
May be slippery due to snow or ice or oil spills.

explanation: LESSON 1 - 'The public road'.

text: What does this sign mean?
explanation: LESSON 1 - 'The public road'.Meaning: steep hill down wards.It is a warning sign.

text: What is the maximum speed limit on an ordinary road in Wallonia ?
explanation: LESSON 1 - 'The public road'.On ordinary roads in Flanders and Brussels region: up to 70 km/h.Unless traffic signs or rules impose a different speed limit.(In Wallonia: 90 km/hour).

text: This picture is taken from the car you drive. Are you still allowed to drive to the right lane?
explanation: LESSON 2 – ‘The lanes’.There's a white interrupted line.

text: Zipper merging is required. Where should you merge?

options.text: As soon as it is safe.

explanation: LESSON 2Zipper merging is mandatory when a lane disappears and traffic is heavily slowed down or stopped (like in a traffic jam). You must merge just before the disappearing lane ends.When entering a motorway, zipper merging is not used—instead, you must give priority to drivers already on the motorway.

text: What is the maximum speed allowed for the white car on this ordinary road in the Walloon Region?
explanation: LESSON 2On an ordinary road, under normal conditions, the maximum permitted speed in the Walloon Region is 90 km/h.In the Flemish Region and the Brussels Region, it is 70 km/h.

text: The left and right lane are closed. Zip-merge is obligatory Car B drives first. Who may drive next?

options.text: Car A on the middle lane.
Car C on the left lane.

explanation: LESSON 2 – ‘The lanes’.The car in the middle lane gives first priority to the car on the right lane and then priority to the car on the left lane. Then car A may drive.

text: What is this part of the public road, with the question mark, called?
explanation: LESSON 2 – ‘The lanes’.It is the roadway.This roadway has two lanes.

text: What is indicated by this yellow line?
explanation: LESSON 2 – ‘The lanes’.It is the roadway. With a road marking it’s divided into two lanes.

text: Which drivers are also allowed to drive on this bus lane?

options.text: Only cyclists and mopeds class A.
Cyclists and mopeds class A and B.

explanation: LESSON 2 – ‘The lanes’.The plate at the bottom indicates that cyclists may also drive on this bus lane.

text: Are you allowed to be stationary on a bus lane to let someone out of the car?
explanation: LESSON 2 – ‘The lanes’.The traffic regulations forbit on a bus lane to be stationary (1 April 2023) or to park.You may also not drive on a bus lane, except the last meters for a turn at the crossroads to sort.

text: What does this information sign mean?

options.text: Advanced road sign, indicating a temporary crossover on the verge.
Advanced road sign, indicating a lane diversion.
Advanced road sign, indicating traffic allowed in both directions on a part of a one way road.

explanation: LESSON 2 – ‘The lanes’.Meaning: Advance road sign indicating a temporary crossover on the verge.Information sign.

text: Why are you required to zipper-merge?
explanation: LESSON 2Zipper-merging is mandatory in very slow traffic or traffic jams when a lane ends.You may only merge into the free lane right before the lane reduction.

text: When the road of a motorway has at least three lanes, the drivers can choose freely what lane to drive.
explanation: LESSON 2 – ‘The lanes’.You should always ride, as much as possible, on the right side of the roadway.

text: Which drivers are also allowed to drive on this bus lane?
explanation: LESSON 2 – ‘The lanes’.Motorcycles can use this bus lane too.

text: Are you allowed to stop on these road markings on your left to let someone out of the car?
explanation: LESSON 2 – ‘The lanes’.On a traffic displacement area you are not allowed to drive, to wait and to park.

text: Is the driver of the white car allowed to turn left to enter the driveway of his home?
explanation: LESSON 2 – ‘The lanes’.On a white or yellow interrupted stripe between the lanes you can drive.

text: On this road marking you are not allowed to ride/drive, to be stationary or to park. What is it called?

options.text: Traffic displacement area or a gore.

explanation: LESSON 2 – ‘The lanes’.On a traffic displacement area or a gore you are not allowed to drive, to be stationary and to park.

text: Yellow road markings have the same meaning as the white ones.
explanation: LESSON 2 – ‘The lanes’.Yellow and white road markings have the same meaning.If you see white and yellow at the same time, then you only need to take into account the yellow.

text: What part of the public road is marked by the yellow line?
explanation: LESSON 2 – ‘The lanes’.It is a lane of the motorway.The roadway has two lanes in each direction of travel.

text: Is the driver of this car allowed to turn left to enter the driveway of his home?
explanation: LESSON 2 – ‘The lanes’.On a white or yellow solid stripe between two lanes you are not allowed to drive, even not to reach the driveway of your home.

text: What is this part of the public road, with the question mark, called?
explanation: LESSON 2 – ‘The lanes’.It is a lane.

text: Which road sign indicates a narrowing of the roadway to the right?
explanation: LESSON 2 – 'Traffic Lanes'.Sign 1: Danger sign.Sign 2: Sign indicating a narrowing having the importance of a traffic lane.

text: Is the white car allowed to cross over the white broken line and overtake the red car?
explanation: LESSON 2 – ‘The lanes’.But over a white solid line you may not drive to overtake.

text: This picture is taken from the car you drive. Are you still allowed to turn left here?
explanation: LESSON 2 – ‘The lanes’.Yes, because there's a white dashed line to the left of you.

text: What does this traffic sign mean?

options.text: Advanced road sign indicating a temporary diversion.
Advanced road sign indicating a temporary crossover on the verge.
Advanced road sign indicating a temporary lane closure.

explanation: LESSON 2 – ‘The lanes’.Meaning: Advanced road sign indicating a temporary diversion.Positive instruction sign.

text: What is the maximum speed allowed for the red car on this ordinary road in the Brussels Region?
explanation: LESSON 2On an ordinary road, under normal conditions, the maximum permitted speed in the Walloon Region is 90 km/h.In the Flemish Region and the Brussels Region, it is 70 km/h.

text: Within a built-up area you have two lanes in your driving direction. Can you continue to drive in the left lane?
explanation: LESSON 2 - 'The lanes'.

text: You have taken the wrong exit. Are you still allowed to turn left here?
explanation: LESSON 2 – ‘The lanes’.On a traffic displacement area you are not allowed to drive, to wait and to park.

text: Is car A allowed to turn left?
explanation: LESSON 2 – ‘The lanes’.You may not drive over a solid white line.

text: The yellow line in this picture indicates a road divided into two lanes.
explanation: LESSON 2 – ‘The lanes’.This roadway is not divided into lanes, because there is no white interrupted or white solid line in the middle of the road. It is a roadway, on which one can drive in two directions.

text: What does this information sign mean?

options.text: Advanced road sign indicating a temporary crossover on the verge.
Advanced road sign indicating two way traffic on a normally one way road.
Advanced road sign indicating a temporary lane closure.

explanation: LESSON 2 – ‘The lanes’.Meaning: advanced road sign indicating two way traffic on a normally one way road.Information sign.

text: Is the driver of the white car allowed to overtake the blue car on the left.
explanation: LESSON 2 – ‘The lanes’. There is a solid yellow line in the middle of the roadway.

text: What part of the public road is marked by the yellow line?
explanation: LESSON 2 – ‘The lanes’.The roadway.This roadway is not divided into lanes.

text: Dense traffic and a two lane closure In what order are the cars allowed to drive on?
explanation: LESSON 2 – ‘The lanes’.Tip exam: read very well the explanation in your manual.

text: What kind of sign is this traffic sign?
explanation: LESSON 2 – ‘The lanes’.Advance warning or arrow markings, showing your choice of lane. This sign can indicate the different directions. The white line may be broken or solid.

text: What kind of traffic sign is this?
explanation: LESSON 2 – ‘The lanes’.Meaning: lane reduction to the right.Positive instruction sign.

text: The driver realizes he is driving in the wrong direction. Is he allowed to turn around here?

options.text: Yes, if he does not hinder other drivers.

explanation: LESSON 2You are not allowed to cross a solid white line — neither to turn off nor to make a U-turn.

text: How many lanes do you see on this public road?
explanation: LESSON 2 – ‘The lanes’.On the image you can see three traffic lanes and a hard shoulder.

text: What is the maximum speed limit on a regular road in Flanders?
explanation: LESSON 2 – ‘The lanes’.In Flanders and Brussels region: 70 km/hour unless traffic signs or rules impose a different speed limit.In Wallonia: 90 km/hour).

text: Dense traffic and a lane closure.

options.text: Zip-merge is not obligatory but recommended and courteous.

explanation: LESSON 2 – ‘The lanes’.Zip-merge is obligatory.

text: This sign means: road works. What kind of sign is it?
explanation: LESSON 2 – ‘The lanes’.Most triangular signs with a red border are hazard signs.Hazard signs stand 150 meter for a danger.

text: What does this information sign mean?

options.text: Advanced road sign indicating a temporary lane diversion.
Advanced road sign indicating a temporary lane closure.
Advanced road sign indicating a temporary crossover on the verge.

explanation: LESSON 2 – ‘The lanes’.Meaning: Advanced road sign indicating a temporary lane closure.

text: Which vehicles are you not allowed to overtake with your car after this sign?

options.text: Only a cyclist and a class A moped.
A cyclist, a class A moped and a motorcycle.

explanation: LESSON 3This sign marks the beginning of a bicycle zone.In a bicycle zone, motor vehicles (including mopeds) are not allowed to overtake cyclists, speed pedelecs and bicycles up to 1 m wide.Other vehicles may be overtaken if they are driving too slowly.The maximum permitted speed in a bicycle zone is 30 km/h.

text: Are you allowed to drive your car on this road marking?
explanation: LESSON 3 – ‘The bicycle lane’.This road marking does not indicate a cycle path.

text: Drivers of mopeds class A, once past this board …

options.text: ... are allowed to drive on the cycle lane.
... are not allowed to drive on the cycle lane.
... must drive on the cycle lane.

explanation: LESSON 3 – ‘The bicycle lane’.In any case, cyclists and mopeds class A have to do itIn this case, says the charger plate, that mopeds class B also have to do it.

text: In this bicycle zone, the boy is riding an e-scooter at 20 km/h. Is the driver of the car allowed to overtake the e-scooter on the left?

options.text: Yes, because it is not a cyclist.

explanation: LESSON 3A bicycle zone starts at the “begin bicycle zone” traffic sign and ends at the “end bicycle zone” traffic sign.In a bicycle zone:• cyclists, speed pedelecs and personal mobility devices (such as an e-scooter) may use the roadway;• motor vehicles are allowed to drive there, but they are not allowed to overtake cyclists, e-scooters or similar vehicles;• the maximum speed is 30 km/h.➡️ Even if the e-scooter is riding at 20 km/h, overtaking is not allowed.

text: You are driving your car in a bicycle zone. Are you allowed to overtake a step?
explanation: LESSON 3 - 'Cyclists'In a bicycle zone, motor vehicles are not allowed to overtake cyclists or users of mobility devices (such as electric steps), even if there is enough space.The maximum speed is limited to 30 km/h.

text: Is the blue car allowed to use the cycle lane a bit in order to overtake on the right, the car that wants to turn left?

options.text: Yes, but not more than 50% of the cycle lane.

explanation: LESSON 3 – ‘The bicycle lane’.A cycle lane is a part of the public road, reserved for the use of bicycles and 2-wheeled class A mopeds (max 25 km/hour). You are not allowed to drive your car on a cycle lane and you are not allowed to park or wait to let a passenger in or out of your car.

text: From how many people must a group of cyclists be accompanied by at least 2 supervisors?
explanation: From 51 cyclists.

text: The driver of the red car only looks through the windshield and in the mirrors. Which cyclist is in the blind spot?
explanation: LESSON 3 - 'Cyclists'.

text: Are you allowed to pass this group of cyclists over the solid white line?

options.text: Yes, if you can keep a sideways distance of 1.5 meters.

explanation: LESSON 3 - 'Cycle path and cyclists'.

text: The car in front of you wants to turn left. There is no cyclist on the cycle path next to you. Are you allowed to drive on the cycle path to pass the car on the right?
explanation: Lesson 3 - 'Cyclists'The cycle path is not part of the roadway.You are not allowed to drive your car on it.

text: What is the maximum speed limit in a bike zone?
explanation: LESSON 3 – ‘The bicycle lane’.The maximum speed limit = 30 km/hour.In a bike zone cars are not allowed to overtake the cyclists or speed pedelecs.

text: This girl is 14 years old. There is no cycle path. May she ride on the pavement?

options.text: Yes, only within a built-up area.
Yes, only outside a built-up area.

explanation: LESSON 3If there is a cycle path, a cyclist must use it (unless it is not rideable).It is forbidden to cycle on the pavement within a built-up area, except for children under 10, who may always ride on the pavement or on the raised verge.Outside built-up areas, cyclists may, if there is no usable cycle path and provided they ride on the right-hand side of the road, ride on the pavement or on the raised verge.

text: Enter a number. You are not allowed to be stationary or to park on the road within … meters of a crossing for cyclists and two-wheeled mopeds.
explanation: LESSON 3 – ‘The bicycle lane’.Up to 5 meters for a crossover it is not allowed.Beyond the crossover it’s allowed.

text: Enter a number. A child must be less than (...) years to ride on a footpath within built-up areas.
explanation: LESSON 3 – ‘The bicycle lane’.In built-up area or outside built-up area: under the age of 10 years (31/5/2019).Outside built-up areas, all the cyclists, except if there is a bike path is in their direction of travel.

text: This sign means that you should be careful when changing direction, because cyclists and riders of two-wheeled mopeds follow the same public road.
explanation: LESSON 3 – ‘The bicycle lane’.This sign means that you should be careful when changing direction, because cyclists and riders of two-wheeled mopeds follow the same public road.

text: The cycle lane ends and the moped driver must drive onto the road.

options.text: The moped driver has to give way to the drivers on the road.
The drivers on the road must give way to the driver of the moped.

explanation: LESSON 3 – ‘The bicycle lane’.If a warning/danger sign says that the bicycle lane ends, they have right of way and therefore the drivers of cars and motor vehicles on the road have to give priority.

text: From how many cyclists in a group must 2 road captains be present?
explanation: LESSON 3 – ‘The bicycle lane’.

text: Are mopeds allowed to drive past this sign?

options.text: Mopeds class A and class B.

explanation: LESSON 3 – ‘The bicycle lane’.Pedestrians, cyclists and mopeds class A are allowed to drive past this instruction sign.

text: Are you allowed to overtake a moped on the left with a car in a bicycle zone?
explanation: In a bicycle zone, motor vehicles are not allowed to overtake a cyclist, scooter, or any other means of transport considered equivalent to a bicycle.Other vehicles (for example, a moped) may be overtaken on the left in a bicycle zone, provided that the maximum permitted speed is not exceeded.

text: How much lateral distance should you leave when you overtake a cyclist in a built-up area?
explanation: Outside the built-up area 1.5 meters.

text: From how many cyclists in a group, are these cyclists not obliged to ride on the bicycle lane?
explanation: LESSON 3 – ‘The bicycle lane’.Groups of 15 to 50 cyclists are not obliged to follow the cycle paths. They are allowed to drive with two next to each other on the roadway. Provided they stay together (grouped). Groups of less than 15 cyclists must follow the same rules as individual cyclists.

text: This sign indicates a bicycle zone. But where does a bicycle zone end?

options.text: At the sign: End of bicycle zone.
At the sign End of bicycle zone or at the next intersection.

explanation: LESSON 3 – ‘The bicycle lane’.The maximum speed limit = 30 km/hour.In a bike zone cars are not allowed to overtake the cyclist.

text: How many meters is this warning sign placed in front of a crossing for cyclists and two-wheeled mopeds?
explanation: LESSON 3 – ‘The bicycle lane’.Warning/danger signs are placed at approximately 150 meters of the danger.

text: May a user of a motorized personal mobility device be overtaken by motor vehicles in a bicycle zone?
explanation: LESSON 3Users of motorized personal mobility devices are treated the same as cyclists.In a bicycle zone, cyclists may not be overtaken by motor vehicles. This overtaking ban also applies to motorcycles and mopeds of class A and B. The speed pedelec, however, is considered a bicycle and may overtake other cyclists.On the other hand, cyclists may overtake each other and other road users. Overtaking must always be done on the left. A cyclist may also pass stationary vehicles on the right.Priority vehicles (police, fire brigade, ambulance with siren and flashing light) are still allowed to overtake cyclists. If a priority vehicle is approaching, clear the roadway.

text: Can you overtake a speed pedelec with your car in a bike zone?
explanation: LESSON 3 – ‘The bicycle lane’.Drivers of motor vehicles (eg cars, vans, trucks, mopeds class A and B) are NOT allowed to overtake cyclists and speed pedelecs in a bike zone.

text: This sign means:

options.text: No entry for cyclists and mopeds class A.

explanation: LESSON 3 – ‘The bicycle lane’.Meaning: no entry for cyclists.Prohibitive sign.

text: Are you allowed to park a car on this suggested cycle lane?
explanation: LESSON 3 – ‘The bicycle lane’.A bicycle reserved/suggested lane is not a bicycle lane at all. It is nothing else but a painted part of the road, where you can drive, park or wait.

text: Enter a number. How many km/h is the maximum permitted speed in a bicycle zone?
explanation: LESSON 3 – ‘The bicycle lane’.Motor vehicles (including mopeds) are not allowed to overtake cyclists, speed pedelecs and bicycles up to 1 m wide in a bike zone.

text: Which drivers are not allowed to drive on the cycle lane past this sign?
explanation: LESSON 3 – ‘The bicycle lane’.If the pedestrians and bicycles are not next to each other, but among each other, then only cyclists and pedestrians use this part of the public road.

text: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Crossing for cyclists and two-wheeled mopeds.
Cyclists are allowed to ride on the road.

explanation: LESSON 3 – ‘The bicycle lane’.This istruction sign is placed at the crossing.

text: This girl is 8 years old. She is cycling on the roadway within a built-up area. May she also ride on the raised pavement?
explanation: LESSON 3If there is a cycle path, a cyclist must use it (unless it is not rideable).It is forbidden to cycle on the pavement within a built-up area, except for children under 10, who may always ride on the pavement or on the raised verge.Outside built-up areas, cyclists may, if there is no usable cycle path and provided they ride on the right-hand side of the road, ride on the pavement or on the raised verge.

text: When the verge is too small, you are allowed to park your car on a small part of the cycle lane.
explanation: LESSON 3 – ‘The bicycle lane’.A car should not ride on a cycle lane, not standing still and not parking.

text: How should you react when driving on a motorway near roadworks?

options.text: Drive at a maximum speed of 30 km/h.
Always keep a lateral distance of 2 metres.
Drive carefully so as not to endanger the road workers.

explanation: LESSON 4When driving near roadworks on a motorway, you must:- respect the applicable speed limits;- keep a sufficient distance;- drive carefully and attentively (watch out for workers, equipment and stationary vehicles);- make sure you do not endanger or hinder anyone.

text: On the motorway you have to drive minimum (…) km/hour in normal circumstances.
explanation: LESSON 4 – ‘The motorway’. At least: 70 km/hour (of course in the right circumstances)Maximum: 120 km/hour.

text: What is the maximum speed allowed in Wallonia on an ordinary road when using studded tyres?
explanation: LESSON 4Studded tyres may be used from 1 November to 31 March on vehicles with a maximum authorised mass of up to 3.5 tonnes.The maximum permitted speed is:- on motorways and roads with 2×2 lanes separated by a central strip: 90 km/h;- on ordinary roads in all regions: 60 km/h.

text: There is stationary traffic on the motorway. Can you drive on the hard shoulder the last few meters before an exit?
explanation: You are not allowed to drive on a hard shoulder.

text: Do you have to turn on the indicator on a motorway entrance?
If you want to enter the motorway via the insertion lane ... A ... the direction indicator must light up. B ... the direction indicator may light.
What does this road sign indicate?
explanation: LESSON 4 - 'Motorway'.A traffic interchange, because you can drive from one motorway to another without any problem.

text: What does this combination of signs mean?

options.text: From here on until the exit maximum 90kph.
From here on 90kph. You have to leave the motorway at the first exit.

explanation: LESSON 4 – ‘The motorway’. This speed limit only applies on the exit.

text: Is a reflective safety jacket obligatory in the car?
explanation: LESSON 4 – ‘The motorway’. . A reflective safety jacket. A warning triangle.. An extinguisher.. A first aid kit.

text: Are the cars allowed to ride on the rush-hour lane (spitsstrook)?
explanation: LESSON 4 – ‘The motorway’.If a green arrow hangs above the rush-hour lane, cars may drive on that lane.

text: When you place a warning triangle on the hard shoulder, other drivers travelling in your direction must see the triangle from a distance of (…) meters.
explanation: LESSON 4 – ‘The motorway’. When you stop on a breakdown lane, you have to put a warning triangle at least 100 meters behind your car immediately.It must always be visible for oncoming traffic from a distance of 50 meters.

text: The maximum speed limit on a motorway is (…) km/hour.
explanation: LESSON 4 – ‘The motorway’. At least: 70 km/hour (of course in the right circumstances)Maximum: 120 km/hour.

text: This picture is taken from the car you’re driving in. Are you allowed to drive to the right lane to take the exit?
explanation: LESSON 4 – ‘The motorway’. It is allowed, because at your right hand side is a broken white line.

text: You are on a motorway entrance ramp, but you forgot to start your GPS. Can you stop behind the white line?

options.text: I can stop behind the white line because I am not yet on the motorway.
I cannot stop behind the white line because I am already on the motorway.

explanation: LESSON 4 - 'Motorway'The entrance ramp is part of the motorway. Stopping or parking on the ramp is prohibited.

text: Are you allowed to stop on a motorway at this sign to send an urgent message?
explanation: LESSON 4On a motorway, you may only stop on an emergency bay if your vehicle breaks down or in case of a real emergency. Sending a message, even an urgent one, is not a valid reason. Stopping without a justified reason is dangerous and prohibited.

text: Are the students with a provisional driving licence B allowed to practice/train on a motorway?
explanation: LESSON 4 – ‘The motorway’. Drivers with a provisional driving licence B must also exercise on the motorway.

text: What is the maximum speed limit for the blue car on this motorway?
explanation: LESSON 4 – ‘The motorway’. The speed limit only applies to the bus lane.

text: A motorway with three lanes in your direction of travel. Between which lanes can a motorcycle ride when there is a traffic jam?
explanation: Between the 2 left lanes.

text: This sign indicates the start of a motorway. What kind of sign is this?
explanation: LESSON 4 – ‘The motorway’.Information sign.Start or entry of a motorway.

text: Traffic jam on the motorway. You may only merge at the end of the merging lane.
You want to join a motorway. Do you have to drive to the end of the insertion lane first?
explanation: LESSON 4

text: You didn’t go to a driving school, but your dad teaches you how to drive a car. Are you allowed to practice/train on the motorway?
explanation: LESSON 4 – ‘The motorway’. Drivers with a provisional driving licence B must also exercise on the motorway.

text: What is the maximum speed limit on the motorway when you drive with studded tires?
explanation: LESSON 4 – ‘The motorway’. Studded tyres can be placed from 1 November till 31 March on vehicles with a M.G.W. up to 3.5 ton.On motorways and roads with 2x2 lanes with a central berm: 90 km/hour.On regular roads: 60 km/hour.

text: You have to drive minimum (…) km/hour in normal circumstances on a motorway.
explanation: LESSON 4 – ‘The motorway’. At least: 70 km/hour (of course in the right circumstances)Maximum: 120 km/hour.

text: The driver of this grey car wants to go to Hasselt. Which lane must he drive on?
explanation: LESSON 4 – ‘The motorway’.

text: The black car (yellow circle) is allowed to drive maximum (…) km/hour on the motorway on that spot.
explanation: LESSON 4 – ‘The motorway’. This speed limit 70 km/hour only applies on the exit.

text: On a motorway, the red car is driving in the wrong direction. What are you doing?

options.text: You continue slowly on the hard shoulder.
You stop on the hard shoulder.
You continue on the right-hand lane.

explanation: LESSON 4 – ‘The motorway’.

text: When there is dense traffic on the access of a motorway …
explanation: LESSON 4 – ‘The motorway’.On the access of a motorway, you don’t have to zip-merge.

text: Are you allowed to stop on the access of a motorway to let in a colleague who wants to join you.
explanation: LESSON 4 – ‘The motorway’. The ramp is a part of the motorway.On a motorway, you may not stop to let passengers on or off.

text: The driver of this car realizes that he has taken the wrong driveway. Can he still drive backwards?
explanation: LESSON 4 – ‘The motorway’. The driveway is part of the motorway.Reversing on a motorway is a serious offence.

text: An accident on the motorway. The driver positions the red warning triangle. Where should the passengers stay?
explanation: LESSON 4 – ‘The motorway’.The safest place is behind the crash barriers.

text: Are you allowed to stop on the breakdown lane to provide assistance in an accident that happened in the other direction.
explanation: LESSON 4 – ‘The motorway’. It is forbidden to go on foot on the lanes of a motorway.

text: You want to drive on to the motorway via the merging lane.

options.text: You accelerate as soon as possible on the merging lane.
You accelerate when you drive on the right lane.

explanation: LESSON 4 – ‘The motorway’. You have to accelerate as soon as possible on the merging lane.

text: When your car breaks down or with an accident on the motorway you place the warning triangle at least (…) m behind the vehicle, so the oncoming traffic from behind has a clear view of the situation.
explanation: LESSON 4 – ‘The motorway’.When you stop on a breakdown lane, you have to put a warning triangle at least 100 meters behind your car immediately.It must always be visible for oncoming traffic from a distance of 50 meters.

text: What do you see on this sign?

options.text: The number of an international road.
The number of a regular way.

explanation: LESSON 4 – ‘The motorway’. It is an international road.In Belgium that are all motorways, but abroad, that are sometimes ordinary roads.

text: What is the meaning of this sign?
Must you use your indicator when you enter the motorway via the acceleration lane?

options.text: No, because you can only drive in that direction.

explanation: LESSON 4What does Article 13 of the traffic regulations say?Before carrying out a manoeuvre or a movement that requires a lateral displacement or a change of direction, the driver must indicate their intention in good time by using the direction indicators, if the vehicle is equipped with them, or otherwise, if possible, by a hand signal. This indication must stop as soon as the lateral movement or change of direction has been completed.

text: When is it allowed to drive on the peak-hour lane if there is no green arrow above it?

options.text: You may not drive on it.
It is allowed to exit or enter the road.

explanation: LESSON 4

text: Are you allowed to stop on the breakdown lane to text a message?
explanation: LESSON 4 – ‘The motorway’. You may not drive on a breakdown lane, not stand still and not park.So do not stop to answer your mobile phone or to check the road map.

text: There is heavy traffic on the motorway entrance ramp. When are you allowed to merge?

options.text: You may merge as soon as it is safe to do so.
You must follow the cars in front of you to the end of the ramp before merging.

explanation: LESSON 4The zipper principle does not apply when entering a motorway.So you do not have to drive to the end of the ramp before merging.You may merge wherever it is safe to do so.

text: A driver wants to insert. The driver of the red car:

options.text: ... must drive for a while in the left lane.
... may drive for a while in the left lane.

explanation: LESSON 4- 'Motorway'.If the left lane is clear, he may drive in that lane for a while to make insertion easier. But it is not an obligation. (courteous driving behavior).

text: What is the maximum permitted speed for a car with studded tyres on a motorway?
explanation: LESSON 4Studded tyres may be used between 1 November and 31 March on vehicles with a maximum authorised mass up to 3.5 tonnes.Speed:– Motorways and roads with 2×2 lanes separated by a median: maximum 90 km/h.– Ordinary roads: maximum 60 km/h.

text: What‘s there at 1600 meters?
explanation: LESSON 4 – ‘The motorway’. There are no junctions on a motorway. But there are places where two motorways merge. This place is called an interchange. Via an interchange you can drive from one motorway to another.

text: The ambulance with your father on board, drives 140 km/hour. Are you allowed to follow it?
explanation: LESSON 4 – ‘The motorway’. Maximum: 120 km/hour.

text: What does this road sign indicate?
explanation: LESSON 4 - 'Motorway'.A traffic interchange, because you can drive from one motorway to another without any problem.

text: What does this traffic sign mean?
explanation: LESSON 4 – ‘The motorway’.Information sign.End or exit of a motorway.

text: When you need help, you dial the international emergency number (…).
explanation: LESSON 4 – ‘The motorway’. 112 is the international emergency number.Important for the exam.

text: Where must the reflective safety vest be located?

options.text: Inside the interior of the car.
In the trunk of the car.

explanation: LESSON 4 - 'Motorway'The reflective safety vest, also known as the yellow vest, must be located inside the vehicle’s interior, within easy reach, and not in the trunk. It is recommended to store it in the glove compartment, under the driver’s seat, or in a door pocket so that it is immediately accessible to the driver if they need to exit the vehicle on a motorway or a road for motor vehicles.

text: The maximum speed limit on a motorway is (…) km/hour.
explanation: LESSON 4 – ‘The motorway’. At least: 70 km/hour (of course in the right circumstances)Maximum: 120 km/hour.

text: There is a traffic jam. The grey car drives on the left lane on this motorway. A motorcycle wants to overtake between the left and the middle lane. Where should the car driver drive on the lane?

options.text: As far to the left as possible.
As far to the right as possible.

explanation: LESSON 4 – ‘The motorway’. In a queue motorcycles are allowed to ride:. between the two left lanes of traffic.. at a maximum speed of 20 km/hour faster than the other vehicles.. and at a maximum speed of 50 km/hour.So the grey car drives as far as possible to the left, to give place.

text: Which of these signs won’t you see at a motorway?
explanation: LESSON 4 – ‘The motorway’. Sign A: regular road.

text: When the road of a motorway is segregated into at least 3 lanes, the drivers are allowed to choose the lane they want to drive in.
explanation: LESSON 4 – ‘The motorway’. If possible, you should always drive on the right lane.

text: Are towing services allowed to drive on the hard shoulder while working?
explanation: LESSON 4Police, emergency services and towing services (while working) may drive on the hard shoulder, the peak-hour lane and the emergency corridor.

text: When should you wear the fluorescent jacket in the event of a breakdown on a motorway?
explanation: LESSON 4 – ‘The motorway’.The fluorescent jacket must be mandatory in the car and the driver must always wear it in the event of a breakdown.

text: When you drive past this sign, you know that …

options.text: ... from here on until 1500m ahead you are allowed to drive maximum 70 km/hour on the right lane.
... at the distance of 1500m you are allowed to drive maximum 70 km/hour on the right lane.

explanation: LESSON 4 – ‘The motorway’. At the distance of 1500m you are allowed to drive maximum 70 km/hour on the right lane.

text: Which statement is correct about the speed on the motorway?

options.text: you should always drive at least 70 kph.
you should adjust the speed to the circumstances.

text: On a motorway it is prohibited to tow a car with an emergency link.
explanation: LESSON 4 – ‘The motorway’. It is forbidden since 1 March 2014.

text: The photo is taken from the car you are driving. You want to enter the motorway. Which statement is correct?

options.text: You must drive to the very end of the acceleration lane.

explanation: LESSON 4When you enter a motorway via an acceleration lane,you must give way to traffic already driving on the motorway.That is why there is a yield (inverted triangle) road sign.You are not required to drive to the end of the acceleration lane.You may merge as soon as you have enough speed and it can be done safely.

text: A motorway. Who has priority?
explanation: LESSON 4 - 'Motorway'.If you are entering a motorway, you must give priority to drivers who are already driving on the lanes.

text: 500 meters further is an exit. Where do you ride on the exit?

options.text: At the beginning of the exit.
Approximately in the middle of the exit.
As far as possible at the end of the exit.

explanation: LESSON 4 – ‘The motorway’. At the beginning of the exit.

text: What do you see on this sign?

options.text: The number of an international road.
The number of a regular road.

explanation: LESSON 4 – ‘The motorway’. Number of an international road.Information sign.

text: When you need assistance on an express road and there is no emergency phone, you dial the international number (…).
explanation: LESSON 5 – ‘The express road’.112 is the international emergency number.(Important for the exam).

text: You want to test your car and you drive 167 km/hour on this express road.

options.text: This is an offence and you will be fined.
This is an offence and your driving licence can be suspended immediately.

explanation: LESSON 5 – ‘The express road’.Exam Tip: read very well the explanation in your book under Chapter 12.

text: The driver of the brown car keeps driving on the left lane. Is the blue car allowed to overtake on the right?
explanation: LESSON 5 – ‘The express road’.It would be a very serious breach of the rules, because you are only allowed to overtake on the left.

text: When a car breaks down or with an accident on an express road the warning triangle must be placed at least (…) meters behind the vehicle so that other drivers travelling in your direction can see the triangle from a distance of 50 meters.
explanation: LESSON 5 – ‘The express road’.Motorway: 100 meters.Express road: 30 meters.

text: Are you allowed to drive on an express road with a moped class B?
explanation: LESSON 5 – ‘The express road’.Motor vehicles with their trailer may on a motorway driving, except:. Mopeds;. Agricultural vehicles;. Quadricycles without passenger compartment;. Dragging fairground vehicles.

text: On a motorway, only a towing service that has been called by the police can tow a car. What happens on an express road?

options.text: You may ask a friend to tow your car.
A towing service that you call can tow.
The police will request a towing service.

explanation: LESSON 5 – ‘The express road’.If your car breaks down on a highway or an express road, the police call a towing service they prefer.

text: What do these signs mean?

options.text: Start of a built up area.

explanation: LESSON 5 – ‘The express road’.Meaning: start of a built up area.Information sign.

text: On this express road in Flanders, the driver of the blue car is allowed to drive maximum (…) km/hour.
explanation: LESSON 5 – ‘The express road’.The express road runs in a built-up area.

text: What is the maximum speed limit of a car on this express road?
explanation: LESSON 5 – ‘The express road’.120 km/hour because the directions are separated by a berm.

text: Beyond which traffic sign must you drive at least 70 km/h, if conditions allow?
explanation: LESSON 5Only on a motorway (sign 1) does a minimum speed of 70 km/h apply, if conditions allow. On an express road (sign 2), this obligation does not exist.

text: You are not allowed to drive past this sign with a car.
explanation: LESSON 5 – ‘The express road’.Meaning: end of an express road.Information sign.

text: What is the maximum speed limit (… km/hour) a car is allowed to drive on this express road within a built up area in the Brussels region?
explanation: LESSON 5 – ‘The express road’.Within a built-up area in Flanders and Wallonia is the maximum permitted speed 50 km/h.

text: This sign indicates the start of an express road. What kind of sign is this?
explanation: LESSON 5 – ‘The express road’.It is an information sign.

text: Is this car allowed to turn right here?
explanation: LESSON 5 – ‘The express road’.The indication or information sign says: end of the express road.

text: On this express road In Wallonia with 2x2 lanes, a car is allowed to drive maximum (…) km/hour.
explanation: LESSON 5 – ‘The express road’.In Flanders: 70 km/hour unless traffic signs or rules impose a different speed limit.In Wallonia: 90 km/hour.In Brussels-capital region: 70 km/hour.

text: What is the maximum speed allowed for the white car on this road in the Brussels Region?
explanation: LESSON 5It is a normal carriageway divided into two lanes.The maximum permitted speed in the Flemish and Brussels Regions is 70 km/h.In the Walloon Region, it is 90 km/h.

text: When must a driver who has broken down on a motorway or express road, stopped on the hard shoulder, wear a fluorescent safety vest?
explanation: LESSON 4When a driver breaks down on a motorway or express road and leaves the vehicle, wearing a fluorescent safety vest is always mandatory.This applies both during the day and at night.

text: Where must the reflective safety vest be kept?

options.text: In the passenger compartment or in the trunk.

explanation: LESSON 5When a vehicle stops on a motorway or a road for motor vehicles and the driver gets out at a place where parking is prohibited, the driver must wear a reflective safety vest.The vest must be kept inside the passenger compartment, not in the trunk, so it can be put on before exiting the vehicle.

text: What does this blue information sign mean?
explanation: LESSON 5 – ‘The express road’.Meaning: end of an express road.

text: On this express road in Flanders the driver of the blue car is allowed to drive maximum (…) kph.
explanation: LESSON 5 – ‘The express road’.In Flanders: 70 km/hour unless traffic signs or rules impose a different speed limit.In Wallonia and Brussels-capital region: 90 km/hour).

text: Who must wear a reflective safety jacket on an express road when leaving the car at a place where waiting and parking is prohibited.
explanation: LESSON 5 – ‘The express road’.Only the driver. But passengers do best as well.

text: What is the maximum speed limit (… km/hour) a car is allowed to drive on this express road with 2x3 lanes outside a built up area?
explanation: LESSON 5 – ‘The express road’.120 km/hour because the directions are separated by a berm.

text: What is the maximum speed limit of a car on this express road?
explanation: LESSON 5 – ‘The express road’.120 km/hour because the directions are separated by a berm.

text: On this express road with 2x2 lanes you are allowed to drive maximum (…) km/hour with a car.
explanation: LESSON 5 – ‘The express road’.120 km/hour because the directions are separated by a berm.

text: You must drive minimum 70kph on an express road.
explanation: LESSON 5 – ‘The express road’.Only on motorways you should, under normal circumstances, drive at least 70 km/hour.

text: On this express road in Flanders with 2x2 lanes, a car is allowed to drive maximum (…) km/hour.
explanation: LESSON 5 – ‘The express road’.As of 1/1/2017 in Flanders: 70 km/hour unless traffic signs or rules impose a different speed limit.In Wallonia and Brussels-capital region: 90 km/hour.

text: What is the maximum permitted speed within a built-up area in the Walloon Region when passing the sign indicating a pedestrian crossing?
explanation: LESSON 6The sign indicating a pedestrian crossing does not set a speed limit.Within built-up areas:- Flanders and Wallonia: maximum 50 km/h.- Brussels Region: maximum 30 km/h.

text: You parked your car in this street at night. The next day it is a play street (or school street). Can you leave this street with your car?
explanation: LESSON 6 – ‘Special places’.At certain times you are not allowed to enter this street. But you can drive away with your car.

text: What is the maximum speed limit of a car in a bike zone?
explanation: LESSON 6 – ‘Special places’.In a bike zone cars are not allowed to overtake the cyclists and speed pedelecs.The maximum speed limit is 30 km/hour.

text: How fast can this car drive within this built-up area?
explanation: LESSON 6 - 'Special places'.In case of heavy rain, fog, snow, sleet (...) a driver must adjust the speed to the circumstances.

text: You are allowed to cross over a special reserved route to drive up to your property.
explanation: LESSON 6 – ‘Special places’.Other vehicles are allowed to cross over when:. they need to park or exit a parking space next to this reserved road.. they drive up or exit a property.. there is a junction.

text: You are allowed to drive maximum (…) km/hour with your car past these signs.
explanation: LESSON 6 – ‘Special places’.You leave the built up area. But the upper plate says that the maximum speed you can drive = 50 km/hour up to the next crossing

text: At what maximum speed may this car drive, inside a built-up area in the Walloon Region, past this sign?
explanation: LESSON 6This sign indicates, inside a built-up area, the end of a 30 km/h zone.The car therefore continues within the built-up area.The maximum permitted speed inside built-up areas is:- in the Flemish Region and the Walloon Region: 50 km/h- in the Brussels-Capital Region: 30 km/h

text: Your car is parked in this street, which suddenly becomes a school street for half an hour. Are you allowed to leave the street with your car?

options.text: No, you must wait for half an hour.
Yes, if you drive at walking speed.

explanation: LESSON 6To reduce traffic at the start and end of the school day, a street near a school can be temporarily closed to motor vehicles. It then becomes a school street.The closure is indicated by sign C3 (no entry) together with an additional sign stating SCHOOL STREET.In principle, a permit is required to drive in a school street. However, leaving a parking space is allowed, provided that you drive at walking speed and proceed with extra caution.

text: You drive in the Netherlands by car.

options.text: You follow the speed rules of that country.

explanation: Each country has its own rules.

text: What is correct? In a residential area ...

options.text: ... is the maximum speed limit 25 km/hour.
... are cars allowed to park on the left and right of the direction of travel.
... may pedestrians and cyclists use the full lane.

explanation: LESSON 6 – ‘Special places’.The maximum speed limit is 20 km/hour.Only pedestrians may use the full road.

text: You have a temporary driving licence B. Past these signs you drive 48 km/hour. What are the consequences?

options.text: You will have to pay a fine.
The judge will probably make you do the theoretical and practical examination again.

explanation: LESSON 6 – ‘Special places’.Exam Tip: read also very well in your book the difference between a fine and the prohibition of a right for the driving of vehicles (Lesson 12).

text: This sign indicates the start of a built up area.
explanation: LESSON 6 – ‘Special places’.The yellow sign with the red border only indicates the administrative boundary of a city and has no significance in the traffic regulations.

text: Which car is properly parked in this residential area?
explanation: LESSON 6 – ‘Special places’.In a residential area, you may park left and right of your direction of travel on the indicated parking places.

text: Please enter a number. What speed limit can you drive in Wallonia, on a normal road outside the built-up area?
explanation: LESSON 6 – ‘Special places’.

text: You are allowed to drive maximum (…) km/hour with your car past these signs.
explanation: LESSON 6 – ‘Special places’.He leaves a built-up area. But there is a sign that says that he may drive up to 70 km/hour.

text: Within a built-up area in the Brussels-Capital Region, you must ...

options.text: ... drive at least 30 kilometers per hour.
... drive at least 50 kilometers per hour.
... adapt your speed to the conditions.

explanation: LESSON 6 – ‘Special places’.The maximum permitted speed within a built-up area is 30 km/h. But you are not obliged to drive 30 km/h. Often you will not be able to achieve that speed.

text: When you leave this built up area, the maximum speed limit is 70 km/hour until the next junction.
explanation: LESSON 6 – ‘Special places’.Until you see the plate end of the ZONE.

text: Are you allowed to cross over a special reserved route with your car to access your home?
explanation: LESSON 6 – ‘Special places’.Vehicles are allowed to cross over when:. they need to park or exit a parking space next to this reserved road.. they drive up or exit a property.. there is a junction.

text: Beyond this sign ...

options.text: ... you may park left or right in parking spaces on the roadway.
... the maximum permitted speed is 30 km / hour.
... only pedestrians and cyclists are allowed.

explanation: LESSON 6 - 'Special places'.In a residential area (max 20 km / hour) cars can park both left and right on the parking spaces.

text: This zone sign applies …

options.text: ... only when it is lit up.

explanation: LESSON 6 – ‘Special places’.When you drive past an electronic sign, it is only mandatory when it lights up.

text: Past these signs you are only allowed to drive 70 km/hour until you leave the town.
explanation: LESSON 6 – ‘Special places’.70 km/hour up to the next crossing.

text: You have a temporary driving licence B. Past this sign in Flanders you drive 73 km/hour. What are the consequences?

options.text: You will only get a fine.
You risk an immediate temporary suspension of your driving licence.
The judge will disqualify you from driving.

explanation: LESSON 6 – ‘Special places’.Exam Tip: read also very well in your book the difference between a fine and the prohibition of a right for the driving of vehicles (Lesson 12).

text: Enter a number: What is the speed limit in the Brussels region, within a built-up area.
explanation: LESSON 6 – ‘Special places’.

text: What does this combination of signs indicate?

options.text: Zone where the priority of the right applies everywhere.

explanation: LESSON 6 – ‘Special places’.The term “School surroundings” (NL Schoolomgeving - FR Abords d'école) designates an area made up of one or more public roads, or parts of a public road, including access to a school and the beginning and end of which are delimited by signals F4a and F4b. Signal A23 is associated with signal F4a.

text: Past this sign you are allowed to drive maximum (…) km/hour with your car.
explanation: LESSON 6 – ‘Special places’.70 km/hour up to the next crossing.

text: Past this sign in Flanders you are allowed to drive maximum (…) km/hour with a car.
explanation: LESSON 6 – ‘Special places’.As of 1/1/2017 in Flanders and Brussels region: 70 km/hour unless traffic signs or rules impose a different speed limit.In Wallonia: 90 km/hour.

text: In a residential area or estate you are allowed to drive maximum (…) km/hour.
explanation: LESSON 6 – ‘Special places’.It is a residential area.Pedestrians are allowed to walk on the street.Children are allowed to play on the road.Maximum speed 20 km/hour.

text: What does this traffic sign mean?

options.text: End of a residential area or estate.

explanation: LESSON 6 – ‘Special places’.Meaning: end of a residential area.Information sign.

text: What is the maximum speed limit of a car in a play street?
explanation: LESSON 6 – ‘Special places’.The whole width of the public road is reserved for playing.You can only drive at footpace.

text: When you see these two signs together, you know the speed limit only applies during the schooldays.
explanation: LESSON 6 – ‘Special places’.As long as you are in a zone, it is mandatory –e.g. the speeding limit or the parking regulations – to do what is indicated when driving into the zone, day and night.

text: What is wrong? In a residential area or estate …

options.text: ... children are allowed to play on the road.
... you are allowed to drive maximum 25 km/hour with a car.
... you are only allowed to park on reserved places.

explanation: LESSON 6 – ‘Special places’.We did not ask 'what is right' but 'what is wrong'.In a residential area, the maximum speed limit is 20 km/hour.

text: In a 30 zone you have to give priority everywhere.
explanation: LESSON 6 – ‘Special places’.We didn’t write this in our book.

text: Once you’re past these signs you are allowed to drive maximum (…) km/hour.
explanation: LESSON 6 – ‘Special places’.Beyond the second board you drive in a ZONE 30.

text: You have a permit to drive your car in a play street. A child wants to cross the road at a place without a pedestrian crossing. Who has the right of way?
explanation: LESSON 6In a play street, children may use the entire roadway.Anyone allowed to drive there must proceed at walking speed.

text: Riders who are allowed to ride in this street, are allowed to ride maximum (…) km/hour.
explanation: LESSON 6 – ‘Special places’.The maximum speed limit is 30 km/hour.It is a street reserved for special groups of road users.Symbols in the sign show us which road users are admitted.

text: Please enter a number. You have a driving license B. What speed limit can you drive in the Brussels region, on a normal road outside the built-up area.
explanation: LESSON 6 – ‘Special places’.

text: You are allowed to drive with your car maximum (…) km/hour past these signs in Flanders.
explanation: LESSON 6 – ‘Special places’.You drive within a built-up area.

text: In Flanders. The car in the picture is allowed to drive maximum (…) km/hour there.
explanation: LESSON 6 – ‘Special places’.He leaves a built-up area. But there is a sign that says that he may drive up to 70 km/hour.

text: In Flanders. Before you pass this sign, you were allowed to drive maximum (…) km/hour with a car.
explanation: LESSON 6 – ‘Special places’.The white sign indicates the end of a built up area.

text: Past this sign within a built up area in Flanders you are allowed to drive maximum (…) km/hour in this street.
explanation: LESSON 6 – ‘Special places’.Past this sign, you are in a built up area.The maximum speed = 50 km/hour until the end of the built up area.(In Brussels region: 30kph.

text: Are you allowed to drive past this sign with a car?
explanation: LESSON 6 – ‘Special places’.Symbols in the sign show us which road users are admitted.The maximum speed limit is 30 km/hour.

text: You are allowed to drive maximum 30 km/hour in this street until the next junction.
explanation: LESSON 6 – ‘Special places’.Until you see the sign end of the ZONE.

text: How much is the maximum permitted speed in a 'school street'? (Dutch: 'Schoolstraat' -- French: 'Rue scolaire').
explanation: LESSON 6 - 'Special places'.Vehicles that are allowed to drive in a school street must do this step-by-step.(except if there are traffic signs that allow a different speed).

text: In a bike zone cars are not allowed to overtake cyclists and speed pedelecs.
explanation: LESSON 6 – ‘Special places’.In a bike zone cars are not allowed to overtake the cyclists and speed pedelecs.The maximum speed limit is 30 km/hour.

text: The pedestrian is about to cross over the road.
explanation: LESSON 7 – ‘The pedestrians’.Pedestrians on the zebra crossing or intending to use it, must get priority.A pedestrian who wants to cross the road where there is no zebra crossing, he himself has to give priority.

text: When you are driving behind this bus, you know ...

options.text: ... that children may also be in this bus.
... that it is a school bus.

explanation: LESSON 7School transport vehicles are recognizable by a yellow sign (at least 0.40 m), clearly visible at the front and rear of the vehicle. This sign must be removed or covered when the vehicle is not being used for school transport.Be extra cautious and reduce your speed.Stop if necessary when you see a school transport vehicle switching on its indicators, which means children are about to get on or off. This applies both to vehicles that are stationary and to those that stop on the roadway.

text: The maximum permitted speed in this built-up area is 30 km/h. Must you give way if pedestrians cross the road?

options.text: Yes, because the speed limit is 30 km/h.
No, they only have priority on a pedestrian crossing.

explanation: LESSON 7A pedestrian who wants to cross the road at a place where there is no pedestrian crossing must give way themselves.Nevertheless, drivers must always be cautious.

text: Your girlfriend lives in this pedestrian zone. Can you drive your car to her home?
explanation: LESSON 7It is forbidden to drive a car in a Belgian pedestrian zone (sign F103).Access is only allowed with a special permit, usually for residents or for loading and unloading during specific hours.If you enter without permission, you risk a fine.Drivers who are allowed to enter must:• drive at walking pace• always give way to pedestrians• stop if necessary• never endanger or hinder pedestrians.

text: A car may not park on the roadway within 5 metres before a pedestrian or cyclist crossing. But may a driver stop there to let someone get in?
explanation: LESSON 7It is forbidden to park or stop on a pedestrian crossing, even to let someone get in or out.It is also forbidden to park or to stop on the roadway within 5 metres before the crossing (parking on the verge is allowed if possible).The same rule applies to crossings for cyclists and two-wheeled mopeds.After the crossing, parking and stopping are allowed, unless prohibited by traffic signs.

text: The indication or information sign is placed at the pedestrian crossing. Which sign is the indication sign?
explanation: LESSON 7 – ‘The pedestrians’.The red sign is a warning or danger sign and is placed 150 meters in front of the crossover.

text: If there is a pedestrian crossing or a zebra crossing within (…) meters, pedestrians must use it.
explanation: LESSON 7 – ‘The pedestrians’.A pedestrian who wants to cross over the road where there is no zebra crossing, he himself has to give priority.The message is: always be careful.(Before 31/5/2019 it was 30 meters).

text: Are you allowed to drive your car into this street?

options.text: Only if your parents, brother or sister live there.

explanation: You need to have a special permission.

text: Traffic is moving very slowly and keeps stopping. If traffic comes to a halt again, are you allowed to stop on a pedestrian crossing?

options.text: No, you must stop before the pedestrian crossing.

explanation: You are not allowed to stop or park on a pedestrian crossing.This rule is strict.Even in a traffic jam, you may not stop, not even briefly, on a pedestrian crossing to follow traffic.Note: in a traffic jam, stopping on an elevated section is allowed.

text: Someone pushing a moped is …
explanation: LESSON 7 – ‘The pedestrians’.Who pushes a moped is a pedestrian.He should step on the footpath.Who pushes a motorcycle or car, is a driver.

text: A winged zebra crossing. Who is allowed to cross here?
A pedestrian is not using or going to use the pedestrian crossing. Is the brown car allowed to overtake the red one on the left?
explanation: LESSON 7 – ‘The pedestrians’.You may not overtake a driver on the left who slows down or stops in front of a zebra crossing.

text: Beyond these signs, a child wants to cross the street in a place where there is no pedestrian crossing. Do you need to stop and give priority to the child?
explanation: LESSON 7 – ‘The pedestrians’.A pedestrian who wants to cross the roadway in a place where there is no pedestrian crossing should itself give priority. However, the message is that you should always be careful.

text: Which mopeds are allowed to ride past this sign?
explanation: LESSON 7 – ‘The pedestrians’.Pedestrian and bicycle under each other: no mopeds are allowed.Pedestrian and bicycle next to each other: only class A mopeds are allowed.

text: The man walking next to the horse is …
explanation: LESSON 7 – ‘The pedestrians’.A horseback rider or a person accompanying a horse is not a pedestrian but a driver.

text: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Pedestrians can cross over the road.
No entry to all road users, except pedestrians.

explanation: LESSON 7 – ‘The pedestrians’.Meaning: no entry for pedestrians.Prohibitive sign.

text: An adult wants to cross the road with young children. How should you react?

options.text: You continue driving because there is no pedestrian crossing.
You stop and let the children cross calmly.
You pay extra attention and are ready to brake if a child suddenly steps onto the road.

explanation: DEFENSIVE DRIVINGChildren can behave unpredictably and may suddenly step onto the road.You adjust your speed, keep the situation under control, and are ready to brake immediately.

text: This warning sign indicates that there is a pedestrian crossing further ahead. May this pedestrian cross the roadway here?
explanation: LESSON 7If there is a pedestrian crossing within 20 metres, pedestrians must use it.The warning sign indicates that a pedestrian crossing is located about 150 metres ahead.➡️ The pedestrian may cross here.

text: A girl is pushing her moped on the road. According to the traffic regulations she is …
explanation: LESSON 7 – ‘The pedestrians’.Someone who pushes a moped is for the traffic regulations code a pedestrian.Someone who pushes a car or motorcycle is for the traffic regulations code a driver.

text: This warning sign is placed (…) meters in front of the pedestrian crossing.
explanation: LESSON 7 – ‘The pedestrians’.Warning or danger signs are placed 150 meters in front of the danger.

text: In a Zone 30, drivers must always give way to pedestrians, even if there is no zebra crossing.
A blind person is crossing the road at a place where there is no pedestrian crossing. You stop your car — but are you required to do so?

options.text: No, there is no pedestrian crossing, so you have priority.
You may stop; it is courteous behaviour.
You must give way to the blind person.

explanation: LESSON 7In Belgium, every driver (car, bicycle, etc.) is legally required to give way to a blind or visually impaired pedestrian,recognisable by a white cane, when that person is crossing or clearly intends to cross.This rule applies even if there is no pedestrian crossing.It also applies to other persons with reduced mobility, such as those using a walking frame or rollator.

text: A cyclist steps next to his bike. He wants to cross the road. Where does he have priority?
The pedestrian is not yet on the crossing. Does the driver have to stop?
explanation: LESSON 7 – ‘The pedestrians’.Pedestrians on the zebra crossing or intending to use it, must get priority.A pedestrian who wants to cross the road where there is no zebra crossing, he himself has to give priority.

text: You are not allowed to be stationary or to park within (…) meters in front of the pedestrian crossing.
explanation: LESSON 7 – ‘The pedestrians’.You are not allowed to be stationary or to park on a zebra crossing, or on the road within 5 meters of a zebra crossing.Past a zebra crossing you are allowed to park and to be stationary (except when traffic signs prohibit it).

text: A dog walking in the street is according to the traffic regulations …
explanation: LESSON 7 – ‘The pedestrians’.According to the traffic regulations a road user is anyone who uses the public road. So they are persons.An animal like a horse or a dog and things like a bicycle or a car are not road users.

text: A school bus stops outside a built-up area, not at a bus stop but on the roadway near a house. The driver switches on the four hazard lights. How do you react?

options.text: You just continue driving, because it is not a bus stop.
You slow down sharply and stop if necessary because children may get off.

explanation: LESSON 7School transport vehicles are recognizable by a yellow sign (at least 0.40 m), clearly visible at the front and rear of the vehicle. This sign must be removed or covered when the vehicle is not being used for school transport.Be extra cautious and reduce your speed.Stop if necessary when you see a school transport vehicle switching on its indicators or hazard lights, which means children are about to get on or off. This applies both to vehicles that are stationary and to those that stop on the roadway.

text: May the car stop at that place within a built-up area to let a passenger get in?
explanation: LESSON 7It is forbidden to park or stop on a pedestrian crossing, even to let someone get in or out.It is also forbidden to park or to stop on the roadway within 5 metres before the crossing (parking on the verge is allowed if possible).The same rule applies to crossings for cyclists and two-wheeled mopeds.After the crossing, parking and stopping are allowed, unless prohibited by traffic signs.

text: How do you react when you see a scared horse on the way?
explanation: LESSON 8 – ‘The drivers’.Every driver should immediately slow down when approaching pulling animals, welding, driving or livestock on public roads. He had to stop if these animals show signs of fear.

text: Pedestrians are road users as well?
explanation: LESSON 8 – ‘The drivers’.According the traffic regulations a road user is anyone who uses the public road.. The pedestrians.. The drivers of vehicles.

text: The farmer walking next to his cows is …
explanation: LESSON 8 – ‘The drivers’.A farmer walking next to his cows is a driver.A driver is someone accompanying or guarding draft animals, farm animals, horses on the public road.

text: Dad is walking in the street with his son who is sitting on a pony. Dad is …
explanation: LESSON 7A rider or a person who leads a horse is not a pedestrian, but a driver under the traffic rules.

text: What kind of sign is this traffic sign?
explanation: LESSON 8 – ‘The drivers’.Meaning: no entry for motorcycles.It’s a prohibitive sign.

text: This prohibitive sign applies to all road users.
explanation: LESSON 8 – ‘The drivers’.Meaning: no entry for pedestrians.Prohibitive sign.

text: In a mini bus/van there are maximum (…) seats allowed for passengers.
explanation: LESSON 8 – ‘The drivers’.Passengers: 8.Driver: 1

text: What does this sign mean?
explanation: LESSON 8 – ‘The drivers’.Passage of livestock.Warning or danger sign.

text: A car you can drive with a driving licence B, is a car with a M.A.W. of maximum (…) kg.
explanation: LESSON 8 – ‘The drivers’.Vehicles with a M.A.W. of maximum 3.5 ton.Car – a car for double use – minibus – light truck.

text: Are you allowed to drive a light truck with a temporary licence B?
explanation: LESSON 8 – ‘The drivers’.This is a light truck.All vehicles with a M.A.W. of maximum 3.5 ton.Car – a car for double use – minibus – light truck.

text: A shepherd walking on the road with his sheep is...
explanation: LESSON 8In the road code, he is considered a driver.

text: Someone who is pushing this trailer on the public road is …
explanation: LESSON 8 – ‘The drivers’.It’s a driver of a non-motorized vehicle.

text: Someone with a driving licence B is allowed to drive a mini bus.
explanation: LESSON 8 – ‘The drivers’.All vehicles with a M.A.W. of maximum 3.5 ton.Car – a car for double use – minibus – light truck.

text: The man standing next to the horses is according to the traffic regulations …
explanation: LESSON 8 – ‘The drivers’.A driver is someone accompanying or guarding draft animals, farm animals, horses on the public road.

text: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No entry to vehicles used to transport people and business goods.

explanation: LESSON 8 – ‘The drivers’.Meaning: no entry to goods vehicles.

text: A driver who gets out of the car and is now pushing the car …
explanation: LESSON 8 – ‘The drivers’.Who pushes a car or motorcycle, remains a driver.Who pushes a moped is according to the traffic regulations a pedestrian.

text: This man is pushing a broken down motorcycle. What is the most complete and correct answer?

options.text: He must wear a helmet and walk on the road.
He must wear a helmet, walk on the road and have a driving licence.

explanation: LESSON 8 – ‘The drivers’.It is a driver of a motorcycle.He needs: a driving licence A, a helmet and has to push the motorcycle on the road.

text: Are you allowed to drive past this sign with a car?
explanation: LESSON 8 – ‘The drivers’.Meaning: no entry for busses.Prohibitive sign.

text: What is car sharing?

options.text: With several people at the same time use the car to reach a destination together.
Occasionally using a car at times fixed in advance via reservation system.

explanation: LESSON 9 – ‘M.A.W. and M.G.W.’.If you share a car, you use one car with several people at a different time. You use the car when you need it. When you don't need it, someone else can drive it. In this way, a car is used better and thoughtfully and not everyone has to buy a car.

text: This traffic sign applies to …
explanation: LESSON 9 – ‘M.A.W. and M.G.W.’.Maximum Gross weight M.G.W.Read this lesson very well in your book.

text: You have a provisional licence B. Are you allowed to drive with a light truck over this bridge?
explanation: LESSON 9 – ‘M.A.W. and M.G.W.’.A light truck is a vehicle with a M.A.W. up to 3500 kg.

text: The real weight of the car + the load + the persons; if you put everything on a certain moment on a scale, it is called …
explanation: LESSON 9 – ‘M.A.W. and M.G.W.’.Maximum Gross weight M.G.W.Read this lesson very well in your book.

text: The M.A.W. is set by …
explanation: LESSON 9 – ‘M.A.W. and M.G.W.’.The manufacturer, because who knows how strong the vehicle is made.

text: Which of these signs relate to the Maximum Authorized Weight M.A.W. of a car?
explanation: LESSON 9 – ‘M.A.W. and M.G.W.’.Signs 1 relate to the M.G.W.Since October 1, 2022, board three relates to the M.A.W.

text: All documents that you show to the police must be original, except one document. Which one?
explanation: LESSON 9All documents that must be carried in the vehicle have to be original.The only exception is the insurance certificate: this document may also be shown digitally, for example as an image on your smartphone.

text: Which of these signs no longer exists since October 1st, 2022?
explanation: LESSON 9 – ‘M.A.W. and M.G.W.’.Signs 1, 2 and 3 (since 1/10/2022) relate to the M.A.W.Read this chapter very well in your book.

text: This combination of signs applies …
explanation: LESSON 9 – ‘M.A.W. and M.G.W.’.Starting from the road sign to the next intersection, it’s forbidden for drivers of vehicles with a M.A.W. of more than 3.5 ton to drive with greater speed than this that is referred to.

text: A road with 2x2 lanes segregated by a verge. Past these signs the blue car is allowed to drive maximum (…) kph.
explanation: LESSON 9 – ‘M.A.W. and M.G.W.’.Up to 90 km/hour for cars.Vehicles with a M.A.W. of more than 3.5 ton: up to 70 km/hour.Read this lesson very well in your book.

text: During a roadside check, the police ask for the vehicle registration certificate. In which form must this document be presented?

options.text: The original or a colour copy.
A copy is sufficient, provided the original is presented later.
