explanation: LESSON 9The following documents must be present in the vehicle:- Registration certificate (original)- Certificate of conformity (original)- Insurance certificate (original, copy or digital version on a smartphone)- Roadworthiness inspection certificate (original), once the vehicle is 4 years old

text: This combination of signs indicates, it is prohibited to drive to the right for drivers of vehicles …

options.text: ... with a M.G.W. of more than 3.5 ton.
... with a M.A.W. of more than 3.5 ton.

explanation: LESSON 9 – ‘M.A.W. and M.G.W.’.Maximum Gross weight M.G.W.Read this lesson very well in your book.

text: A driver has his provisional licence B. Is he already allowed to drive a light truck?
explanation: LESSON 9 – ‘M.A.W. and M.G.W.’.A light truck is a vehicle with a M.A.W. up to 3500 kg.

text: What is obligatory in the car?
explanation: LESSON 9 – ‘M.A.W. and M.G.W.’.Reflective safety jacket – warning triangle – fire extinguisher – first aid kit.

text: A car you can drive with a driving licence B is a car with a M.A.W. of maximum (…) kg.
explanation: LESSON 9 – ‘M.A.W. and M.G.W.’.Up to 3500 kg.

text: What is obligatory in the car?
explanation: LESSON 9 – ‘M.A.W. and M.G.W.’.Reflective safety jacket – warning triangle – fire extinguisher – first aid kit.

text: What is not obligatory in the car?
explanation: LESSON 9 – ‘M.A.W. and M.G.W.’.Reflective safety jacket – warning triangle – fire extinguisher – first aid kit.

text: You are in possession of a driving licence B. You drive in a car with a M.A.W. of 2500 kg. How much is the maximum M.A.W. your trailer can have?
explanation: LESSON 9 – ‘M.A.W. and M.G.W.’.As the M.A.W. of the trailer is more than 750 kg, a driving licence B shall be sufficient provided that the M. A.W. of the assembly (car + trailer) does not exceed 3500 kg.

text: The police ask for your driving licence during a check.

options.text: You must always carry the original driving licence with you.
You have 24 hours to present the original driving licence.

explanation: LESSON 9If you are driving, you must have your original driver's license with you.

text: What is not obligatory in the car?
explanation: LESSON 9 – ‘M.A.W. and M.G.W.’.Reflective safety jacket – warning triangle – fire extinguisher – first aid kit.

text: This combination of signs applies to …
explanation: LESSON 9 – ‘M.A.W. and M.G.W.’.Meaning: parking allowed for vehicles with a M.A.W. of more than 3.5 ton.

text: A diving license B allows to pull a trailer with a M.A.W. to (...) kg.
explanation: LESSON 10 – ‘The load and the passenger spaces’.BUT when the M.A.W. of the trailer exceeds 750 kg, a license B is ok, provided that the M.A.W. of car and trailer together does not exceed 3.5 ton.With a provisional driving license B you cannot pull a trailer.

text: The blind spot detection system ensures that an LED light lights up in the exterior mirror when a road user is in the blind spot.
How far may a load project beyond the front bodywork of the car?

options.text: Material that cannot be taken apart max. 3 meters.

explanation: LESSON 10 – ‘The load and the passenger spaces’.Absolutely nothing may project beyond the front bodywork of a car.

text: The width of a vehicle and its load is maximum …?
explanation: LESSON 10 – ‘The load and the passenger spaces’.A vehicle along with his load should not be wider than 2.55 meters. If wider = "exceptional transport".(Height: up to 4 m)

text: When there are 2 seat belts in the back of the car, only (…) persons maximum are allowed to take place in the back.
explanation: LESSON 10 – ‘The load and the passenger spaces’.A safety belt per person.

text: Beyond which sign may you drive with a car that is 7 meters long?
explanation: LESSON 10C27. No entry for drivers of vehicles whose width, including load, exceeds the indicated limit.C29. No entry for drivers of vehicles whose height, including load, exceeds the indicated limit.

text: For material that cannot be taken apart, any load must carry a warning marker that projects more than (…) behind the car.
explanation: LESSON 10 – ‘The load and the passenger spaces’.From 1 meter to 3 meters.

text: How should you wear the seat belt?
explanation: LESSON 10 – ‘The load and the passenger spaces’.Pregnant women must also wear a seat belt.

text: This boy is 12 years old and 1.45 metres tall. He is sitting in the back seat of the car and is wearing a seat belt. Is that correct?

options.text: Yes, because he is 1.45 metres tall.
No, he must sit in a child seat because he is only 12 years old.

explanation: LESSON 10Children under 18 years old and smaller than 1.35 m must be transported in an approved child restraint system that meets the required standards.A child taller than 1.35 m may still be transported in a special child seat.Children under 18 may not be transported in the front seat in a rear-facing child seat, unless there is no front airbag or it can be deactivated.

text: This prohibition sign applies to:
explanation: LESSON 10Access prohibited to drivers of vehicles or vehicle combinations whose total length, including load, exceeds the length indicated.

text: What determines whether someone should sit in a child seat?
explanation: LESSON 10 - "The Charge."Children up to the age of 18 and under 1m35 MUST be transported in an adapted safety seat or child restraint system that complies with the prescribed rules and standards.(A child taller than 1m35 MAY still be transported in a special child seat).

text: Children taller than (…) cm do not have to be seated in an appropriate safety seat for children.
explanation: LESSON 10 – ‘The load and the passenger spaces’.Every child under the age of 18 and smaller than 1m35 must travel in an appropriate safety system.

text: When do you have to increase the tire pressure a bit?

options.text: You have to drive in the mountains.
There is a lot of snow and ice.
You have a long journey ahead of you.

explanation: LESSON 10 – ‘The load and the passenger spaces’.Only in case of a long drive, or if you're a heavy load to carry.(Not when there is snow or freezing rain on the roadway).

text: This DHL driver is delivering parcels. Does he have to wear a seat belt while driving?
explanation: LESSON 10In principle, a driver must always wear a seat belt.However, the law provides a few strict exceptions.The following persons are exempt from wearing a seat belt:- a driver who is reversing;- taxi drivers while transporting passengers;- postal workers delivering parcels from house to house(this does not apply to delivery drivers such as DHL, Amazon or other courier services);- authorised persons and emergency services, when required for their duties.➡️ A DHL driver is not exempt and must therefore wear a seat belt.

text: This truck is carrying tons of washing powder. May it drive past this sign?
explanation: LESSON 10Meaning of sign C24a:No entry for drivers of vehicles carrying dangerous goods.Washing powder is not a dangerous substance.

text: When are the back lights allowed to be hidden away by the load?

options.text: During the day between 09 am and 06pm.

explanation: LESSON 10 – ‘The load and the passenger spaces’.The rear lights must be visible.

text: When the M.A.W. of the trailer exceeds 750 kg, a driving license B is ok, provided that the M.A.W. of the car and the trailer together does not exceed (…) ton.
explanation: LESSON 10 – ‘The load and the passenger spaces’.With a provisional driving license B you cannot pull a trailer.

text: This sign indicates that drivers of certain (…) are not allowed to drive their vehicle past this sign.
explanation: LESSON 10 – ‘The load and the passenger spaces’.Contaminated goods.

text: Which original document must be in the car? 1. Only the registration. 2. Only the insurance. 3. Only the certificate of conformity. 4. All documents must be original.
explanation: LESSON 10 – ‘The load and the passenger spaces’.All documents must be original.

text: When this warning marker is placed at the back, material that cannot be taken apart, may project the back of the bodywork of the car by (…) meters.
explanation: LESSON 10 – ‘The load and the passenger spaces’.Up to 3 meters.

text: Children until the age of (…), smaller than 1.35m, must be seated in an appropriate safety seat for children.
explanation: LESSON 10 – ‘The load and the passenger spaces’.Every child under the age of 18 and smaller than 1m35 must travel in an appropriate safety system.

text: This sign indicates that drivers of certain (…) are not allowed to drive their vehicle past this sign.
explanation: Meaning of sign C24a:No entry for drivers of vehicles carrying dangerous goods.

text: The fuel of your car is LPG or petrol. Are you allowed to drive past this sign with your car?

options.text: Yes, only when you switch from LPG to petrol.

explanation: LESSON 10 – ‘The load and the passenger spaces’.The sign is about the goods you transport and not about the fuel in the car.

text: A passenger sitting in the back seat of a car...

options.text: ... is recommended to wear a seat belt.

explanation: LESSON 10 – ‘The load and the passenger spaces’.

text: Do backseat passengers also have to wear a seat belt?
How far may an indivisible load extend beyond the rear of the vehicle if it is properly marked?
explanation: LESSON 10A load may extend up to 1 metre beyond the rear of the vehicle.If the load is indivisible and cannot be shortened or folded, it may extend up to 3 metres beyond the rear, provided that it is properly marked with the required warning panel.This load is not properly marked.

text: In a van, there is a front seat where the driver and two passengers can sit. What is the minimum required width of that seat?
explanation: LESSON 10The width must be enough for:Driver: 55 cm.Each passenger: 40 cm.Total: 55 + 40 + 40 = 135 cm.

text: A child is 10 years old and 1m45 tall.

options.text: It must be seated in an appropriate safety seat for children.
It is allowed to be seated in an appropriate safety seat.
It is not allowed to be seated in an appropriate safety seat for children.

explanation: LESSON 10 – ‘The load and the passenger spaces’.Every child under the age of 18 and smaller than 1m35 must travel in an appropriate safety system.

text: You have a provisional driving license B. Can you pull a trailer with your car?
explanation: LESSON 10 – ‘The load and the passenger spaces’.With a provisional driving license B you cannot pull a trailer.

text: Children younger than 18 and smaller than (…) m must be seated in an appropriate safety seat for children.
explanation: LESSON 10 – ‘The load and the passenger spaces’.Every child under the age of 18 and smaller than 1m35 must travel in an appropriate safety system.

text: Who must not wear a seat belt?

options.text: Someone who is driving in a 30 zone.
Someone who is delivering packages from home to home.

explanation: LESSON 10 – ‘The load and the passenger spaces’.In a Zone 30 you should also wear a belt.Only a postman collecting and delivering post from door to door should not.

text: A car, load included, is allowed to be maximum (…) meters high.
explanation: LESSON 10 – ‘The load and the passenger spaces’.Maximum height: 4 meters.Maximum width: 2.55 meters.

text: A load, without a special warning marker, may project at the rear of the bodywork of a car, maximum (…) meters.
explanation: LESSON 10 – ‘The load and the passenger spaces’.Up to 1 meter.

text: A child taller than 1m35 …

options.text: ... is allowed to sit in an appropriate safety seat for children.
... must sit in an appropriate safety seat for children.
... is not allowed to sit in an appropriate safety seat for children anymore.

explanation: LESSON 10 – ‘The load and the passenger spaces’.Every child under the age of 18 and smaller than 1m35 must travel in an appropriate safety system.

text: This prohibitive sign applies …
explanation: LESSON 10 – ‘The load and the passenger spaces’.No entry to vehicles or combination of vehicles which, load included, exceed the length shown.

text: What happens if a driver does not wear the seat belt correctly? For example, under the arm instead of over the shoulder.

options.text: The seat belt only provides less protection.
This is considered the same as not wearing a seat belt.

explanation: LESSON 10Wearing a seat belt incorrectly, for example under the arm or not over the shoulder, is legally considered the same as not wearing a seat belt.

text: This driver holds a full category B driving licence. The M.A.M. of the van is 2,700 kg. The trailer may have a M.A.M. of …
explanation: LESSON 10A vehicle with a M.A.M. of 3,500 kg may tow a trailer with a M.A.M. of up to 750 kg.If the M.A.M. of the towing vehicle is less than 3,500 kg, the trailer’s M.A.M. may be higher, provided that the combined M.A.M. does not exceed 3,500 kg.➡️ 2,700 kg + 800 kg = 3,500 kg → permitted.

text: The width of the seat of the driver must be (…) cm.
explanation: LESSON 10 – ‘The load and the passenger spaces’.Driver: 55 cm.Passengers: 40 cm.

text: This sign indicates that vehicles wider than 3.5m are not allowed to drive on.
explanation: LESSON 10 – ‘The load and the passenger spaces’.Meaning: no entry to vehicles which, load included, exceed the height shown.

text: When does a driver not have to wear a seat belt?

options.text: A driver must always wear a seat belt.
When there are no passengers in the car.

explanation: LESSON 10In general, a driver must wear a seat belt at all times.However, the law provides a number of exceptions.The following persons are exempt from wearing a seat belt:- a driver who is reversing;- taxi drivers while transporting passengers;- postal workers delivering parcels from house to house (this does not apply to everyone who delivers parcels;)- authorised persons and emergency services, when required for their duties.

text: This girl is 1.45 metres tall.

options.text: She must sit in an adapted child seat.
She may sit in an adapted child seat.
She may no longer sit in an adapted child seat.

explanation: LESSON 10Children under 18 years old and smaller than 1.35 m must be transported in an approved child restraint system that meets the required standards.A child taller than 1.35 m may still be transported in a special child seat.Children under 18 may not be transported in the front seat in a rear-facing child seat, unless there is no front airbag or it can be deactivated.

text: This sign indicates: no entry to drivers of vehicles which, load included, exceed the width shown. What kind of sign is this?
explanation: LESSON 10 – ‘The load and the passenger spaces’.It’s a prohibitive sign.

text: The cyclist and the truck both want to turn right at this intersection. How does the cyclist react?

options.text: He hurries so that he can turn first.
He turns at the same time as the truck.
He slows down and lets the truck turn first.

explanation: LESSON 10No matter how well the mirrors are adjusted, there are always areas beside or behind the vehicle that the driver of a truck or car cannot see.These areas are called blind spots.Many accidents happen at intersections because a cyclist is in the truck’s blind spot.A smart cyclist slows down and lets the truck turn first.

text: Is a truck of 8m long allowed to drive past these signs?
explanation: LESSON 10 – ‘The load and the passenger spaces’.These signs say nothing about the length of a vehicle.

text: Which sign indicates that drivers of vehicles transporting inflammable goods are not allowed to drive past this sign?
explanation: LESSON 10 – ‘The load and the passenger spaces’.Sign 1: dangerous goods.Sign 3: dangerous contaminated goods.

text: You park your car on an unlit road in the evening. What lights must be lit? 1. The parking lights. 2. The two red rear lights. 3. The dipped beam headlights (low beam).
explanation: LESSON 11 – ‘The lights’.At the front: one or two white or yellow sidelights.At the back: one or two red lights.

text: During heavy rainfall the dipped beam headlights or low beam must be used during the day when the visibility is less than (…) meters.
explanation: LESSON 11 – ‘The lights’.200 meters.

text: When is a driver, when it is fairly dark outside built-up areas, allowed to keep the high beams on?

options.text: When an oncoming vehicle is approaching.
When another car is driving in front of him.
When overtaking the car in front of him.

explanation: LESSON 11Article 30/1High beams must be switched off and replaced by low beams:a) when approaching an oncoming road user,b) when approaching a rail vehicle or a boat whose driver could be dazzled,c) when following another vehicle at less than 50 meters, except when overtaking,d) when the road is continuously and sufficiently lit so the driver can clearly see up to about 100 meters.

text: Is it allowed to turn on the four warning lights to alert the driver behind you that there is a traffic jam?
explanation: LESSON 11- 'The lights’.You may only use the four warning lights for signaling:. a school bus with children during embarkation or disembarkation;. a vehicle that is defective or immobilized after an accident;. a dangerous situation as it suddenly slowing the vehicles before you.

text: From when must the front fog light be switched on in heavy fog?

options.text: When visibility is less than 200 metres.
When visibility is less than 100 metres.

explanation: LESSON 11A car is not required to have front fog lights.Therefore, there is no traffic rule that obliges drivers to use them.

text: It is no longer snowing. Can the rear fog light stay on for a while?
explanation: It should burn while the snow falls

text: It is night, outside a built-up area. While the blue car is overtaking, the distracted driver of the white car suddenly swerves to the left. What may the driver of the blue car do?

options.text: He may only use the main beams because it is night.
He may use the horn to avoid an accident.

explanation: LESSON 11When may you use the horn?During the day:Inside and outside built-up areas: to warn others and prevent an accident.Outside built-up areas: to warn a driver you intend to overtake.Between dusk and dawn:Only in case of imminent danger.In all other cases, you must flash your headlights alternately instead of using the horn.

text: The dipped beam headlights must be switched on from sunset until dawn or during the day when you can’t see (…) m ahead due to rain, fog, snow or other circumstances.
explanation: LESSON 11 – ‘The lights’.200 meters.

text: Nighttime, outside a built-up area. Before starting to overtake, the driver of the white car briefly used the horn. Was he allowed to do that?

options.text: Yes, because it is outside the built-up area.

explanation: LESSON 11When may you use the horn?- During the day:Inside and outside built-up areas: to warn others and prevent an accident.Outside built-up areas: to warn a driver you intend to overtake.- Between dusk and dawn:Only in case of imminent danger.In all other cases, you must flash your headlights alternately instead of using the horn.

text: When you park somewhere it isn’t allowed, you should use the four hazard warning lights.
explanation: LESSON 11 – ‘The lights’.If you do so, then you make a double violation.

text: Your car is parked. When is the rear fog lamp allowed to be used?

options.text: In fog, snow and heavy rain.

explanation: LESSON 11 – ‘The lights’.When you park your car, the rear fog lamp may burn in case of fog, snowfall or heavy rain. It is not an obligation.

text: There is a thick fog and you park the car on the road. What’s wrong?

options.text: The rear fog light may be on.
The parking lights and the rear fog light must be lit.
The front fog lights may be on.

explanation: LESSON 11 – ‘The lights’.The dipped headlights or front fog-lamps don’t have to burn. But it is allowed.

text: You park your car on the road or on the verge during nightfall. Are you allowed to leave the dipped beam headlights on?
explanation: LESSON 11 – ‘The lights’.They may continue to burn. But the position lights are sufficient.

text: There is heavy rain and visibility is reduced to 130 metres. Must the rear fog lights be switched on?

options.text: No, because visibility is more than 100 metres.
Rear fog lights are never compulsory.

explanation: LESSON 11The rear fog light must be switched on:in fog, when visibility is less than about 100 metres;in snowfall, when visibility is less than about 100 metres;in heavy rain, it must always be on in Belgium, regardless of visibility.

text: Is it allowed to give a warning signal with the horn of your car when you want to overtake another driver?

options.text: Yes, during the day outside built-up areas.
Yes, during the day in built-up areas.

explanation: LESSON 11- 'The lights’Horn during the day:. Inside and outside built-up areas: to warn others and thus to avoid an accident.. Outside built-up areas: to warn a driver that you want to catch up.

text: There is a lot of smoke in a tunnel and you stop. What do you do wrong?

options.text: You leave the tunnel through an emergency exit.
You leave the key in the ignition.

explanation: LESSON 11 – ‘The lights’.During heavy smoke or fire, you leave the tunnel through an emergency exit. You don’t lock the doors of the car and you leave the key in the ignition.

text: You must switch off the headlights (main beam) when the driver in front of you is less than (…) m away.
explanation: LESSON 11 – ‘The lights’. 50 meters.

text: When it’s snowing, the rear fog lights must be used when the visibility is less than (…) meters.
explanation: LESSON 11 – ‘The lights’.100 meters.

text: There is fog and visibility is only 90 meters. The white car is parked. Which lights must be switched on?

options.text: The parking lights at the front, and at the rear: one or two red lights.
The parking lights and the dipped-beam headlights.
The parking lights, dipped-beam headlights and the rear fog light.

explanation: LESSON 11When you are stationary or parked on the road or on the verge: between sunset and sunrise; and whenever it is no longer possible to see clearly for about 200 meters, the following lights must be on:at the front: one or two white or yellow parking lightsat the rear: one or two red lights.In foggy weather, snowfall, or heavy rain, the dipped headlights or front fog lights and also the rear fog lights may be used, but it is not required.

text: You're driving and there is heavy fog. What lights are required to burn?

options.text: The front and rear fog lamps.

explanation: LESSON 11- 'The lights’.The front fog lamps are not required on a car.You are therefore never required to make them burn.

text: The dipped beam headlights must be used during the day when it’s snowing and the visibility is less than (…) m.
explanation: LESSON 11 – ‘The lights’.200 meters.

text: Which lights are always used together with the dipped beam headlights (low beam)? 1. Two red rear lights 2. Two parking lights 3. Two front fog lights
explanation: LESSON 11 – ‘The lights’.Together with the dipped beam headlights, two red rear lights and two position lights are on.

text: It is dusk inside a built-up area. Before the driver of the white car started overtaking, he briefly flashed the high beams. Was he allowed to do that?

options.text: No, because he is driving inside a built-up area.

explanation: LESSON 11When may you use the horn?During the day:Inside and outside built-up areas: to warn others and prevent an accident.Outside built-up areas: to warn a driver you intend to overtake.Between dusk and dawn:Only in case of imminent danger.In all other cases, instead of using the horn, you should flash the headlights (switch between high and low beams).

text: When must the rear fog lights be used during heavy rainfall?

options.text: The visibility is less than 200 meters.
The visibility is less than 100 meters.

explanation: LESSON 11 – ‘The lights’.Due to fog or snowfall, whenever the visibility is reduced to less than 100 meters.Due to heavy rainfall, always in Belgium.

text: It’s snowing. When must you switch on your dipped-beam headlights?

options.text: As soon as visibility is less than 100 metres.
As soon as visibility is less than 200 metres.

explanation: LESSON 11During the day, you must switch on your dipped-beam headlights:- in rain, when you cannot see farther than 200 metres;- in fog, when you cannot see farther than 200 metres;- in snowfall, when you cannot see farther than 200 metres;- or in other situations (e.g. smoke from a fire) when visibility is less than 200 metres.

text: A school bus has stopped and the hazard warning lights are being used. What do you have to do?

options.text: Slow down and stop if necessary.

explanation: LESSON 11 – ‘The lights’.If a school bus stops so that students can go out, the driver has to switch on the four direction indicators or hazard warning lights.Upcoming vehicles are obliged to reduce speed and if it is necessary to stopThey should be careful while driving by the bus.

text: It is night. A driver is overtaking another car. May the high beams be on during the overtaking?
explanation: LESSON 11High beams must not be used:- when the road is continuously and sufficiently lit so that you can see 100 metres ahead;- when they would dazzle an oncoming road user;- when a vehicle is driving less than 50 metres ahead of you and you are not overtaking it immediately. If you are overtaking, you may use them.- when approaching a rail vehicle or a boat.

text: Which lights must be switched on when you drive in a tunnel and you can’t see 200 meters ahead?
explanation: LESSON 11 – ‘The lights’.If you cannot see 200 meters far, then switch the dipped beam headlights lamps on before you drive in the tunnel, so that the driver behind you doesn't think that you brake at the entrance of the tunnel.

text: There is an accident without casualties. Are you allowed to leave the four hazard warning lights on?
explanation: LESSON 11 – ‘The lights’.The four hazard lights of a car can only be switched on when:. your car has broken down.. in order to warn other road users of a real danger.. a school bus when pupils are getting in or out.

text: May you use the horn at night in case of imminent danger?

options.text: No, at night you should rather flash your high beams.

explanation: LESSON 11Only in case of imminent danger, such as when a car suddenly changes lanes, you may use the horn at night.

text: On roads with little lighting the headlights (main beam) can be used instead of the dipped beam headlights if you don’t hinder anyone.
explanation: LESSON 11 – ‘The lights’.They may burn together with the dipped beam headlights or without.

text: How do you react when you drive into a fogbank?
explanation: LESSON 11 – ‘The lights’.You should definitely not suddenly brake.

text: On this road within the built up area the headlights can be used instead of the dipped beam headlights.
explanation: LESSON 11 – ‘The lights’.It should not, because the roadway is adequately illuminated, so you easily can see 100 meters far.

text: There is heavy fog. Should the front fog lights burn?
explanation: LESSON 11- 'The lights’The front fog lamps are not required on a car.You are therefore never required to make them burn.

text: The police will stop you, because you drive 75 km/h in a built-up area. What are the consequences?

options.text: You must pay a fine to the police.
Your driving licence can be withdrawn immediately and temporarily.
You must appear before the police judge within 14 days.

explanation: LESSON 12 – ‘Speed’.Learn very well in lesson 12 the difference between:Immediate temporary withdrawal of your driving licence.Annulment of the right to drive a motor vehicle.

text: What is the maximum speed limit on this road within a built-up area in Brussels Region after driving over the raised surface?
explanation: LESSON 12 – ‘Speed’.On the speed hump: 30 km/hour.Within a built-up area: 50 km/hour in Flanders and Wallonia. In Brussels Region: 30 kph.

text: What is the maximum speed limit (… km/hour) for this car on this motorway?
explanation: LESSON 12 – ‘Speed’.Motorway: up to 120 km/hour.Motorway: at least 70 km/hour.

text: What was the maximum permitted speed of the green car before passing these signs in Flanders? (...) km/hour.
explanation: LESSON 12 – ‘Speed’.You were within a built-up area.

text: What is the maximum speed allowed for this car?
explanation: LESSON 12 – ‘Speed’. The road sign 70 is to his right

text: What is the maximum speed limit (… km/hour) for these cars on this express road within a built up area in Wallonia?
explanation: LESSON 12 – ‘Speed’.Within a built-up area: up to 50 km/hour.

text: You’re driving too fast in a Zone 30. From how many km/hour over the maximum permitted speed the POLICE can disqualify you from driving immediately.

options.text: From more than 20 km/hour over the maximum permitted speed.
From more than 30 km/hour over the maximum permitted speed.
From more than 40 km/hour over the maximum permitted speed.

explanation: LESSON 12 – ‘Speed’. Read very carefully in your book (lesson 12) the difference between:- Immediate temporary suspension of your driving licence.- A declaration of lapse of right for driving a motorized vehicle.

text: The blue car is allowed to drive maximum (…) km/hour on this express road.
explanation: LESSON 12 – ‘Speed’.120 km/hour because the directions are segregated by a central reservation.

text: On this speed hump you are allowed to drive maximum (…) km/hour.
explanation: LESSON 12 – ‘Speed’. Speed hump: up to 30 km/hour.It's allowed to overtake a cyclist (1/4/2023).

text: The police stopped you because you were driving at 67 km/h in a built-up area in the Brussels region. What are the consequences?

options.text: You only have to pay a fine.
Your driving licence will be temporarily withdrawn.
You will have to appear in court.

explanation: LESSON 12The maximum speed limit in a built-up area in the Brussels region is 30 km/h.You were therefore driving 36 km/h too fast.A driving disqualification is imposed when you exceed the limit by more than 40 km/h on motorways, expressways or ordinary roads.However, in a built-up area, a 30 km/h zone or a residential area, you already risk disqualification if you exceed the limit by more than 30 km/h.This is not done by the police but by a judge in court.Depending on the verdict, you may lose your right to drive for at least 8 days and up to 5 years, even for vehicles that do not require a driving licence.For novice drivers (with a full driving licence for less than 2 years), the rule is even stricter.

text: When a family member is in an ambulance that is driving faster than the maximum speed limit, you are still allowed to follow the ambulance.
explanation: LESSON 12 – ‘Speed’.You may not drive faster than the maximum speed allowed.

text: What is the maximum speed limit (… km/hour) for these cars at that location in Flanders?
explanation: LESSON 12 – ‘Speed’. Ordinary roads:In Flanders up to 70 km/hour.In Wallonia and in the Brussels region: 90 km/h.

text: In normal circumstances you are allowed to drive minimum 70 km/hour with a car past this sign.
explanation: LESSON 12 – ‘Speed’.Express roads: no minimum speed.Motorway: minimum 70 km/hour.

text: You want to leave the motorway.

options.text: You slow down/brake on the exit.
You already slow down/brake on the lane.

explanation: LESSON 12 – ‘Speed’.You have to slow down on the exit.

text: Is the dark green car allowed to drive past the sign 70 km/hour?

options.text: Yes, but only in the Flemish region.

explanation: LESSON 12 – ‘Speed’.The maximum speed permitted on ordinary roads outside built-up areas =in Flanders: 70 km/hour.in Wallonia and Brussels region: 90 km/hour.Nowhere is it forbidden to drive 70 km/hour.

text: Is it allowed to overtake with a car a cyclist in a bike zone?

options.text: Yes, if you can get 1 meter safe spacing.

explanation: LESSON 12 – ‘Speed’.In a bike zone is the maximum permitted speed: 30 km/hour.

text: Can you overtake a cyclist on the left with a car on an elevated section?
explanation: For years, it has been allowed to overtake a cyclist on the right who is about to turn left. Since 2023, overtaking a cyclist on the left is also allowed.

text: What does this combination of signs mean?

options.text: From here on until 200m ahead, maximum 50 km/hour.

explanation: LESSON 12 – ‘Speed’.Starting from 200 meters further up to the next crossing.

text: What is the maximum speed for a car in this street?
explanation: LESSON 12 – ‘Speed’.Traffic sign: up to 50 km/hour.

text: From how many km/hour over the maximum permitted speed on this road outside a built up area the police can disqualify you from driving?

options.text: From more than 20 km/hour over the maximum permitted speed.
From more than 30 km/hour over the maximum permitted speed.
From more than 40 km/hour over the maximum permitted speed.

explanation: LESSON 12 – ‘Speed’Reed very carefully in your book (lesson 12) the difference between:- Immediate temporary suspension of your driving licence.- A declaration of lapse of right for driving a motorized vehicle.

text: The blue car on this express road in Flanders is allowed to drive maximum (…) km/hour.
explanation: LESSON 12 – ‘Speed’.Ordinary roads:In Flanders and in the Brussels region up to 70 km/hour.In Wallonia: 90 km/h.

text: Enter a number: What is the speed limit in the Brussels region, within a built-up area.
explanation: LESSON 12 – ‘Speed’.

text: Past this sign you are allowed to drive in Flanders maximum (…) km/hour with a car.
explanation: LESSON 12 – ‘Speed’.Within a built-up area: up to 50 km/hour.

text: Can you overtake a cyclist on the right with a car on an elevated section?
explanation: For years, it has been allowed to overtake a cyclist on the right who is about to turn left. Since 2023, overtaking a cyclist on the left is also allowed.

text: An ordinary road divided into two lanes in Wallonia. You are driving this car at 110 km/h. The police stop you. What are the consequences?

options.text: Your driving licence is immediately and temporarily withdrawn.
You will have to explain yourself in court.

explanation: LESSON 12You risk an immediate withdrawal of your driving licence if you exceed the speed limit by more than 30 km/h on motorways, expressways or ordinary roads.If you drive in a built-up area, a 30 km/h zone or a residential area more than 20 km/h too fast, you also risk an immediate withdrawal.This immediate withdrawal is done by the police, because it is a serious offence.For any serious offence, your driving licence can be immediately withdrawn.

text: You drive past this sign on a motorway. On the left lane you are allowed to drive maximum (…) km/hour.
explanation: Answer: 120LESSON 12 – ‘Speed’.The speed restriction starts 1500 meters away.

text: This board means: end of all local prohibitions imposed on vehicles in motion.
explanation: This is sign C 46. It is a prohibition sign.Example: imagine you see a traffic sign saying that the maximum speed allowed is 30 km/h. Then that sign will apply until the next intersection or until you see this sign, or a road sign that imposes another maximum speed limit.

text: In a bike zone you may overtake a cyclist on the left. A/ Correct. B/ Wrong.
explanation: LESSON 12 - 'Speed'.

text: Past this sign in Flanders a car is allowed to drive maximum (...) km/hour.
explanation: LESSON 12 – ‘Speed’.Ordinary roads:In Flanders and Brussels region up to 70 km/hour.In Wallonia: 90 km/h.

text: What is the maximum speed limit in a bike zone?
explanation: LESSON 12 – ‘Speed’.Up to 30 km/hour.Cars may overtake cyclists (1/4/2023).

text: What is the maximum speed limit (… km/hour) for this car?
explanation: LESSON 12 – ‘Speed’.Up to 70 km/hour up to the next crossing.

text: Past this sign you drive in a Zone 30.
explanation: LESSON 12 – ‘Speed’.It is a road where you can drive up to 30 km/hour up to the next crossing.

text: You are allowed to drive maximum (…) km/hour with a car on this road in Flanders.
explanation: LESSON 12 – ‘Speed’.Ordinary roads:In Flanders and in the Brussels region up to 70 km/hour.In Wallonia: 90 km/h.

text: This speed limit only applies …
explanation: LESSON 12 – ‘Speed’.The speed limit only applies on the exit.

text: On the motorway you must drive minimum (…) km/hour, in normal circumstances.
explanation: LESSON 12 – ‘Speed’.Motorway: at least 70 km/huur.

text: On a speed hump, you may overtake a cyclist on the left. On an elevated device in a built-up area, a cyclist makes his intention to turn to the left with the arm moving towards the left. May you overtake that cyclist on the right?

options.text: Yes, provided you leave a lateral gap of 1 meter.

explanation: LESSON 12 - 'Speed'.The maximum speed allowed on an elevated device is 30 km/hour.

text: This speed limit applies …

options.text: ... until you see an ‘End zone’ sign.

explanation: LESSON 12 – ‘Speed’.At the next junction.

text: Within a residential area you are allowed to drive maximum (…) km/hour.
explanation: LESSON 12 – ‘Speed’.Pedestrians may walk on the roadway and children can play there.

text: How much is the maximum permitted speed on an ordinary road outside the built-up area in Wallonia?
explanation: LESSON 12 - 'Speed'.Wallonia: 90 km / h.Flanders + Brussels-Capital Region: 70 km / hour.

text: Past this sign a Zone 30 starts.
explanation: LESSON 12 – ‘Speed’.Zone plate: beginning of a Zone 30.

text: What is the maximum speed limit (… km/hour) for this car at that location in Flanders?
explanation: LESSON 12 – ‘Speed’.Within a built-up area: up to 50 km/hour.

text: The cars in this picture are allowed to drive maximum (…) km/hour.
explanation: LESSON 12 – ‘Speed’.A built up area.But the traffic sign says that the maximum speed is 70 km/hour up to the next junction.

text: N -roads are …
explanation: LESSON 12 – ‘Speed’N-roads are regular roads.

text: You are allowed to drive maximum 60 km/hour with snow tires on normal roads. When?

options.text: Only when the roads are covered with snow or ice.
From the 1st November till the 31st March.

explanation: LESSON 12 – ‘Speed’.On ordinary roads: up to 60 km/hour.On motorways: up to 90 km/hour.

text: You are driving at 47 km/h in a residential area in Wallonia. What are the consequences?

options.text: You receive an immediate temporary withdrawal of your driving licence.
You will have to appear before the court.

explanation: LESSON 12You risk an immediate withdrawal of your driving licence as soon as you drive more than 30 km/h too fast on motorways, expressways or ordinary roads.However, in a built-up area, a 30 km/h zone, or a residential area (woonerf), you already risk an immediate withdrawal if you drive more than 20 km/h too fast.You risk a disqualification from driving as soon as you exceed the speed limit by more than 40 km/h on motorways, expressways or ordinary roads.In a built-up area, a 30 km/h zone or a residential area, you already receive a disqualification once you exceed the speed limit by more than 30 km/h.This is not decided by the police but by the judge when your case is handled in court.

text: What is the maximum speed limit (…) km/hour for this car at that location?
explanation: The maximum permitted speed on a speed hump is 30 km/hour.You may overtake a cyclist on this speed hump (1/4/2023).

text: This combination of signs indicates that at 150 meters,

options.text: ... there is a speed hump of 500 meters.
... there are several speed humps over a distance of 500 meters.

explanation: LESSON 12 – ‘Speed’.See the arrows on the charger plate.

text: This black car is allowed to drive maximum (…) km/hour at that location.
explanation: LESSON 12 – ‘Speed’.50 km/hour.

text: This zone sign applies
explanation: LESSON 12 – ‘Speed’.A fixed zone plate applies day and night.An electronic only if it lights up.

text: What is the maximum speed limit (… km/hour) for a car at this junction?
explanation: LESSON 12 – ‘Speed’.It is a speed hump.

text: Is it allowed to overtake a cyclist on this elevated device?
explanation: LESSON 12 – ‘Speed’.1/4/2023: It is allowed.On the speed hump: 30 km/hour.

text: Past this sign in Flanders you are allowed to drive maximum (…) km/hour with a car.
explanation: LESSON 12 – ‘Speed’.Ordinary roads:In Flanders and in the Brussels region up to 70 km/hour.In Wallonia: 90 km/h.

text: What is the maximum speed limit (… km/hour) for this car in this street?
explanation: LESSON 12 – ‘Speed’.The traffic sign says: up to 90 km/hour.

text: N-roads are ...
explanation: LESSON 12 – ‘Speed’.Ordinary roads:In Flanders until 31/12/2016 up to 90 km/h.In Flanders starting from 1/1/2017 up to 70 km/hour.(In Wallonia 90 km/hour).

text: The police stop you in a built-up area in Flanders because you were driving at 75 km/h. What are the consequences?

options.text: You receive an immediate temporary withdrawal of your driving licence.
You will have to appear before the court.

explanation: LESSON 12You risk an immediate withdrawal of your licence as soon as you drive more than 30 km/h too fast on motorways, expressways or ordinary roads.But in built-up areas, 30 km/h zones, or residential areas, you already risk this when you drive more than 20 km/h too fast.You risk a driving disqualification as soon as you exceed the speed limit by more than 40 km/h on motorways, expressways or ordinary roads.In built-up areas, 30 km/h zones, or residential areas, you already receive a disqualification once you exceed the limit by more than 30 km/h.This is decided by the judge, not by the police.

text: What is the maximum speed limit on a play street?
explanation: LESSON 12 – ‘Speed’. You must drive at walking pace.

text: This blue sign “200 m” belongs …
explanation: LESSON 12 – ‘Speed’The blue charger plate belongs to the board just above it.

text: Vehicles that are allowed to pass this sign, may drive a maximum of (...) km per hour.
This speed limit applies until the next junction.
explanation: LESSON 12 – ‘Speed’.Until you pass the board ‘End Zone’.

text: When you brake with ABS on a dry road surface, the stopping distance is shorter than without ABS on a dry road surface.
explanation: LESSON 13 – ‘The stopping distance’.Braking with ABS doesn’t necessarily mean that the stopping distance is shorter, than braking without ABS.

text: You drive 120 km/hour on this motorway. The stopping distance is about …
explanation: LESSON 13 – ‘The stopping distance’.50 km/hour: 30 meters.100 km/hour: 80 meters.120 km/hour: 110 meters.

text: The reaction time when you're tired …
explanation: LESSON 13 – ‘The stopping distance’.Because of fatigue, you will react more slowly to something.

text: On a wet road surface the braking distance is … on a dry road surface.
explanation: LESSON 13 – ‘The stopping distance’.On a wet surface is the braking distance longer.

text: Is the braking distance shorter or longer when driving on snow?
explanation: When driving on snow, the braking distance can be up to four times longer.

text: ABS or the anti-lock braking system prevents the wheels from slipping when you have to hit the brakes.
explanation: LESSON 13 – ‘The stopping distance’.The ABS-system makes sure that the driver is always in control of the car.

text: Another word for the braking distance is the stopping distance.
explanation: LESSON 13 – ‘The stopping distance’.The braking distance is the distance the car travels, starting from the moment when the driver presses the brake pedal, to the car completely stationary.

text: When you drive 50 km/hour, the thinking distance is about …
explanation: LESSON 13 – ‘The stopping distance’.At 50 km/hour is the reaction or thinking distance for example 15 meters,At 90 km/hour 27 meters.At 120 km/hour 36 meters.

text: The distance required to come to a halt once you start using the braking system of the car is the braking distance.
explanation: LESSON 13 – ‘The stopping distance’.This is the braking distance.

text: You are driving at 120 km/h on a motorway and it starts raining heavily. What do you do?

options.text: Keep a safe distance of 60 metres.
Slow down and increase the distance.

explanation: LESSON 13The faster you drive, the more distance you must keep.A simple formula helps you calculate it: speed divided by two.At 120 km/h, the safe following distance is 60 metres.At 100 km/h, it becomes 50 metres.But in heavy rain, snow or fog, you must slow down and increase the following distance.

text: A driver has to make a long trip abroad. How often should he ideally take a break?
explanation: LESSON 13During a long car journey, it is recommended to take a short break of at least 15 minutes about every two hours to prevent fatigue and stay alert. Make sure to get out of the car, stretch your legs, take deep breaths, and stay hydrated with water or light snacks.

text: What is the reaction distance when you are driving at 90 km/h?
explanation: LESSON 13Between the moment the driver sees the danger and the moment the brain processes this information and realises that the brake pedal must be pressed, the vehicle has already travelled a certain distance.The higher the speed, the longer the distance covered during the reaction time.• At 50 km/h, the reaction distance is about 15 metres.• At 90 km/h, the reaction distance is about 27 metres.• At 120 km/h, the reaction distance is about 36 metres.- This happens before the brake pedal is pressed.- A drunk driver reacts more slowly, which makes the reaction distance even longer.

text: The speed of the car in front of you is 90 km/hour. What is the safe following distance?
explanation: LESSON 13 – ‘The stopping distance’.Via a simple formula, you can calculate that distance: the speed at which you drive, divided by two.

text: You drive 100 km/hour with your car on a dry road surface. The stopping distance is …
explanation: LESSON 13 – ‘The stopping distance’.The stopping distance is about 80 meters.

text: You have to slow down. Is it correct that the faster you drive, the longer the stopping distance will be?
explanation: LESSON 13 – ‘The stopping distance’.The faster you drive, the longer the stopping distance.

text: The faster you drive, the longer the thinking distance.
explanation: LESSON 13 – ‘The stopping distance’.At 50 km/hour is the thinking or reaction distance for example 15 meters,At 90 km/hour 27 meters.At 120 km/hour 36 meters (before you have pressed the brake pedal).

text: When you brake with ABS on a wet road surface, the stopping distance is the same as with ABS on a dry road surface.
explanation: LESSON 13 – ‘The stopping distance’.When you brake with ABS on a wet road surface, the distance will be longer than with ABS on a dry road surface.

text: Who has priority?
explanation: LESSON 14 – ‘Crossing’.The blue sign says that car B has priority.

text: The sign 3,5 ton indicates on...
explanation: LESSON 14 – ‘Crossing’.Exam Tip: learn very well what signs have to do with M.A.W. or M.G.W. (Lesson 9).

text: Two cars on a central lane want to pass each other. Which car should drive on the lateral strip to make the crossing possible?
Do you have to give priority to the approaching traffic, when you drive your car in this street?
explanation: LESSON 14 – ‘Crossing’.The round sign says that you should give way.

text: Which driver has priority at this narrow passage?

options.text: The one who sees the red sign.
The one who sees the blue sign.

explanation: LESSON 14 – ‘Crossing’.Red sign: giving way.Blue sign: priority.

text: You approach this traffic sign with your car.

options.text: Oncoming traffic must give right of way to you.
You must give right of way to the oncoming traffic.

explanation: LESSON 14 – ‘Crossing’.The blue sign says you have priority.

text: In this street outside a built-up area, two cars want to cross each other. How much lateral distance must be kept?
explanation: LESSON 14 – ‘Crossing’.The traffic regulations don’t define 'how much' it must be. There is written: 'sufficient'.

text: What is the meaning of this sign?

options.text: Give priority to drivers coming from the other direction.
Traffic allowed in both direction, after there was first only one way direction.

explanation: LESSON 14 – ‘Crossing’.The sign that says that you should give priority, is a round sign with a red and black arrow.

text: Is a driver allowed to drive on the levelled verge to ease the passing?
explanation: LESSON 14 – ‘Crossing’.He may drive over the berm along the way.He may not drive on a cycle lane or on the part of the public road where cars can wait and park.

text: There is no oncoming traffic. Can you continue driving?
explanation: You have to wait until the traffic light is green.

text: What kind of sign is the bottom sign?
explanation: LESSON 14 – ‘Crossing’.Top warning sign: road narrows.

text: Who is allowed to drive first under the bridge?
explanation: LESSON 14 – ‘Crossing’.You see a sign that says that you should give priority.

text: This danger sign indicates a lane closure.
explanation: LESSON 14 – ‘Crossing’.Meaning: road narrows.Warning or danger sign.

text: The road is very narrow. Is the blue car allowed to drive a bit on the cycle lane to ease the passing?

options.text: Yes, only when he doesn’t hinder other road users.

explanation: LESSON 14 – ‘Crossing’.The bicycle lane is not part of the roadway. You may not drive on it.

text: What do these cars have to do at this junction?

options.text: They pass each other on the right.
They pass each other on the left.

explanation: LESSON 14 – ‘Crossing’.Arrows on the ground indicate that they should pass each other on the left.If there are no arrows, then they pass each other on the right.

text: Is the driver of the blue car allowed to drive on the reserved cycle lane in order to ease the passing?

options.text: He isn’t only allowed to, he must do it.

explanation: LESSON 14 – ‘Crossing’.A bicycle suggestion strip or reserved cycle lane is not a bicycle lane, but is part of the carriageway and the driver must drive on the right side of the road.

text: Who has priority?
explanation: LESSON 14 – ‘Crossing’.The road narrows along the side of car A. Therefore car A has to give priority.

text: Are you allowed to overtake a tram on the left when you come across an obstacle on the road?
explanation: LESSON 14 – ‘Crossing’.It may, on condition that you don’t disturb the other drivers.

text: Two cars will cross each other on a dirt road. How much lateral distance must be kept?
explanation: LESSON 14 – ‘Crossing’.The traffic regulations don’t define 'how much' it must be. There is written: 'sufficient'.

text: Speed can be reduced by parking reserved spaces on the road. This picture is taken within the car you drive.

options.text: The approaching traffic must give right of way to you.
You must give right of way to the approaching traffic.

explanation: LESSON 14 – ‘Crossing’.The obstacle is by your side, so you should give priority.

text: You drive a car on this road outside the built-up area and you want to cross an oncoming vehicle. How much lateral distance should be between the two cars.
explanation: LESSON 14

text: The driver of the blue car has stopped to let the cyclist pass first under the bridge. Should he have done that?
explanation: LESSON 14 – ‘Crossing’.The top blue sign says that you have priority.

text: A driver who sees this sign at a narrow passage, must give way to approaching traffic.
explanation: LESSON 14 – ‘Crossing’.Along the opposite direction is a blue sign.

text: What does this traffic sign mean?
explanation: LESSON 14 – ‘Crossing’.Meaning: one-way traffic.Information sign.

text: Roadworks. Which car has priority?
explanation: LESSON 14If there are no traffic signs regulating priority, the driver on the side where the obstacle is located must give way.In this example, the blue car may pass the road narrowing first, because the obstacle is on the side of the red car.

text: This sign indicates a narrow passage. What kind of sign is it?
explanation: LESSON 14 – ‘Crossing’.Triangular signs with a red border are usually warning or danger signs.Warning signs stand 150 meters for a danger.

text: Are you allowed to drive on the reserved parking lane to ease the passing?
explanation: LESSON 14 – ‘Crossing’.You are not allowed to drive there in order to pass a vehicle.

text: Which drawing is correct?
explanation: LESSON 14 – ‘Crossing’.At a crossroads without arrows on the road surface you cross to the right.

text: Who must give priority?
explanation: LESSON 14 – ‘Crossing’.There is no priority sign.The driver along whose side the road narrows, has to give way.

text: A bike suggestion lane. When passing a car …

options.text: ... you are not allowed to drive on it.
... you are allowed to drive on it.

explanation: LESSON 14 – ‘Crossing’.A bike suggestion lane (reserved cycle lane) is not a bicycle lane, but part of the roadway.You have to drive on the right side of the roadway, so on this strip.

text: There are two lanes in your direction on this one way road, at the top of a hill. Are you allowed to overtake another car on the left?
The barrier of this level crossing is open and no bell is ringing. However, the lights are out of order. Are you allowed to overtake a moped on the left?
explanation: LESSON 16At level crossings indicated by this sign, overtaking on the left is prohibited for: a horse-drawn vehicle; a vehicle with more than two wheels; or a two-wheeled motor vehicle, except when barriers are present or when the lunar white light is on.

text: You have a provisional driving licence B. Are you allowed to overtake a horse in harness on the left with a car?
Are you allowed to overtake the motorcycle on the left at this intersection?

options.text: Yes, if you leave sufficient lateral distance.

explanation: LESSON 16At intersections where you have priority, you may overtake other drivers on the left.- Priority at the next intersection.- Priority road.- Green traffic light.

text: Is the driver of the brown car allowed to overtake the blue one on the left?
In a built-up area, the blue car (A) continues to drive on the left lane.

options.text: This is only permitted if the driver turns left at the next intersection.
This is not allowed, because this lane is reserved for overtaking.

explanation: Drivers are allowed to follow the lane they prefer within built-up areas: . on a one-way road divided into lanes,. on a two-way road, with four or more lanes of which at least two are for each direction.

text: Can you catch another passenger car on the left during the hours indicated under the signboard?
explanation: This designation board applies only to drivers of vehicles of more than 3.5 tonnes intended for the carriage of goods.

text: May the driver of the blue car overtake the white car while it is overtaking a moped?
explanation: LESSON 16 On a two-way road, you may overtake a car that is overtaking a moped or a motorcycle.BUT: you may not overtake a car that is itself overtaking another car.

text: The brown car drives 35 kph. Is the blue car allowed to overtake on the left?
Is the blue car allowed to overtake the brown one on the left?
A one-way street within a built-up area. May the blue car continue driving on this lane?
explanation: LESSON 15Within a built-up area, drivers may choose the lane that best suits their destination, provided that:- the road is divided into lanes, and- the road is located in a built-up area.This is allowed in two cases:- on one-way roads with lanes;- on two-way roads divided into four or more lanes, with at least two lanes for each direction.

text: A roadway not divided into lanes inside a built-up area. May the red car overtake the white car on the left?
explanation: LESSON 16This prohibition sign indicates that trucks or combinations with a maximum authorised mass exceeding 3500 kg may not overtake:- a combination of vehicles, or- any vehicle with more than two wheels.The no-overtaking rule applies:- up to and including the next intersection, or- ends earlier if you see the “end of overtaking prohibition” sign.A car driver may therefore overtake a truck on the left after this sign.A bus may also overtake, since it is not a truck.

text: You are approaching a crossroads and you see one of these signs. At which intersection can you overtake a cyclist on the left?
explanation: At intersections where there are no signs that control the priority, or where board 1 is, and thus the priority of the right, it is forbidden to overtake animals in harness or a vehicle on more than two wheels or a two-wheel motor vehicle. (A cyclist is not a motor vehicle and may you catch up with it).

text: Enter a number. You want to overtake a car. What do you do first? 1. You put your turn signal on. 2. You look over your shoulder. 3. You look in the outside mirror. 4. You look in the rear view mirror.
explanation: Always check in the rear-view mirror first to make sure you are not being overtaken yourself.

text: Is the blue car allowed to overtake the red one on the left?
The brown car drives 48kph. Is the blue car allowed to overtake it on the left?
explanation: It would take too long to overtake.

text: Outside a built-up area. If you want to overtake this cyclist on the left, you have to leave a safe space in between of …
Are you allowed to overtake a moped rider on the left on a raised area within a built-up area?

options.text: Yes, if you leave one metre of lateral safety distance.

explanation: LESSON 16On a raised area, you may only overtake a cyclist on the left.(When the new traffic code comes into effect at the end of 2026, this will also be prohibited.)

text: The cars on the left and right-hand lane both run very slowly. Can the black car driving on the center lane overtake the car on the right-hand lane on the left?
explanation: If the car does, then at the same time, at the same time, he would overtake the car on the left-hand lane to the right and that is forbidden.

text: You are not allowed to overtake that car at this intersection. But who are you allowed to overtake?

options.text: Only a cyclist and a class A moped.
A cyclist, a class A moped, and a motorcycle.

explanation: LESSON 16At an intersection where the priority-to-the-right rule applies, you may only overtake a cyclist and similar users, such as an electric scooter, on the left.

text: Is the driver of a car allowed to overtake a lorry on the left past this sign?
On a carriageway, subdivided into lanes, you approach the top of a cluttered slope. A slow bicycle is driving in front of you. Can you overtake the bike?
explanation: You may overtake near the top of a cluttered slope if the road is divided into lanes and you do not drive over the white continuous line.

text: Is the blue car allowed to overtake these two cars at the same time on the left on this
Is a motorcycle allowed to overtake a car on the left past this sign?
There are no cyclists on and near the crossing. Is the blue car allowed to overtake the brown one on the left?
A roadway divided into lanes outside a built-up area. May the red truck overtake the white car on the left?
explanation: LESSON 16This prohibition sign indicates that trucks or combinations with a maximum authorised mass exceeding 3500 kg may not overtake:- a combination of vehicles, or- any vehicle with more than two wheels.The no-overtaking rule applies:- up to and including the next intersection, or- ends earlier if you see the “end of overtaking prohibition” sign.A car driver may therefore overtake a truck on the left after this sign.A bus may also overtake, since it is not a truck.

text: On a motorway with at least three lanes you are allowed to choose the lane you drive on.
The driver of a car wants to overtake another car on the left. Is he allowed?
Is a motorcycle allowed to overtake a car on the left past these signs?
Is the driver of the brown car allowed to overtake the blue one on the left?
Are you allowed to overtake a car on the left on this road with your car?
May the car overtake the horse-drawn cart on the left?
explanation: LESSON 16The red circular prohibition sign indicates that it is forbidden for drivers to:- overtake a combination of vehicles, or- overtake any vehicle with more than two wheels.The no-overtaking rule applies:- up to and including the next intersection, or- ends earlier if you see the “end of overtaking prohibition” sign.A car driver may therefore overtake a two-wheeled motorcycle,but the motorcyclist may not overtake a car, because a car has more than two wheels.

text: You drive behind a garbage truck that is difficult to overtake. What are you doing?

options.text: You give a short signal with your horn.

explanation: LESSON 16

text: What is right? Beyond this sign....

options.text: .... a car may overtake a motorcycle on the left.
.... a motorcycle may overtake a car on the left.
.... a car or motorcycle may not overtake on the left.

explanation: The red sign says that drivers are forbidden to overtake a vehicle with more than two wheels on the left.

text: May the motorcycle overtake the motorcycle on the left?
explanation: LESSON 16The red circular prohibition sign indicates that drivers are forbidden to:- overtake a combination of vehicles, or- overtake any vehicle with more than two wheels.The no-overtaking rule applies:- up to and including the next intersection, or- it ends earlier if you see the end-of-prohibition sign.A car driver may therefore overtake a two-wheeled motorcycle.But the motorcyclist may not overtake a car, because a car has more than two wheels.

text: Are you allowed to overtake a cyclist on the left at this junction?
If you want to overtake this cyclist on the left outside a built-up area, you have to leave a safe space in between of 1,5 meter.
explanation: Inside a built-up area: 1 meter.Outside a built-up area: 1,5 meter (31/5/2019).

text: Can you overtake a cyclist on the right who is about to turn left on a raised section?
explanation: LESSON 16A cyclist who is about to turn left on a raised section of the road, inside or outside a built-up area, may be overtaken on the right.

text: The moon-white light is on at this level crossing with double tracks. Which vehicles are you allowed to overtake on the left if it's safe?

options.text: Only cyclists and similar road users.

explanation: LESSON 16As long as the red lights are not flashing, you may approach the level crossing.When the red lights flash alternately, you must stop and you are not allowed to enter the level crossing.

text: The brown car is parked. The blue car …

options.text: ... passes the brown car on the left.
... overtakes the brown car on the left.

text: What lateral distance must the car keep when overtaking the cyclist?
explanation: LESSON 15When overtaking a pedestrian stepping onto the carriageway, or a cyclist or moped rider riding on the carriageway, you must keep at least 1.5 metres of lateral distance outside built-up areas.The distance kept by this car is therefore insufficient.

text: You must overtake this tram on the right.
Give the most correct answer. On a speed hump, a driver of a car is allowed to overtake…

options.text: ... a cyclist or a moped on the left.
... a car, a moped or a cyclist on the left.

text: When you see these signs and you want to follow a certain direction and therefore you pass the vehicles driving on your left, then you are not overtaking these vehicles.
The brown car wants to turn left. Is the blue car allowed to overtake the brown one on the right?
An intersection without traffic lights or priority signs. Is the blue car allowed to overtake a two-wheeled moped on the left?
explanation: This is an intersection where the priority-to-the-right rule applies.At this type of intersection, the car is only allowed to overtake a cyclist on the left.

text: Past which of these signs are you allowed to overtake another car on the left with your car?
You approach a dangerous bend. Are you allowed to overtake on the right a cyclist, who rides on the road on the left side and who wants to turn left?
Are you allowed to overtake the motorcycle on the left at this intersection?

options.text: Yes, if you leave sufficient lateral distance.

explanation: LESSON 16At intersections where no traffic signs regulate priority, or where this road sign is present and therefore the priority to the right applies, it is forbidden to overtake on the left:a vehicle with a trailer,a vehicle with more than two wheels,or a motor vehicle with two wheels.A cyclist is not a motor vehicle, so you are allowed to overtake them. You may also overtake a personal mobility device.

text: You drive on a road with this traffic sign on it. Are you allowed to overtake a car on the left at the next junction, when it is safe?
A level crossing without white lights and no barriers. Is a car allowed to overtake a motorcycle on the left?
Beyond which sign you cannot overtake a cyclist on the left?
Where are you allowed to overtake a moped on the left at an intersection?

options.text: On a road with priority from the right.
On a priority road and a road with priority from the right.

text: The grey car keeps driving on the middle lane. Are you allowed to overtake it in a way the arrow points out?

options.text: Yes, but only when there are three lanes in your direction.

text: A level crossing with barriers. The white lights are flashing. Is a car allowed to overtake a lorry on the left on this level crossing?
This picture is taken from your car. Are you allowed to overtake the cyclist on the left?
May the motorcycle overtake the truck on the left?
explanation: LESSON 16The red circular prohibition sign indicates that drivers are forbidden to:- overtake a combination of vehicles, or- overtake any vehicle with more than two wheels.The no-overtaking rule applies:- up to and including the next intersection, or- it ends earlier if you see the end-of-prohibition sign.A car driver may therefore overtake a two-wheeled motorcycle.But the motorcyclist may not overtake a car, because a car has more than two wheels.

text: How much lateral distance should the car driver leave when he passes the cyclist.
explanation: Within a built-up area: 1 meter.Outside a built-up area: 1.5 meters.

text: You drive with the blue car. The driver in front of you only drives 70 km / h. Can you overtake that driver on the left?

options.text: No, because I can only drive 70 km/hour.

explanation: The speed limit (70) applies only to the strip above which the board hangs (Explanation lesson 12: 'Speed').

text: Are you allowed to overtake on the left here?
Outside a built-up area. If you want to overtake this moped on the left, you have to leave a safe space in between of 1,5 meter.
Is the black car allowed to overtake the grey car on the left?
How much lateral distance must the driver keep here when overtaking the moped rider?
explanation: LESSON 15When overtaking a cyclist or a moped rider within built-up areas, you must keep 1 metre of lateral distance.Outside built-up areas, the distance must be at least 1.5 metres.

text: Is the driver of the red car allowed to overtake the blue one on the left?
Can the blue car cross the brown by the right in a built-up area?
Can you overtake a cyclist on the left on a raised section?
explanation: LESSON 16A cyclist who is about to turn left on a raised section of the road, inside or outside a built-up area, may also be overtaken on the right.

text: Is the blue car allowed to overtake the brown lorry on the left?
A junction with traffic lights and the light is green for you. Under the green light there is this traffic sign. Are you allowed to overtake a car on the left at this junction, when it’s safe?
You have a provisional driving licence B. Are you allowed to overtake a lorry on the left as soon as you pass this sign?
The blue car is slowing down. Is the grey car allowed to overtake on the left?

options.text: Yes, if there is no pedestrian.

text: To overtake a car on the left which is already overtaking another car on the left is called …
How much lateral distance should the car driver leave when he passes the cyclist.
explanation: Within a built-up area: 1 meter.Outside a built-up area: 1.5 meters.

text: Is it allowed to overtake a moped on the left beyond this sign?
explanation: The red sign says that drivers are forbidden to overtake a vehicle with more than two wheels on the left.

text: May the truck overtake the blue car on the left?

options.text: Yes, because a truck is not a passenger car.

explanation: LESSON 16The red circular prohibition sign indicates that it is forbidden for drivers to:- overtake a combination of vehicles, or- overtake any vehicle with more than two wheels.The no-overtaking rule applies:- up to and including the next intersection, or- ends earlier if you see the “end of overtaking prohibition” sign.A car driver may therefore overtake a two-wheeled motorcycle,but the motorcyclist may not overtake a car, because a car has more than two wheels.

text: May the car overtake the truck on the left?
explanation: LESSON 16This prohibition sign indicates that trucks or combinations with a maximum authorised mass exceeding 3500 kg may not overtake:- a combination of vehicles, or- any vehicle with more than two wheels.The no-overtaking rule applies:- up to and including the next intersection, or- ends earlier if you see the “end of overtaking prohibition” sign.A car driver may therefore overtake a truck on the left after this sign.A bus may also overtake, since it is not a truck.

text: The driver of the blue car drives faster than the red one. Is that allowed?
May the car overtake the truck on the left?
explanation: LESSON 16The red circular prohibition sign indicates that drivers are forbidden to:- overtake a combination of vehicles, or- overtake any vehicle with more than two wheels.The no-overtaking rule applies:- up to and including the next intersection, or- it ends earlier if you see the end-of-prohibition sign.A car driver may therefore overtake a two-wheeled motorcycle.But the motorcyclist may not overtake a car, because a car has more than two wheels.

text: A police car with flashing lights approaches a junction. Does the driver of the grey car have to give priority?
explanation: LESSON 17 – ‘Qualified persons’.There is no alarm signal audible.

text: The dipped headlights are switched on. What is your reaction.
explanation: LESSON 17 – ‘Qualified persons’.Only when the blue flashing lights burn and you hear the alarm signal, you should give priority.

text: The police officer raises one arm in the air. Who must stop?
explanation: LESSON 17 – ‘Qualified persons’.When an officer raises one arm vertically, all road users, including pedestrians, must stop.

text: What is the hierarchical order?
explanation: LESSON 17 – ‘Qualified persons’.At the top of the commands of an agent.Then the traffic lights.Then the road signs.Then the traffic rules.

text: The driver of the moped …

options.text: ... is allowed to drive straight through.

explanation: LESSON 17 – ‘Qualified persons’.He drives to the belly of the agent and needs to stop.

text: Is the blue car allowed to cross over the junction?
explanation: LESSON 17 – ‘Qualified persons’.Yes, because the driver drives in the direction of the side or the fingertips of the agent.

text: Two arms stretched out horizontally have the same meaning as one arm.
explanation: LESSON 17 – ‘Qualified persons’.The command is the same.

text: Who must stop?

options.text: The red car and the moped.

explanation: LESSON 17 – ‘Qualified persons’.The moto drives to the belly and the brown car to the back of the agent. They must stop.

text: Just as you enter an intersection, a police officer raises one arm vertically. What do you do?

options.text: You slow down and wait for the order he will give.
You continue driving and leave the intersection.

explanation: LESSON 17When a police officer raises one arm vertically at an intersection, all road users must stop.Anyone already on the intersection must leave it as quickly as possible.

text: You approach this junction. Do you have to stop?
explanation: LESSON 17 – ‘Qualified persons’.It is a crossroads without traffic lights.

text: Who is allowed to cross the junction?
explanation: LESSON 17 – ‘Qualified persons’.The agent gives the order that the motorcycle has to stop.

text: Is the red car allowed to cross the junction?
explanation: LESSON 17 – ‘Qualified persons’.He drives to the belly of the agent and needs to stop.

text: A tram driver doesn’t need to take into account the orders of an authorized person.
explanation: LESSON 17 – ‘Qualified persons’.Tram drivers do not have to follow the traffic regulations, except the orders of an authorized person and the traffic lights.

text: The driver of the black car wants to turn left.

options.text: He is only allowed to drive on.

explanation: LESSON 17 – ‘Qualified persons’.The driver may drive straight through, or turn to the left or to the right.

text: Who is allowed to cross the junction?
Who is allowed to cross the junction?

options.text: The blue and the green car.
The brown car and the moped.

explanation: LESSON 17 – ‘Qualified persons’.The blue and the green car drive to the fingertips of the agent.

text: The traffic lights are out of order. Who is allowed to cross first?
explanation: LESSON 17 – ‘Qualified persons’.The brown car drives to the belly of the agent and needs to stop.

text: You are approaching an intersection where an officer is standing with one arm extended horizontally. What instruction is the officer giving?

options.text: You may continue driving, but not turn left.

explanation: LESSON 17When an officer extends one or both arms horizontally, road users approaching the officer’s chest or back must stop.Road users approaching the officer’s fingertips or side may continue onto the intersection to go straight, turn left, or turn right.An officer with both arms extended horizontally gives exactly the same instruction as with only one arm extended horizontally.

text: Who is allowed to cross the junction?

options.text: Not the blue car nor the brown one.

explanation: LESSON 17 – ‘Qualified persons’.The brown car drives to the side or to the fingertips of the agent.

text: The blue car driver approaches the back of the agent.

options.text: The driver may turn to the right.

explanation: LESSON 17 – ‘Qualified persons’.If an officer has one or two arms stretched out horizontally, this is a stop signal for all traffic approaching from in front of or from behind the outstretched arms.

text: You are entering an intersection. Suddenly, a police officer raises his arm. What do you do?
explanation: LESSON 17When an officer raises his arm, it means that all vehicles must stop.Vehicles already in the intersection must leave it as quickly as possible, continuing in the direction they intended to go.

text: You approach this police officer with your car.

options.text: You are allowed to cross the junction.

explanation: LESSON 17 – ‘Qualified persons’.He drives to the belly of the agent and needs to stop.

text: Which order does the police officer give?

options.text: The driver must stop next to the road.

explanation: LESSON 17 – ‘Qualified persons’.You need to stop (for a control).

text: The driver of this car must stop.
explanation: LESSON 17 – ‘Qualified persons’.The driver drives to the back of the agent, who has horizontal stretched arms.

text: Does the ambulance with flashing lights and warning signal have to stop?
explanation: LESSON 17 – ‘Qualified persons’.The orders of a police officer are going above all.

text: Is the blue car still allowed to turn left?
explanation: LESSON 17 – ‘Qualified persons’.When an officer raises one arm vertically, all road users, including pedestrians, must stop.

text: When a police officer whistles, the drivers must stop.
explanation: LESSON 17 – ‘Qualified persons’.If he blows on a whistle, this means that you need to look to him and to the command he gives or is going to give.

text: What must drivers do who are on the road that is blocked by the police officer’s horizontally extended arm?
explanation: LESSON 17When a police officer extends one or both arms horizontally, all drivers approaching the officer’s front or back must stop.➡️ Continuing to drive or turning, as this driver intends to do, is a fourth-degree offence.

text: A police car with blue flashing lights and warning signal. What do you do?

options.text: You drive faster in order to stay ahead.
You just drive on as if nothing is happening.

explanation: LESSON 17 – ‘Qualified persons’.It is a priority vehicle and you should give priority.

text: What is the international emergency number?
explanation: LESSON 17 – ‘Qualified persons’.112 is the international emergency number.

text: If a police officer raises his arm, must a tram also stop?

options.text: No, because a tram always has priority.

explanation: LESSON 17When a police officer raises his arm, all drivers must stop.Drivers who are already on the intersection must leave it as quickly as possible.A tram normally has priority, but it must always obey the instructions of an authorised person and traffic lights.

text: Traffic sergeants, group leaders for cyclists or motorcyclists on a junction with traffic lights have the same authorization as an authorized person.
explanation: LESSON 17 – ‘Qualified persons’.They may only give directions and have no authorization.At a crossroads with traffic lights, they can do nothing.

text: The traffic light is red. Are you allowed to read the messages on your cell phone while you wait?
Does a driver of a car have to take into account the special lights for cyclists?
explanation: LESSON 18 – ‘Traffic lights’.Cyclists and mopeds must do it.

text: When should you stop?

options.text: If the amber light is flashing.

explanation: LESSON 18 – ‘Traffic lights’.If the orange light flashes, this means that the lights are defective.If the lights are defective, you must take into account the priority tables and rules.

text: This traffic light for a tram has the same meaning as ...
explanation: LESSON 18: 'Traffic lights'.

text: Is the driver of the moped allowed to turn left?
explanation: LESSON 18 – ‘Traffic lights’.The moto may go straight, or turn left or right.

text: Are you allowed to hold your mobile phone in the car while waiting at a red traffic light?
explanation: Even when stopped at a red light, you are still considered a road user and are not allowed to hold or use a mobile phone, unless it is placed in a holder designed for that purpose.

text: The barriers are already open, but the red light is still on. Can I cross the crossing already?
explanation: You are not allowed to drive onto the level crossing as long as the red flashing light is on, even if the barriers are open.

text: The traffic lights are defective. Who has priority?
explanation: LESSON 18 – ‘Traffic lights’. If the traffic lights are defective, then the usual priority rules apply.There are no signs under the lights that control the priority, so priority from the right.

text: Who must stop?

options.text: The brown and the blue car.

explanation: LESSON 18 – ‘Traffic lights’.An agent's order goes above the traffic lights.

text: This traffic light for a tram means:

options.text: In every direction you can drive on.

explanation: LESSON 18 – ‘Traffic lights’.Just straight ahead.

text: You want to turn right. Do you have to stop first, before you cross the junction?
explanation: LESSON 18 – ‘Traffic lights’.Traffic signs at traffic lights do not apply when the lights work.

text: When you see three green arrows above the lanes, it means you can choose the lane you drive on.
