explanation: LESSON 18 – ‘Traffic lights’.You should drive as far as possible on the right-hand lane.The other lanes can be used to retrieve links, or to follow a blue sign indicating a direction, or file.

text: What does the white / yellow flashing light mean in the middle of the lights for a tram?

options.text: Tram must be driven very slowly due to a possible defect on the tracks.
You may cross the light with double caution, with due observance of the prevailing priority rules.

explanation: LESSON 18 – ‘Traffic lights’.Important: double caution and compliance with the priority rules.

text: The round traffic light is green and you want to turn left. But the evacuation arrow is not burning yet. Can you cross the crossroads?
explanation: LESSON 18 – ‘Traffic lights’. A left-hand green arrow placed separately when crossing a crossroads means that the opposite traffic on the lane that leaves the drivers on the left will be held by a red light to facilitate clearing of the intersection.

text: The traffic lights turn amber. The blue car …

options.text: ... is allowed to drive past the amber lights if it can’t stop safely anymore.

explanation: LESSON 18 – ‘Traffic lights’.Normally he must stop except if it cannot really be safe.

text: This picture is taken from the car you drive in. What do you do?

options.text: You are allowed to follow the grey car.

explanation: LESSON 18 – ‘Traffic lights’.The orange light flashes and so you stop.

text: Does the driver of the blue car have to give right of way to the pedestrian?
explanation: LESSON 18 – ‘Traffic lights’.The green arrow says that you can turn right, but give priority to other road users.

text: Past the flashing amber light …

options.text: ... you are not allowed to drive.
... you are allowed to drive and you have priority.
... you are allowed to drive and you have to apply the normal priority rules.

explanation: LESSON 18 – ‘Traffic lights’.It means the lights are defective.Important: "double caution" and "valid priority rules".

text: You see these lights. What can you do?
explanation: LESSON 18 – ‘Traffic lights’.The green arrow says you can turn right.BUT, you should give priority to drivers who regularly come from other directions and also to pedestrians.

text: When the traffic lights are green, it is allowed

options.text: ... to cross the junction when it is free.

explanation: LESSON 18 – ‘Traffic lights’.You can drive past a green light when the crossroads are free.

text: The driver of the brown car wants to turn left. He is allowed to cross at the junction. B, Incorrect.
explanation: LESSON 18 – ‘Traffic lights’.He can turn left or right.

text: Can you send a text while waiting in the car for a red light?
explanation: LESSON 18 – ‘Traffic lights’. That is prohibited.

text: If the green evacuation arrow is burning ....

options.text: ... all other lights at the intersection are red.
... the oncoming traffic has a red light.

explanation: LESSON 18 - 'Traffic lights'.The oncoming traffic has a red light.

text: You are approaching a red traffic light. You press the clutch pedal.
explanation: Never press the clutch pedal to slow down.

text: Entering a level crossing while the red lights are flashing, is ...
The barriers are going down. You are only allowed to pass the red flashing lights and the lowering barriers when you can’t stop safely anymore.
explanation: LESSON 18 – ‘Traffic lights’.That is a serious violation and your driving license can be revoked.

text: The green filter arrow is lit up. Is the driver of the blue car still allowed to cross at the junction and turn left?
explanation: LESSON 18 – ‘Traffic lights’.Drivers at the intersection can leave it.The blue car must not drive past the red light.

text: This picture is taken from the car you drive in.

options.text: You must, if necessary, give priority.

explanation: LESSON 18 – ‘Traffic lights’.The traffic lights do not apply to your lane.The board says that you have to give priority.

text: The traffic lights are green. Do you still have to consider the sign below?
explanation: LESSON 18 – ‘Traffic lights’.You must only take note of the priority sign if the traffic lights are defective.

text: This traffic light for a tram has the same meaning as ...
explanation: LESSON 18 – ‘Traffic lights’.An inverted triangle has the same meaning as a green traffic light.

text: The barriers are still fully open, but the alarm signal is clearly audible. Can you still drive on the road?
explanation: LESSON 18 – ‘Traffic lights’. No. That would be a serious offence !!!

text: A driver of a car must not take into account the special traffic lights for the pedestrians.
explanation: LESSON 18 – ‘Traffic lights’.Only pedestrians need to take this into account.

text: A level crossing without barriers, but with lights. The lights are defective. Can a car overtake a moped on the left?
explanation: LESSON 18 - "Traffic Lights."If there are either barriers or lights that work, then it is allowed.

text: Which driver is not allowed to cross the junction?

options.text: From the car and the moped.

explanation: LESSON 18 – ‘Traffic lights’.Blue car: red light (= stop).Moto: orange yellow light (= stop).

text: The arrow you see here is a green filter arrow which indicates that the drivers who are already on the junction can drive safely to the left.
explanation: LESSON 18 – ‘Traffic lights’.It's not an evacuation arrow.This arrow says that you can cross the intersection to the left.

text: The traffic light turns orange. Can you still cross the intersection?

options.text: Yes, if you endanger others by stopping.

explanation: LESSON 18 – ‘Traffic lights’.Orange says you have to stop. Except if you are too close to the intersection, and you put the driver behind you at risk.

text: This sign says there are traffic lights 150 meters further. This plate is ...
explanation: LESSON 18 – ‘Traffic lights’. This danger or warning sign means traffic lights. Danger signs are placed 150 meters before a danger.

text: The brown car driver wants to turn left. May he drive onto the intersection?

options.text: Yes, because the light is green.
No, because the intersection is not free.

explanation: LESSON 18 – ‘Traffic lights’.Although the light is green, the driver of the brown car must not drive the intersection yet. He has to wait until the intersection is free.

text: Who is allowed to cross at the junction?
explanation: LESSON 18 – ‘Traffic lights’.The driver of the blue car sees a round green light.

text: Which vehicle is allowed to cross at the junction?
explanation: LESSON 18 – ‘Traffic lights’.An agent's order goes above the traffic lights.

text: You approach a red traffic lights with your car. You stop in front of …
explanation: LESSON 18 – ‘Traffic lights’.The first stop line is the line that a driver sees first.

text: The driver of the brown car wants to cross at the junction. Does he have to consider the red light?
explanation: LESSON 18 – ‘Traffic lights’.No, because the round red light is just left of him.

text: Does the driver of the car have to stop before he can enter this intersection?
explanation: LESSON 18 - 'Traffic lights'No, because the traffic light works and is green.If the lights are defective, he must stop.

text: Who is allowed to cross the junction?
explanation: LESSON 18 – ‘Traffic lights’.The brown car drives to the fingertips or side of the agent and may cross the intersection.

text: Who is allowed to cross at the junction?

options.text: The green and the blue car.
The brown car and the moped.

explanation: LESSON 18 – ‘Traffic lights’.The agent orders the brown car and the motorcycle to stop.

text: Fill in a number. Which traffic sign has the same meaning as a green light?
explanation: LESSON 18(1) An inverted triangle has the same meaning as a green light.(2) A circle has the same meaning as a steady amber light.(3) A horizontal bar has the same meaning as a red light.(4) A diagonal bar pointing left allows driving only in that direction.

text: This traffic light for a tram has the same meaning as ...
explanation: LESSON 18 – ‘Traffic lights’.

text: The traffic light is green, but the crossroads are not yet free. May you stay on the crossing point while waiting for the intersection to be free?
explanation: LESSON 18 – ‘Traffic lights’. You must not cross the crossroads unless the light is green and the crossroads are free. But you cannot block the crossing point while waiting.

text: You stop behind a car that has stopped at a red traffic light. When do you keep a safe distance?

options.text: When you can still see the license plate.
When you can still see the rear tyres.

explanation: LESSON 18It is always safe to leave enough distance. Driving schools teach that it is safe if you can still see the rear tyres of the vehicle in front of you.

text: A yellow arrow above a lane means …

options.text: ... you must take the first exit.

explanation: LESSON 18 – ‘Traffic lights’.You must leave the lane.

text: You're waiting in your car when the traffic light is red. May you constantly give some gas to keep warm the engine?
explanation: LESSON 18 – ‘Traffic lights’.Gently give gas while you wait (broum ... broum ... broum ...) may not.

text: This sign means …
explanation: LESSON 19 – ‘Junction and traffic sign’. Meaning: End of priority road. Type: Priority board.

text: What does this traffic sign mean?
explanation: LESSON 19 – ‘Junction and traffic sign’. Type: Priority board.

text: Is the blue car allowed to overtake the brown car on the left?
explanation: LESSON 19 – ‘Junction and traffic sign’. At a crossroads where you see this priority board, left overtaking is allowed.

text: Are you allowed to overtake the brown car at this junction?
explanation: LESSON 19 – ‘Junction and traffic sign’. It is a crossroads where you have priority.

text: Who must give priority?
explanation: LESSON 19 – ‘Junction and traffic sign’. The brown car drives on a priority road.

text: Who is the first to cross the intersection?
explanation: LESSON 19 – ‘Junction and traffic sign’. A STOP means that you must stop and give way to the drivers (not the pedestrians) that run on the track you are going to takeA pedestrian is not a driver and there is no pedestrian crossing.

text: Who is allowed to cross first at the junction?
explanation: LESSON 19 – ‘Junction and traffic sign’. The traffic sign at the right of car A says that the driver has priority at this intersection.

text: This driver wants to turn right at this junction. Even if there are no other road users, the driver must first come to a complete stop before entering the junction.
explanation: LESSON 19If there is a STOP sign you must come to a complete stop.The give-way sign (inverted triangle) means that you must yield to other drivers and, if necessary, come to a complete stop.If there are no other drivers, you don’t need to stop completely and may enter the junction.

text: Who has to give priority?
explanation: LESSON 19 – ‘Junction and traffic sign’. At the right of car B is a sign that says that the driver must give priority.

text: When you see these signs, you know you … at the next junction.

options.text: ... must give priority and if necessary stop …

explanation: LESSON 19 – ‘Junction and traffic sign’. There is no STOP on the blue bottom sign.

text: At what maximum speed may this car drive past the yellow sign within a built-up area in the Brussels Region?
explanation: LESSON 12It is a roadway within a built-up area.In the Walloon and Flemish Regions, the maximum permitted speed inside built-up areas is 50 km/h.In the Brussels Region, it is 30 km/h.The yellow sign has nothing to do with speed — it is a priority-road sign indicating that you are driving on a priority road.

text: Who has priority at this junction?
explanation: LESSON 19 – ‘Junction and traffic sign’. The traffic sign to the right of him says that the driver of the black car has priority at this intersection.

text: Who is allowed to cross first at the junction?
explanation: LESSON 19 – ‘Junction and traffic sign’. Next to car C is a stop sign. Auto A has priority from the right.

text: Who has priority?
explanation: LESSON 19 – ‘Junction and traffic sign’. A driver who wants to drive on a roundabout must give priority.

text: Who is the first to cross the intersection?
explanation: LESSON 19 – ‘Junction and traffic sign’. A triangle on its tip means that you have to give way to the drivers (not the pedestrians) that run on the path you are going to take, and that you eventually have to stop. There is no pedestrian crossing.

text: What is correct? The direction indicator must be switched on …

options.text: ... when leaving or entering a roundabout.

explanation: LESSON 19 – ‘Junction and traffic sign’. You leave a roundabout: it must burn.You want to enter a roundabout: it may burn.

text: This traffic sign applies …

options.text: ... until you see a sign: End priority zone.

explanation: LESSON 19 – ‘Junction and traffic sign’. Meaning: Priority at the next intersection.Type: Priority board.

text: Which car must switch on its right direction indicator?
explanation: LESSON 19 – ‘Junction and traffic sign’. When you enter a roundabout, you must not turn on the direction indicator light.

text: This driver wants to turn right at this junction. No other road users are visible. Must he switch on the right indicator?

options.text: No, if there’s no one around, it’s pointless.

explanation: LESSON 21Every lateral movement you make must be signalled using the indicator.It doesn’t matter whether there are other drivers or not.

text: This driver wants to turn left at this junction. Even if there are no other road users, the driver must first come to a complete stop before entering the junction.
explanation: LESSON 19The give-way sign (inverted triangle) means that you must yield to other drivers and, if necessary, come to a complete stop.If there are no other drivers, you don’t need to stop completely and may enter the junction.If there is a STOP sign, however, you must come to a complete stop.

text: A roundabout. When must you switch on the right indicator?

options.text: When entering and leaving a roundabout.

explanation: LESSON 19When leaving a roundabout, you must switch on the right indicator.

text: Who is allowed to cross first at the junction?
explanation: LESSON 19 – ‘Junction and traffic sign’. At the right of car B is a sign that says that the driver must give priority.

text: Who has priority?
explanation: LESSON 19 – ‘Junction and traffic sign’. The driver of car ‘2’ sees a stop sign.

text: When you follow the road to the left, you have priority at the next junction.
explanation: LESSON 19 – ‘Junction and traffic sign’. The blue underside indicates that the main road turns to the left.

text: This picture is taken from the car you drive and you’re leaving a roundabout. When leaving you have to give priority to the cyclists and mopeds on the cycle lane.
explanation: LESSON 19 – ‘Junction and traffic sign’. The board says that you must give priority and that cyclists and mopeds can come from both directions.

text: Fill in a number. After which traffic sign are you driving on a priority road?
explanation: LESSON 19Sign 2 means you are on a priority road. You have priority at all intersections until the sign is cancelled or another sign changes the priority.Sign 1 gives you priority only at the next intersection.Sign 3 says nothing about priority; it only means traffic flows in one direction.Sign 4 simply indicates a direction you must follow, not priority.

text: Which road markings do you often see at this traffic sign?
Which car is allowed to cross first at the junction?
explanation: LESSON 19 – ‘Junction and traffic sign’. The board says that the blue car must give priority and stop if necessary.

text: At this junction you have to give right of way, except to cyclists and mopeds.
explanation: LESSON 19 – ‘Junction and traffic sign’. Also give priority to cyclists and mopeds who can come from both directions.

text: Who is allowed to cross first at the junction?
explanation: LESSON 19 – ‘Junction and traffic sign’. Next to car A is a stop sign.

text: The white reversed triangles in front of the blue car are also called …
explanation: LESSON 19 – ‘Junction and traffic sign’. Shark teeth indicate where you need to stop if necessary.

text: When you see this traffic sign, you know that you …

options.text: ... have to give priority and if necessary stop.

explanation: LESSON 19 – ‘Junction and traffic sign’. Meaning: Provide priority and, if necessary, stop.Type: Priority board.

text: When you drive on this road, you are allowed to overtake a vehicle on the left, if it is safe.
explanation: LESSON 19 – ‘Junction and traffic sign’. Meaning: Priority road. Type: Priority board.

text: You are driving in the inner lane of a two-lane roundabout. What must you do to exit?

options.text: Stop and wait until the cars in the outer lane have passed.
Exit directly, you have priority over the cars in the outer lane.
Keep circulating until the outer lane is free so you can exit.

explanation: LESSON 19To exit a two-lane roundabout from the inner lane, you must first change lanes to the outer lane, using your right indicator. You must give way to vehicles already driving in the outer lane. If you cannot do this in time, it is safer to make another loop around the roundabout rather than blocking traffic or creating a dangerous situation.

text: You approach a junction. What do you have to do 100m ahead?

options.text: Give priority and stop if needed.

explanation: LESSON 19 – ‘Junction and traffic sign’. If the word STOP is on the blue underside, you will see a STOP board.

text: Who is allowed to cross first at the junction?
explanation: LESSON 19 – ‘Junction and traffic sign’. The brown car drives on a priority road.

text: Who is allowed to cross first at the junction?
explanation: LESSON 19 – ‘Junction and traffic sign’. Next to car A is a stop sign.

text: Who is allowed to cross first at the junction?
explanation: LESSON 19 – ‘Junction and traffic sign’. Next to car B is a stop sign.

text: You are approaching this intersection. Where must you stop?
explanation: LESSON 19You must always come to a complete stop when there is a STOP sign, even if there are no other road users. You stop just before the stop line. If there is no stop line, you stop level with the STOP sign. You must give way to other drivers on the road you intend to enter.

text: The driver of this car saw no other road users and carefully entered the intersection without stopping. Was he allowed to do that?

options.text: Yes, because there is no stop line on the road.

explanation: LESSON 19A STOP means you must come to a complete stop at the stop line and yield to drivers on the public road you want to enter.If there is no stop line on the pavement, you must stop at the traffic sign.Even if there are no drivers on the crossing road, you must still come to a complete stop before entering the intersection.

text: Who has priority?
explanation: LESSON 19 – ‘Junction and traffic sign’. The sign says that the yellow car has priority at the intersection.

text: Which traffic sign is associated with the road marking called shark’s teeth?
explanation: LESSON 19An inverted triangle means you must give way to drivers on the road you are about to enter and stop if necessary.If there are no drivers on the crossing road, you don’t have to stop and may enter the intersection.A line formed by inverted triangles, also known as shark’s teeth, indicates the place where you must stop if necessary.If it’s not really necessary, you don’t have to make a full stop.

text: When the traffic lights don’t work at this junction, the priority rule applies.
explanation: LESSON 19 – ‘Junction and traffic sign’. Under the traffic light there is a sign that says you should give priority.

text: When the traffic lights are red, cyclists and drivers of two-wheeled mopeds stop in front of …
explanation: LESSON 19 – ‘Junction and traffic sign’. Other vehicles stop for the first stop line.

text: Do you have to use the direction indicator when you leave this junction?
explanation: LESSON 19 – ‘Junction and traffic sign’. It's not a roundabout.

text: When you follow the road to the left, you have priority at the next junction.
explanation: LESSON 19 – ‘Junction and traffic sign’. The bottom sign indicates how the priority road goes away.

text: Who is allowed to cross first at the junction?
explanation: LESSON 19 – ‘Junction and traffic sign’. The sign next to car B says that the driver has priority at this intersection.

text: Who is allowed to cross first at the junction?
explanation: LESSON 19 – ‘Junction and traffic sign’. The blue car stops for a stop line.

text: When you cross this junction (direction of the arrow), you have priority to the drivers from the left and from the right.
explanation: LESSON 19 – ‘Junction and traffic sign’. The priority road bends to the right.

text: You want to enter a roundabout and you see this red triangle. What are you doing?
explanation: LESSON 19 – ‘Junction and traffic sign’.

text: When you see these traffic signs, you know that you …

options.text: ... must stop at the next junction.
... must give priority and stop if necessary …

explanation: LESSON 19 – ‘Junction and traffic sign’. The bottom board says that there is a stop sign at the crossroads.

text: Is the red car allowed to overtake another car on the left at this junction?
explanation: LESSON 19 – ‘Junction and traffic sign’. At an intersection where the priority is controlled by this board, you can overtake on the left.

text: At the next junction you are allowed to overtake another car with your car on the left.
explanation: LESSON 19 – ‘Junction and traffic sign’. It's allowed because you drive on a priority road.

text: Who is the first to cross the intersection?
explanation: LESSON 19 – ‘Junction and traffic sign’. The car must give priority to MANAGERS on the intersection.A pedestrian is not a driver, but there is a crossroads for pedestrians.Therefore the pedestrian is allowed to go first.

text: Who is the last one to cross the junction?
explanation: LESSON 20 – ‘Priority form the right’.First: the cyclist because who rides a continuous cycle path.Next: the car, because that comes from the right.Last: the truck, because this gives priority.

text: Who has priority?
explanation: LESSON 20 – ‘Priority form the right’.There is no priority from the right.

text: Who has priority?
explanation: LESSON 20 – ‘Priority form the right’.The bus is coming from the right.

text: In what order are these drivers allowed to cross the junction?
explanation: LESSON 20 – ‘Priority form the right’.The blue car has priority from the right.The moped on the bicycle reserved lane drives straight ahead may go before the brown car.

text: Car A leaves its residence. Who has priority?
explanation: LESSON 20 – ‘Priority form the right’.At the joining of a private ramp with the road, there is no priority from the right.

text: The cyclists have stopped. Who has priority?
explanation: LESSON 20 – ‘Priority form the right’.The cyclists are coming from the right.

text: Who is allowed to cross first at the junction?
explanation: LESSON 20 – ‘Priority form the right’.The agent gives the order that the moped has to stop.

text: Who has priority?
explanation: LESSON 20 – ‘Priority form the right’.A crossroad without traffic signs.The cyclist is coming from the right.

text: Does the priority on the right apply to this intersection?
explanation: LESSON 20

text: The black car stopped before the intersection for safety reasons. Which car may enter the intersection first?

options.text: The gray car, because the black one stopped.
The black car, because it comes from the right.

explanation: LESSON 20At an intersection where priority is not regulated by an authorized person, traffic lights, or signs, the rule of priority to the right applies.Even if the driver coming from the right stops first, they still keep their right of way.

text: Who has priority?
explanation: LESSON 20 – ‘Priority form the right’.A tram always has priority.

text: The red car wants to leave the parking space. Who has priority?

options.text: The red car coming from the right.

explanation: LESSON 20A driver who leaves a parking space must give way to all road users on the public road,including pedestrians.

text: Who has priority?
explanation: LESSON 20 – ‘Priority form the right’. There is no priority from the right because the moped rides on a path.

text: Who has priority?
explanation: LESSON 20 – ‘Priority form the right’.It is a roundabout. Here is no priority from the right.

text: Who has priority?

options.text: The car on the dirt track.

explanation: LESSON 20 – ‘Priority form the right’. A car that runs on a dirt road, should give priority.

text: Who has priority?
explanation: LESSON 20 – ‘Priority form the right’.The brown car is coming from the right.

text: A lane closure. Who has priority?
explanation: LESSON 20 – ‘Priority form the right’.Car B comes from the right.(Court of Cassation Rulings)

text: Who has priority?
explanation: LESSON 20 – ‘Priority form the right’.The red car is coming from the right.

text: Do you have always priority at this junction?
explanation: LESSON 20 – ‘Priority form the right’.Each driver who comes from the right should have priority, even if he first stopped.

text: Is the red car (= red arrow) allowed to overtake the yellow (= yellow arrow) on the left at this junction?
explanation: LESSON 20 – ‘Priority form the right’. It’s forbidden to overtake on the left animals in harness, a vehicle with more than 2 wheels and a two-wheeled motor vehicle on intersections where the priority from the right applies.

text: Who is the first to cross the junction?
explanation: LESSON 20 – ‘Priority form the right’.When a driver comes out of a prohibitive direction, you don’t have to give right of way.

text: Is the driver of the car at this junction allowed to overtake the moped on the left?

options.text: Yes, when there is 1 meter space between them.

explanation: LESSON 20 – ‘Priority form the right’. It’s forbidden to overtake on the left animals in harness, a vehicle with more than 2 wheels and a two-wheeled motor vehicle on intersections where the priority from the right applies.

text: Who has priority?
explanation: LESSON 20 – ‘Priority form the right’.The sign says that car B should give priority and if necessary has to stop.

text: In what order are the cars allowed to cross the junction?
explanation: LESSON 20 – ‘Priority form the right’.Priority from the right.

text: Who has priority?
explanation: LESSON 20 – ‘Priority form the right’.The tram doesn’t have to give priority.

text: Who has priority?
explanation: LESSON 20 – ‘Priority form the right’.The bus is coming from the right.

text: Who has priority?
explanation: LESSON 20 – ‘Priority form the right’. At this junction the priority of the right applies.But there is a crosswalk for pedestrians.(Learn very well in your book when re is not priority from the right.)

text: Who is the last one to cross the junction?
explanation: LESSON 20 – ‘Priority form the right’. 1. Pedestrian – 2. The green car – 3. The blue car.

text: At this intersection the priority from the right applies.
explanation: LESSON 20 – ‘Priority form the right’.No priority from the right. There is a sign that regulates the priority.

text: Who has priority?
explanation: LESSON 20 – ‘Priority form the right’. Priority from the right. The car is coming from the right.

text: At this junction the right of way applies.
explanation: LESSON 20 – ‘Priority form the right’. Yes, because there are no road signs about the priority.

text: Who has priority at this junction?
explanation: LESSON 20 – ‘Priority form the right’. A crossroad without traffic signs.The cyclist is coming from the right.

text: Who has priority?
explanation: LESSON 20 – ‘Priority form the right’. A tram always comes first.

text: A lane closure. Who has priority?
explanation: LESSON 20 – ‘Priority form the right’.The brown car goes straight on.

text: Who has priority?
explanation: LESSON 20 – ‘Priority form the right’.Car 2 is coming from the right.

text: You are approaching this intersection with your car. Can you catch a two-wheeled motorcycle or moped at the crossroads on the left?

options.text: Yes, if no drivers come from the right.

explanation: LESSON 20 – ‘Priority form the right’. It’s forbidden to overtake on the left animals in harness, a vehicle with more than 2 wheels and a two-wheeled motor vehicle on intersections where the priority from the right applies.

text: Due to work, the blue car cannot turn to the right. Should he give priority to the green car?
explanation: LESSON 20 – ‘Priority form the right’.The green car does not come from a prohibited driving direction.

text: Who has priority?
explanation: LESSON 20 – ‘Priority form the right’. At this junction the priority of the right applies.There is not a crosswalk for pedestrians.

text: Who has priority?
explanation: LESSON 20 – ‘Priority form the right’.The green car is coming from the right.

text: Who has priority?

options.text: The skater who moves at walking pace.

explanation: LESSON 20 – ‘Priority form the right’.There is no ongoing cycle path.

text: Who has priority?
explanation: LESSON 20 – ‘Priority form the right’.Priority from the right. The car is coming from the right.

text: What do you know when you see this traffic sign?

options.text: The indicated road is forbidden for cyclists.
By following this road, cyclists may use the carriageway in both directions.
It warns drivers who are changing direction that cyclists and riders of two-wheeled mopeds are using the same public road.

explanation: LESSON 21This traffic sign (F50bis) warns drivers who are changing direction that cyclists and riders of two-wheeled mopeds are using the same public road.When changing direction, you must give way to these road users.On this sign, sometimes only the cyclist symbol or only a pedestrian crossing symbol may be shown.

text: Who has priority?
explanation: LESSON 21 – ‘Priority and changing directions’.The driver of the white car who wants to drive straight on has priority.The driver who wants to turn left, has to give priority.

text: In what order are these drivers allowed to cross the junction?
explanation: LESSON 21 – ‘Priority and changing directions’.Priority from the right.The blue car is coming from the right of the brown car and the brown car drives right of the moto.

text: Who has priority?
explanation: LESSON 21 – ‘Priority and changing directions’.The blue and red car have to stop for the stop line.The gray car drives straight ahead and has priority of the green car who wants to turn down.

text: Who is allowed to cross first at the junction?
explanation: LESSON 21 – ‘Priority and changing directions’.The agent gives the order that the blue car has to stop.The driver who wants to drive straight on has priority.The driver who wants to turn left, has to give priority.

text: In what order are these drivers allowed to cross the junction?
explanation: LESSON 21 – ‘Priority and changing directions’.The blue and Brown car have green light.The driver who wants to drive straight on has priority.The driver who wants to turn left, has to give priority. The moto must wait until the traffic light turns green.

text: When you carry out a manoeuvre, to whom must you give priority?
explanation: LESSON 21A manoeuvre is an action you perform with your vehicle that is not specifically regulated by the traffic rules (for example, reversing).When you carry out a manoeuvre, you must:- observe very carefully first,- give priority to all road users (both drivers and pedestrians).

text: In what order are these drivers allowed to cross the junction?
explanation: LESSON 21 – ‘Priority and changing directions’.The moto rides a priority road and may drive first.The driver who wants to drive straight on has priority.The driver who wants to turn left, has to give priority.

text: In what order are these drivers allowed to cross the junction?
explanation: LESSON 21 – ‘Priority and changing directions’.The blue car and the motorcycle are riding on a priority road.The blue car want to turn right or makes the short corner and has priority of the motorcycle which makes a long turn.As soon as the intersection is free, the brown car continue.

text: You are driving on a one-way road with three lanes and you want to turn left. Where should you position yourself correctly?
explanation: LESSON 21When you want to turn left, you must position yourself as far to the left as possible on the roadway.

text: How should you position your wheels when you are stopped at an intersection?

options.text: With the wheels turned in the direction you want to turn.
With the wheels pointing straight ahead.

explanation: LESSON 21When you stop at an intersection and intend to turn right, you must keep your wheels straight until you actually begin to turn. This prevents your vehicle from being pushed directly into the side street in case of an unexpected impact, which could create a dangerous situation or force you to give way to oncoming traffic. You only turn when it is safe to do so, taking into account other road users and pedestrians.

text: An intersection without traffic signs. The white car wants to turn left. The grey car wants to turn right. Who has the right of way?

options.text: Whoever turns first automatically has the right of way.

explanation: LESSON 21The grey car is turning right and taking the shorter turn. It has the right of way.

text: Who has priority?
explanation: LESSON 21 – ‘Priority and changing directions’.The red car who wants to turn right or makes the shortest turn, has priority.The white car who wants to turn left, or makes the longest turn, has to give priority.

text: When there is a problem of the 'dead angle’?

options.text: Only if the mirrors are incorrectly adjusted.

explanation: LESSON 21 – ‘Priority and changing directions’.Mirrors must be always correctly adjusted before you drive.But there is always a point that you can't see in the mirrors: the dead angle.

text: Who is allowed to cross first at the junction?
explanation: LESSON 21 – ‘Priority and changing directions’.The agent gives the order that the brown car and the moto need to stop.

text: In which direction should a car's wheels be turned if the driver wants to turn left, but the intersection is not yet clear?
explanation: If you already turn your wheels to the left and someone hits you from behind, your car may be pushed into the intersection and crash into oncoming vehicles. That’s why your wheels should remain straight until it’s safe to turn.

text: At an intersection you want to turn left. What do you do?

options.text: Slow down – Look in the mirror – Turn direction indicator.
Turn direction indicator – Look in the mirror – Slow down.
Look in the mirror – Turn direction indicator – Slow down.

explanation: LESSON 21 – ‘Priority and changing directions’.See if a car is coming behind you that you for example catches up. Turn Direction indicator on. Slowing down and turn.

text: Who is allowed to cross first at the junction?
explanation: LESSON 21 – ‘Priority and changing directions’.The driver who wants to drive straight on has priority.The driver who wants to turn left, has to give priority.

text: Who has priority at this intersection?
explanation: LESSON 21The general rule is that traffic going straight ahead has priority over turning traffic.However, this rule does not apply when the straight-ahead vehicle is coming from a dirt road.A driver coming from a dirt road must give way to traffic on the paved road, even when driving straight ahead.

text: The driver of the blue car wants to turn right.

options.text: He takes the first right-hand lane (1).
He takes the second right-hand lane (2).
He can choose between the first or second lane.

explanation: LESSON 21 – ‘Priority and changing directions’.In a build-up area, he can choose the lane he wants to drive on.

text: The white car wants to reverse into a parking space. What is correct?

options.text: The driver must give way to all road users.
The driver must give way to all drivers.
Approaching drivers must stop and give way to the white car.

explanation: LESSON 21Manoeuvres include:• changing lanes;• crossing the carriageway;• entering a parking space;• leaving a parking space;• leaving a property;• turning around in a street;• reversing.When carrying out a manoeuvre, you must:• do so with great care;• not endanger any other road users (including pedestrians);• give way to all road users.

text: An intersection without traffic signs. The white car wants to go straight ahead. The grey car wants to turn left. Who has priority?
explanation: LESSON 21Traffic going straight has priority over traffic that is turning.

text: This photo is taken from the car you are driving. Who has priority?

options.text: The blue car leaving the private driveway of a house.

explanation: LESSON 20The priority to the right rule does not apply when a private driveway joins a public road.The driver who leaves a private driveway must stop and give way to all road users on the public road (including pedestrians).That driver is carrying out a manoeuvre.

text: In what order are these drivers allowed to cross the junction?
explanation: LESSON 21 – ‘Priority and changing directions’.The sign next to the moto says he has priority.Next the blue car, because that will drive straight ahead.

text: You approach this junction and you want to cross it. The oncoming car wants to turn left. Do you have to give priority?
explanation: LESSON 21 – ‘Priority and changing directions’.If the traffic lights work, the board under the lights has no meaning.The traffic light is green, so you're allowed to drive straight through. Your oncoming vehicle (if it also has green light), wants to turn left and must want to give priority.

text: A two-way road. The driver of the white car wants to turn left. He positions himself on the left-hand side of the road. Is he acting correctly?

options.text: Yes, this allows following vehicles to pass him on the right.

explanation: LESSON 21The road on which the white car is driving is not a one-way street.- When turning left, the driver positions himself as close as possible to the centre line of the road.- When turning right, he must position himself as far to the right as possible on the road.➡️ On a one-way street, a driver who wants to turn left must position himself on the far left side.

text: An intersection with traffic signs. In what situation the pedestrian has priority?
explanation: LESSON 21 – ‘Priority and changing directions’.A car that changes direction, should give priority to pedestrians who cross the road where the car wants to go.

text: Must you use the left indicator when you're already properly positioned to turn left?

options.text: Yes, always, and turn it off as soon as the manoeuvre is completed.
No, because you're already well positioned.

explanation: LESSON 21 A turn signal is there to indicate your intentions, even if you are already in the right position.

text: Who is allowed to cross first at the junction?
explanation: LESSON 21 – ‘Priority and changing directions’.The agent gives the order that only the moto may drive.

text: Who has priority?
explanation: LESSON 21 – ‘Priority and changing directions’.The driver who wants to drive straight on has priority.The driver who wants to turn left, has to give priority.

text: Who is allowed to cross first at the junction?
explanation: LESSON 21 – ‘Priority and changing directions’.The agent gives the order that the motor has to stop.The driver who wants to drive straight on has priority.The driver who wants to turn left, has to give priority.

text: You approach this junction and you want to cross it. The oncoming car wants to turn left. Do you have to give it priority?
explanation: LESSON 21 – ‘Priority and changing directions’.If the traffic lights work, the board under the lights has no meaning.The traffic light is green, so you're allowed to drive straight through. Your oncoming vehicle (if it also has green light), wants to turn left and must want to give priority.

text: A crossroad without traffic signs. In what situation the pedestrian has priority?
explanation: LESSON 21 – ‘Priority and changing directions’.A car that changes direction, should give priority to pedestrians who cross the road where the car wants to go.

text: You are not allowed to park on the road in front or past the sign of a bus stop within (…) meters.
Where do you have to drive 50kph?

options.text: As soon as you pass these signs.

text: Who has priority?
In what order are these drivers allowed to cross the junction?
Fill in a number: The police allow you to drive on a special reserved route. Which traffic signal has the same meaning as a red light?
explanation: LESSON 18 + 22On a special overrun lane, the signals mean:1️⃣ An inverted triangle → same meaning as a green light.2️⃣ A circle → same meaning as a steady amber light.3️⃣ A horizontal bar → same meaning as a red light.4️⃣ A diagonal bar to the left → permission to drive only in that direction.

text: Which of these signs indicates a bus lane?
Are mopeds here also allowed on the special tram or bus routes?
Which traffic sign indicates this level crossing?
Are you allowed to turn around on a checkerboard marker at an intersection?
explanation: LESSON 22

text: The picture is taken from the car you drive in. You want to refuel. Are you allowed to use the bus reserved route to the right of you from here on?
Is this driver allowed to drive on the bus stop?
This driver wants to turn right at the junction.

options.text: The car must be on this lane.
The car is allowed on the lane to the right of him.

text: A level crossing with barriers and lights. But the lights are out. Are you allowed to overtake a vehicle on the left?
explanation: The lights are not working but there are open barriers.

text: Standing still to let someone get out, is allowed on a bus stop.
The train is gone and the barriers are going up. If you leave now with your car …

options.text: ... it is not a real offence.
... your driving licence can be suspended immediately.

text: What kind of traffic sign is this?
The driver of this bus has switched on the left indicator and wants to leave the bus stop, outside a built-up area. Must you give way?
explanation: LESSON 22 – Explanation:Within a built-up area, you must give way to a bus leaving a bus stop when its indicator is on.⚠️ This rule does not apply to:• coaches,• buses used for school transport or employee transport.

text: Is the blue car allowed to drive on the bus lane to park on the verge?
The bus wants to leave the bus stop in a built up area.
What must a tram driver take into account? 1. The orders of an authorized person. 2. The traffic lights. 3. The priority rules.
Within a built up area. A tourist bus has stopped at a bus stop to let out some pensioners. The driver wants to leave the bus stop and switches on his direction indicator.

options.text: You don’t have to give priority.

explanation: Not, because it is a tourist bus.

text: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Level crossing with barriers and lights.

text: You are allowed to drive on the bus lane, to pass or overtake safely.
What does this sign mean?
You drive past this sign. Are you allowed to overtake a motorcycle on the right here?
explanation: The sign is placed 150 meters before the level crossing. You are driving on a regular roadway here.

text: Is the blue car allowed to drive on the bus reserved route next to him to park on the verge?
Are you allowed to overtake a moped to the left at this level crossing?
explanation: Yes, because there is a light.

text: You approach this bus stop by car and you see that the bus has its hazard warning lights on. Do you have to slow down and give way?
explanation: LESSON 22 You must give way when a bus wants to leave a bus stop in a built-up area.In that case, the left indicator must be flashing, not the hazard warning lights.When the hazard warning lights are on, this simply means that the bus is stopped to allow passengers to get on or off.

text: On the bus lane you are not allowed to drive.
Being stationary to pick up or drop off people is allowed...

options.text: … only at a bus stop and on a bus lane.
… at a bus stop, on a bus lane, and on a special reserved route.

explanation: LESSON 22You are only allowed to stop at a bus stop to let someone get in or out of the vehicle.

text: Is the blue car allowed to drive on the lane to the right of him to change direction?
Is it true that your driving licence can be suspended immediately when you drive past the red flashing lights on a level crossing?
The red car didn’t give priority to this leaving bus (public transport). He must do it …

options.text: ... only within a built up area.
... only outside a built up area.

text: The bell is not ringing. When are you allowed to overtake a vehicle on this level crossing?

options.text: Only if the barrier is open AND the white lunar light is lit at the same time.
If the barrier is open and the white lunar light is not lit, because it is defective.

explanation: LESSON 22You may overtake a vehicle on the left at a level crossing when the barrier is fully open and the white lunar light is shining at the same time.But if the bell is not ringing, the barrier is open, but the lights are defective, you may also overtake a vehicle on the left.

text: What is this road marking called?
You hear the warning bell sound, but the barriers are still completely open.

options.text: You are allowed to drive through.

text: This danger sign means: one or more tram tracks crossing the public road. Must the tram driver take the traffic lights into account?
Outside a built-up area, must you give way to a bus leaving a bus stop?
explanation: LESSON 22You must give way inside a built-up area. You must never give way to a coach leaving a bus stop.

text: The red light is already on, but the barrier is still open. Are you allowed to drive further?
explanation: Red light and bell sound means stop, even if the barrier is still open.

text: Are you allowed to cross this bus lane with a car in order to enter your property?
You drive your car on the right lane of this motorway. What is the maximum speed limit?
Fill in a number: The police allow you to drive on a special reserved route. Which traffic signal has the same meaning as a green light?
explanation: LESSON 18 + 22On a special overrun lane, the signals mean:1️⃣ An inverted triangle → same meaning as a green light.2️⃣ A circle → same meaning as a steady amber light.3️⃣ A horizontal bar → same meaning as a red light.4️⃣ A diagonal bar to the left → permission to drive only in that direction.

text: Are you allowed to wait a while for your friend, with your car on the bus stop?
What do you do when a bus stops at this stop?

options.text: Stop and wait until the bus leaves again.

explanation: You don't have to stop, but you can drive on carefully.

text: Is the blue car allowed to drive on the bus reserved route to the right of him to change direction, the last meters before the junction?
*** 5 points question *** Can you overtake a moped on the left at this level crossing?

options.text: No, overtaking on the left is forbidden,

explanation: LESSON 22 - 'Train, tram, bus'.There are barriers and the white light is on.

text: This picture is taken from the car you drive in. You want to turn right at the junction.

options.text: You are allowed to drive on the bus lane when you intend to change direction at the next junction.
You have to use this lane to change direction.

text: What does this traffic sign indicate?

options.text: Level crossing with two or more tracks.

text: The tram comes from the left. Should the car give way?
explanation: LESSON 22 - 'Train Tram Bus'.A tram always has right of way.

text: What does this sign mean?
This sign applies …
explanation: LESSON 23 – ‘Prohibited direction’.No entry to vehicles or combination of vehicles which load included, exceed the length shown.(See in your book also lesson 10).

text: Which vehicles can drive past this board?

options.text: Bicycles, mopeds class A and pedelecs.

explanation: LESSON 23 – ‘Prohibited direction’.If the letter P is mentioned, it also applies to pedelcs.If the letters P and A are mentioned, it also applies to pedelecs and mopeds class A.

text: Is a cyclist allowed to ride past this sign?
explanation: LESSON 23 – ‘Prohibited direction’.This sign means: no entry in both directions to any driver.

text: Is the brown car allowed to come out of the street?
explanation: LESSON 23 – ‘Prohibited direction’.This prohibitive sign indicates no entry past this sign to drivers of all vehicles having more than two wheels or motorcycles with a side car.However they are allowed to drive in the opposite direction.

text: Are you allowed to come out of this street with a car?
explanation: LESSON 23 – ‘Prohibited direction’.This prohibitive sign indicates no entry to any driver (including cyclists) to drive past this sign in this direction.

text: You are not allowed to drive past this sign with a car. But are you allowed to come out of this street with your car?
explanation: LESSON 23 – ‘Prohibited direction’.This prohibitive sign indicates no entry past this sign to drivers of all vehicles having more than two wheels or motorcycles with a side car.

text: Which vehicles can drive past this board?

options.text: Bicycles, mopeds class A and pedelecs.

explanation: LESSON 23 – ‘Prohibited direction’.If the letter P is mentioned, it also applies to pedelcs.If the letters P and A are mentioned, it also applies to pedelecs and mopeds class A.

text: Are you allowed to drive past this sign with a car?
explanation: LESSON 23 – ‘Prohibited direction’.A regular passenger car has a M.A.W. up to 3.5 tons.

text: Are you allowed to drive past these signs with a car?
explanation: LESSON 23 – ‘Prohibited direction’.This prohibitive sign indicates no entry to any driver (including cyclists) to drive past this sign in this direction.

text: This sign indicates …
explanation: LESSON 23 – ‘Prohibited direction’.Tip exam: learn very well in your book (chapter 9) the difference between M.A.W. and M.G.W.

text: Are you allowed to drive past this sign with a car?
explanation: LESSON 23 – ‘Prohibited direction’.This positive instruction sign means: no through road.

text: You approach this junction with your car.

options.text: You are allowed to turn right.
You are allowed to cross the junction.

explanation: LESSON 23 – ‘Prohibited direction’.This prohibitive sign indicates no entry to any driver (including cyclists) to drive past this sign in this direction.

text: The driver of this car is allowed …
explanation: LESSON 23 – ‘Prohibited direction’.This sign indicates that turning to the left is prohibited at the next junction to all drivers.

text: Is oncoming traffic from the other direction possible?
explanation: LESSON 23 – ‘Prohibited direction’.This prohibitive sign indicates no entry to any driver (including cyclists) to drive past this sign in this direction.

text: Roadworks. Your friend lives on this street. Can you drive to his house?
explanation: LESSON 22 - 'Prohibited Direction'.You may because you are local traffic.

text: You are not allowed to drive past these signs with a car. But are you allowed to come out of the street with a car?
explanation: LESSON 23 – ‘Prohibited direction’.This sign means: no entry in both directions to any driver.

text: Once you are past this traffic sign you are allowed to make a U-turn again.
explanation: LESSON 23 – ‘Prohibited direction’.This sign indicates that form this sign on until the next junction (also there) a U turn is prohibited.

text: If you see this underplate, it also applies to speed pedelecs.
explanation: LESSON 23 – ‘Prohibited direction’.Speed Pedelecs are mopeds

text: When are you allowed to drive across an exclusion area?

options.text: In order to reach your property.
In order to reach your property or to turn at a junction.

explanation: LESSON 23 – ‘Prohibited direction’.This is a traffic displacement area (see rule in your book chapter 2).

text: Who is allowed to ride out of this street?
explanation: LESSON 23 – ‘Prohibited direction’.This sign prohibits drivers of motor vehicles with more than two wheels and all motorcycles to drive past this sign.However they are allowed to drive in the opposite direction.

text: The bakery is on this street. Can you drive your car on this street?
Are you allowed to drive past this sign with a car?
explanation: LESSON 23 – ‘Prohibited direction’.Yes, because a passenger car with which a driver who has a driving licence B may drive, is a car with a M.A.W. up to 3.5 tons.The M.G.W. can therefore never exceed 3.5 tons.

text: What does this traffic sign indicate?

options.text: No entry for drivers of motor vehicles with four wheels and quads.
No entry for drivers of quads.
No entry for drivers of quads and motorcyclists.

explanation: LESSON 23 – ‘Prohibited direction’.No entry for drivers of quads.

text: This road is a short cut to your workplace. Are you allowed to drive on?
explanation: LESSON 23 – ‘Prohibited direction’.This sign means: no entry in both directions to any driver.

text: You’re without gas and your garage is at the beginning of the street on the right. Are you allowed to push your car to the right?

options.text: No, because you are still a driver.
Yes, because then you are a pedestrian.

explanation: LESSON 23 – ‘Prohibited direction’.If you push your car, you are still a driver.This sign indicates that turning to the right lane is prohibited at the next junction to all drivers.

text: Are you allowed to drive past this sign with a car?
explanation: LESSON 23 – ‘Prohibited direction’.This prohibitive sign indicates no entry to any driver, with the exception of cyclists, pedelecs and mopeds class A to drive past this sign in this direction.

text: Can you drive a car past the first sign?
explanation: LESSON 23 – ‘Prohibited direction’.The blue bottom sign indicates that 50 meters further, it is forbidden to continue driving in this direction.

text: Are you allowed to drive past these signs to visit a relative who lives in this street?
explanation: LESSON 23 – ‘Prohibited direction’.Yes, because the blue plate says "except local traffic".

text: What does this sign indicate?
explanation: LESSON 23 – ‘Prohibited direction’.Tip exam: learn very well in your book (chapter 9) the difference between M.A.W. and M.G.W.

text: Is the driver of car A allowed to turn right at the junction?
explanation: LESSON 23 – ‘Prohibited direction’.This sign indicates that turning to the right is prohibited at the next junction to all drivers.

text: What is the maximum speed limit for a car passing these signs?

options.text: A car isn’t allowed to drive past these signs.

explanation: LESSON 23 – ‘Prohibited direction’.Up to 50 km/hour.

text: You see one of these signs. At which sign can cars come from the other direction of travel?
explanation: LESSON 23 – ‘Prohibited direction’.Sign 3: both directions.

text: Are you allowed to drive past this sign?
explanation: LESSON 23 – ‘Prohibited direction’.Tip exam: learn very well in your book (chapter 9) the difference between M.A.W. and M.G.W.

text: Is the blue car allowed to cross the junction?
explanation: LESSON 23 – ‘Prohibited direction’.This sign means: no entry in this direction to drivers of motorcycles.

text: Is the blue car allowed to turn right?
explanation: LESSON 23 – ‘Prohibited direction’.This prohibitive sign indicates no entry to any driver (including cyclists) to drive past this sign in this direction.

text: What does this traffic sign mean?

options.text: From here until the next junction no U-turn.

explanation: LESSON 23 – ‘Prohibited direction’.This sign indicates that form this sign on until the next junction (also there) a U turn is prohibited.

text: You’re out of gas. Which vehicle are you allowed to push into the street on the right to refuel?

options.text: A two-wheeled moped or a motorcycle.

explanation: LESSON 23 – ‘Prohibited direction’.Someone who pushes a moped is a pedestrian.Someone who pushes a motorcycle is a driver.

text: Are you allowed to drive past this sign to park your car?
explanation: LESSON 23 – ‘Prohibited direction’.This prohibitive sign indicates no entry to any driver (including cyclists) to drive past this sign in this direction.

text: Is the red car allowed to turn right?
explanation: LESSON 24 – ‘Obligatory direction’. There is no sign that it is forbidden.

text: There is no roundabout. Are you allowed to drive with a car in the direction of the arrow past the obstacle?
explanation: LESSON 24 – ‘Obligatory direction’. No, you have to pass the obstacle right.

text: In the middle of the picture you see a roundabout.
explanation: LESSON 24 – ‘Obligatory direction’. There is no sign indicating that it is a roundabout.It is a traffic guide.

text: Which vehicles can come from the other direction?
explanation: LESSON 24 – ‘Obligatory direction’.If the letter P is mentioned, it also applies to pedelcs.If the letters P and A are mentioned, it also applies to pedelecs and mopeds class A.

text: In what direction must you drive your car?
explanation: LESSON 24 – ‘Obligatory direction’. The arrow indicates that you have to drive to the right.

text: Is the blue car allowed to turn left at this junction?
explanation: LESSON 24 – ‘Obligatory direction’. The blue sign says it's a one-way street.

text: If you see this under plate, it also applies to speed pedelecs.
explanation: LESSON 24 – ‘Obligatory direction’.It also applies to pedelecs (P) but not to mopeds class A.

text: This car can only turn to the right. Does the driver have to turn on the turn signal?
explanation: LESSON 24 – ‘Obligatory direction’. The blue sign says the driver must turn to the right.

text: The driver of the brown car is allowed to …
explanation: LESSON 24 – ‘Obligatory direction’. The driver may turn to both directions.

text: You must turn left at an intersection. How should you take the turn?
explanation: LESSON 24- When turning left, you take the turn as wide as possible.- When turning right, you take the turn as short as possible.This prevents you from entering the part of the carriageway intended for traffic coming from the opposite direction.

text: The blue car …

options.text: ... is allowed to turn left or drive straight through.

explanation: LESSON 24 – ‘Obligatory direction’. The sign next to the car says that the driver must drive straight through.

text: Do these signs have the same meaning?
explanation: LESSON 24 – ‘Obligatory direction’.They have the same meaning.

text: This picture is taken from the car you drive in.

options.text: You are only allowed to turn left.
You are only allowed to turn right.
You are allowed to turn left or right.

explanation: LESSON 24 – ‘Obligatory direction’. You may drive in both directions.

text: Which of these signs is an information sign?
explanation: LESSON 24 – ‘Obligatory direction’. Sign 1: road with one-way traffic.Sign 2: required to follow direction of travel.

text: Must you (the blue car) also give priority to the right, when you drive on a one-way street?
explanation: LESSON 24 – ‘Obligatory direction’. If you're driving on a one-way road, you should also grant priority, except of course when there is a traffic sign indicating you have priority.In this example, the brown car may drive first.

text: Is the driver of the grey car allowed to cross these road markings to reach his apartment?
explanation: LESSON 24 – ‘Obligatory direction’. You may not drive on a traffic displacement area.

text: Who has priority?
explanation: LESSON 24 – ‘Obligatory direction’. The brown car has priority from the right.

text: What is the driver of the blue car not allowed to do?
explanation: LESSON 24 – ‘Obligatory direction’. The blue sign says he must go straight ahead or turn to the left.

text: Is the brown car allowed to turn left?
explanation: LESSON 24 – ‘Obligatory direction’. The brown car may turn to the right or to the left or straight on.

text: Is the driver of the blue car allowed to drive straight on?
explanation: LESSON 24 – ‘Obligatory direction’. The red sign says that it is forbidden to drive past the sign in that direction.

explanation: LESSON 241 = Danger sign: succession of dangerous bends.2 = Prohibition sign: no right turn.3 = Danger sign: traffic allowed in both directions after a section of the road with one-way traffic.

text: You are allowed to pass this bollard to the left or to the right?
explanation: LESSON 24 – ‘Obligatory direction’. The board indicates that you should drive along the left or along the right.

text: Which sign indicates a one way street?
explanation: LESSON 24 – ‘Obligatory direction’. Sign 1: Road with one-way traffic.Sign 2. Driver has to follow that direction of travel.

explanation: LESSON 24 – ‘Obligatory direction’.If the letter P is mentioned, it also applies to pedelcs.If the letters P and A are mentioned, it also applies to pedelecs and mopeds class A.

text: This white underside applies to:

options.text: Bicycles, mopeds class A and pedelecs.

explanation: LESSON 24 – ‘Obligatory direction’.If the letter P is mentioned, it also applies to pedelcs.If the letters P and A are mentioned, it also applies to pedelecs and mopeds class A.

text: Beyond which board a car is allowed to turn right?
explanation: LESSON 24 – ‘Obligatory direction’. On a road with one-way traffic you will not see oncoming traffic, except as a charger plate it indicates.

options.text: ... just to the right or straight ahead.
... to the left or right or straight ahead.

explanation: LESSON 24 – ‘Obligatory direction’. He may not turn to the left.

explanation: LESSON 24 – ‘Obligatory direction’. The blue car has priority from the right.

text: The driver of this car has stopped at a house to ask for directions.
explanation: LESSON 25 – ‘Waiting and parking’.Parking: if you stop for a longer time than strictly necessary to allow passengers in or out or to load or unload goods, than in terms of traffic regulations this is a vehicle that is parked.

text: This sign is 1.20 meter high. Your car is lower than 1.65 meter. You are not allowed to park or wait within (...) meters in front of this sign.
explanation: LESSON 25 – ‘Waiting and parking’.Up to 20 meters.

text: Where are you allowed to park on the levelled verge?

options.text: Only within a built up area.
Only outside a built up area.
Within or outside a built up area.

explanation: LESSON 25 – ‘Waiting and parking’.This can be done inside and outside the built-up area.

text: There has been an accident in the other direction. Are you allowed to stop on the hard shoulder to provide assistance.
explanation: LESSON 25 – ‘Waiting and parking’.No, because you should cross the lane and the bark on foot, which is forbidden.

text: There is traffic jam. The car in front of you just drove over a speed hump and stops again. Can you stop on the speed hump.
explanation: LESSON 25 – ‘Waiting and parking’.Just stop in a file because you cannot drive further, is not waiting or parking.Only waiting and parking are prohibited on a speed hump.

text: A carriageway that is not divided into traffic lanes. The driver of the white car is waiting under this bridge for a colleague who will join the ride. Is this allowed?
explanation: LESSON 25On the carriageway, it is forbidden to stop or to park under a bridge.This rule applies at all times, whether or not the carriageway is divided into traffic lanes.

text: On a reserved cycle lane you are …

options.text: not allowed to wait or park.

explanation: LESSON 25 – ‘Waiting and parking’.It is not only allowed, it must.

text: A junction with traffic lights. You are not allowed to wait or park on the road or on the verge within (…) meters in front of the traffic lights.
explanation: LESSON 25 – ‘Waiting and parking’.You are not allowed to wait or to park on the road and on the verge at a junction with traffic lights within 20 meters of the traffic lights.

text: The lane next to the solid white line is meant to park or wait. Are you allowed to use this lane to pass or overtake a car on the right more easily?
explanation: LESSON 25 – ‘Waiting and parking’.Some roads have a white solid line painted at the right of that lane. You are only allowed to park or wait next to it.

text: The black car is stopped and prevents the tram from continuing. When must the driver react?

options.text: As soon as the tram gives an audible warning.

explanation: LESSON 25You are not allowed to stop or park if you obstruct a tram.➡️ The driver must react immediately, even if the tram does not sound its bell.

text: A roadway without road markings within a built-up area. Is this car correctly parked?
explanation: LESSON 25On a one-way street, vehicles may park on both the left and the right side of the roadway.However, this car is incorrectly parked, because it is facing the wrong direction of traffic.

options.text: ... is not allowed to be lit.

explanation: LESSON 25 – ‘Waiting and parking’.It is not mandatory because the battery of the car can get empty

options.text: Yes, if there is no verge.

explanation: LESSON 25It is forbidden to stop or park on the roadway under a bridge.

options.text: Only on the ground level verge.
On a ground level or elevated verge.

explanation: LESSON 25 – ‘Waiting and parking’.Outside a built up area: on a ground level or elevated verge.

options.text: He doesn’t have to wear a seat belt.
He must wear a seat belt.

explanation: LESSON 25 – ‘Waiting and parking’.During reversing you don’t have to wear a belt.

text: You are not allowed to park within (…) meters in front of this pedestrian crossing?
explanation: LESSON 25 – ‘Waiting and parking’.Parking is prohibited until 20 meters from traffic lights at a crossroads.

text: You are not allowed to park or wait within (…) meters in front of the junction.
explanation: LESSON 25 – ‘Waiting and parking’.Up to 5 meters.

text: Are you allowed to wait on the cycle lane to let someone in or out of the car?
explanation: LESSON 25 – ‘Waiting and parking’.The bicycle lane is not part of the roadway.You may not ride, wait or park on a bicycle lane.

options.text: Yes, when he doesn’t hinder other drivers.

explanation: LESSON 25 – ‘Waiting and parking’.Waiting and parking are prohibited until 20 meters from a traffic light at a crossroads.

text: May a driver hold his mobile phone to read a message while passengers are getting into the car?
explanation: LESSON 25You may use the device without a holder only if your vehicle is stationary or correctly parked.The term “stationary” must be interpreted as defined in the Belgian Road Code:“remaining stationary only for the time strictly necessary to allow passengers to get in or out of the vehicle, or to load or unload the vehicle.”Briefly stopping at a traffic light, for example, is not considered ‘being stationary’ within the meaning of the Road Code.

text: What is the blue car allowed to do here?
explanation: LESSON 25 – ‘Waiting and parking’.On a road with one-way traffic you can wait and park on both sides.

text: Traffic is moving very slowly and keeps stopping. If traffic comes to a halt again, are you allowed to stop on an elevated section?

options.text: No, you must stop before the elevated section.

explanation: LESSON 25You are not allowed to stop or park on an elevated section, unless road markings or traffic signs indicate otherwise.This rule is strict.⚠️ However: in a traffic jam, you may stop briefly to follow the flow of traffic.This is not considered illegal stopping, but a stop imposed by traffic conditions.

text: Within (...) meters in front of these traffic signs you are not allowed to park on the road or on the verge.
explanation: LESSON 25 – ‘Waiting and parking’.The traffic sign is less than 2 meters.

On the question mark a car is allowed …

explanation: LESSON 25 – ‘Waiting and parking’.You cannot park because there is a broken white line between the lanes.

text: What are you allowed to do on the left of this road?
explanation: LESSON 25 – ‘Waiting and parking’.On a road with one-way traffic you may wait and park on both sides.

text: The red car is not allowed to park in this bend. Is the driver allowed to wait to let someone out of the car?
explanation: LESSON 25 – ‘Waiting and parking’.You are not allowed to wait or park on the road in or in front of a blind corner.

text: You are not allowed to park or wait on the road within (…) meters in front of a crossing for cyclists or two-wheeled mopeds.
explanation: LESSON 25 – ‘Waiting and parking’.You are not allowed to wait or park on the road within 5 meters of a crossing for pedestrians or cyclists.

text: The cycle lane stops and the cyclists have to ride on the road.

options.text: You are not allowed to park on the road within 5 meters in front of that place.
You are not allowed to park or wait on the road and on the verge within 5 meters in front of that place.
You are not allowed to park or wait on the road and on the verge within 5 meters in front of or past that place.

explanation: LESSON 25 – ‘Waiting and parking’.When the cycle lane stops, up to 5 meters in front of and beyond the place where they come on the roadway.

text: On a speed hump ...

options.text: ... you may not wait and not park

explanation: LESSON 25 – ‘Waiting and parking’.On a speed hump …- ... you may not wait and not park unless a traffic sign allows it.- ... is the maximum speed: 30 km / hour.- ... you may not overtake a vehicle on left (not even a cyclist).

text: Between two parked cars there has to be (…) meters free space.
explanation: LESSON 25 – ‘Waiting and parking’.When you park on the road, you have to leave at least 1 meter free space between two parked cars.

text: What is prohibited under this bridge or a tunnel?

options.text: Park on the road and on the verge.
Wait and park on the road and on the verge.
Wait and park on the road.

explanation: LESSON 25 – ‘Waiting and parking’.You are not allowed to wait or park on the road.

text: On which verge can you park outside a built up area?

options.text: Only on the ground level verge.
On a ground level or elevated verge

explanation: LESSON 25 – ‘Waiting and parking’.Inside a built up area: on the ground level verge.Outside a built up area: on a ground level or elevated verge

text: You are not allowed to park or wait on a cycle lane. Are you allowed to drive on the cycle lane to pass another vehicle more safely?
explanation: LESSON 25 – ‘Waiting and parking’.A bike path is not part of the lane.

text: What are the cars allowed to do on the exclusion area?
explanation: LESSON 25 – ‘Waiting and parking’. The cars should not stand there.

text: The red cars are parked on the roadway. Can the blue car stand still on the road for a passenger to get out?
explanation: LESSON 25 - "Parking".Double parking or standing still is prohibited.

text: What is the safest distance between you and the vehicle in front of you when you stop?

options.text: When you can still see the license plate.
When you can still see the bumper or the exhaust pipe.
When you can still see the rear tyres.

explanation: LESSON 25 – ‘Waiting and parking’.You can still see the rear tyres.

text: This picture is taken within a built up area. Is the black car allowed to park on the ground-level verge?
explanation: LESSON 25 – ‘Waiting and parking’.

text: You are not allowed to park or wait on the lanes of a motorway. But you are allowed on an express way?
explanation: LESSON 25 – ‘Waiting and parking’.It is also not allowed on an express way.

text: You are tired of sitting in the car and you stop for a while on the hard shoulder to stretch your legs. Is this allowed?
explanation: LESSON 25 – ‘Waiting and parking’.You may only stop in the event of a breakdown or an accident.

text: Within a built up area. Is a car allowed to park on that part of the public road marked with the yellow line?
explanation: LESSON 25 – ‘Waiting and parking’.In built-up areas: only on the ground level verge.

text: You are not allowed to park or wait on a pedestrian crossing. But is it allowed on the verge?
explanation: LESSON 25 – ‘Waiting and parking’.ON the crossing for pedestrians and cyclists you are not allowed to wait and park on the road and on the verge.

text: A junction without traffic lights or traffic signs. You are not allowed to park on the road or on the verge within 5 meters of the intersection with the edge of the transverse road. But are you allowed to wait there?
explanation: LESSON 25 – ‘Waiting and parking’.Waiting and parking are prohibited.

text: May the car stop at that place under the bridge to let someone get in?
explanation: LESSON 25On the roadway under a bridge, it is forbidden to stop or park.But on the verge under a bridge, it is allowed to stop and park.

text: A priority road outside a built-up area. May the blue car stop on the roadway to let a passenger get in?
explanation: LESSON 26Inside a built-up area, you may stop on the roadway and also park there if it is not divided into lanes.Outside a built-up area, you may stop on the roadway, but not park.

text: When is the owner of the house allowed to park in front of his garage?

options.text: When the number plate is displayed on the entrance/exit.

text: May this motorcycle also be parked beyond the traffic sign?
explanation: LESSON 26This sign means that parking is allowed for a passenger car, a dual-purpose car, a minibus, and a motorcycle.A light truck is not allowed to park there.

text: When you park your car on the road, you should leave at least (...) meters free.
This car is … here. A, ... allowed to wait or park. B, ... allowed to wait. C, ... not allowed to wait or park.

explanation: LESSON 26When a yellow broken line is painted at the edge of the carriageway, you may only stop.Parking on the carriageway is prohibited.

text: Does the sign that ends all local prohibitions also put an end to parking signs?
explanation: LESSON 26The sign with a black diagonal stripe informs road users of the end of all regulations previously indicated by signs, except those concerning stopping and parking.

options.text: On the carriageway and on the verge.

explanation: LESSON 26The sign prohibits stopping and parking on both the carriageway and the verge.If there are numbers on the sign, the prohibition applies only to the carriageway.

options.text: The first and the second sign.

explanation: LESSON 26This traffic sign means that parking is prohibited on this side of the carriageway from the 1st to the 15th of the month.The additional plate with a downward arrow indicates that the parking prohibition applies up to the sign.

options.text: ... not allowed to wait or park.

explanation: LESSON 26There is a broken white line between the traffic lanes. That means parking is not allowed there.But stopping to let someone get in is allowed.

No parking applies until the next junction …

options.text: ... on the road and on the verge.

options.text: ... not allowed to wait or park.

options.text: ... not allowed to wait or park.

options.text: The first and the second sign.

The blue car is … there.

options.text: not allowed to park or wait.

explanation: LESSON 26This traffic sign means that parking is prohibited on this side of the carriageway and also on the verge.The additional plate with the black downward arrow indicates that the parking prohibition ends at the sign.➡️ However: beyond the sign, the carriageway is divided into two lanes by a broken white line.On such a carriageway, parking is not allowed.➡️ Stopping (for example to allow a passenger to get in or out) is allowed.

text: Within a built-up area. Is the car allowed to park on this priority road?
explanation: LESSON 26Within a built-up area, a car may park on the roadway. Outside a built-up area, a car must park on the shoulder.

text: This sign is above the sign: start of a built-up area. It's March 7th. Where can you park?

options.text: Along the side of the odd house numbers.
Along the side of the even house numbers.

explanation: The sign semi-monthly parking is actually no longer applied. That is why it is no longer on our theory pages. If you still have questions about it, here is the explanation: The half-monthly alternating parking is in effect on all carriageways in a built-up area, when this traffic sign is placed above the traffic signs indicating the start of this built-up area. Parking on the road is then only allowed from the 1st to the 15th of the month, on the side of the buildings with odd numbers and, from the 16th to the end of the month, on the side of the buildings with even numbers.

text: You forget to pull up the hand brake after parking during the practical examination/test.

options.text: The examiner doesn’t pay attention to that.
You have to do the examination again.

text: Is a car also allowed to park in front of this sign?
Are you allowed to wait for a while past this sign until the school bus arrives?
Is the blue car parked according to the regulations?
Past this sign only trailers and caravans are allowed to be parked.
You parked your car in a street and spent the night at your grandparents’ house. The next morning you want to leave, but the street has become a school street. Are you allowed to drive away?

options.text: Yes, but only at walking speed.

explanation: LESSON 6To reduce traffic congestion at the start and end of the school day, a street near a school may be closed twice a day to motor vehicles. When this happens, the street becomes a school street. This is indicated by a C3 (no entry) traffic sign, together with an additional panel stating SCHOOL STREET.Who may enter a school street?– Pedestrians, cyclists, and speed pedelecs.– Residents of the street or drivers who have a garage there (with a permit).– Priority vehicles.– Vehicles with a special permit.

text: It is precisely 12 o’clock when you have to display the parking disc. You put the arrow on …
Do the residents of this road also have to use the parking disc?
Which cars may be parked beyond?

options.text: Electric cars and on LPG or natural gas.

explanation: LESSON 27 – ‘Waiting and parking’.Electric cars.

text: How many minutes are you allowed to park far beyond this board?
explanation: LESSON 27 – ‘Waiting and parking’.The maximum parking time can be indicated on an underboard sign.

text: A broken down car is allowed to stay maximum (…) hours on the public road.
A parking space for electric cars with charging station. Can you park your electric car there?

options.text: Yes, but only when your car is connected.

explanation: LESSON 27 - 'Parking 3'.

text: Are you allowed to park a car past this sign?
Are you allowed to wait past this sign to let someone out of the car?

options.text: From Monday until Saturday between 09:00 am and 06:00 pm.
From Monday until Saturday between 09:00 am and 07:00 pm.
From Monday until Friday between 09:00 am and 07:00 pm.

How many hours is an advertising vehicle allowed to stay on the public road?
How long can the red car be parked there?
explanation: LESSON 27 - 'Waiting and parking'.The time limit only starts past the sign, because the arrow points upwards.

options.text: You look for another parking place.

This sign indicates: free choice between parking on the verge or on the road.
