Parking meter / Parking disk. How long can you park (unless stated otherwise)?
explanation: LESSON 27

options.text: ... allowed maximum 24 hours on the same place.

options.text: ... not allowed to wait or park.

text: Are you allowed to wait past this sign to let a passenger in?
explanation: LESSON 27The traffic sign with the symbol of a lorry indicates that it is a location where lorries are allowed to park.A car may stop briefly there to let a passenger get in or out.

text: Are you allowed to park a car past this sign?
A driver exits a paid parking area. The policeman wants to take a breath test, but the driver refuses his corporation. The policeman will give him a temporary driving ban of (...) hours.
Can a breath test or a breath analysis be imposed to horseback riders on the public road?
You tell the police officer that you have trouble breathing and you refuse a breath test. What is the consequence?

options.text: You are allowed to drive on.
You get a driving ban of 3 hours.
You get a driving ban of 6 hours.

text: The result of a saliva test is positive. How many hours you can not drive?
What is the test called which tests if you have taken drugs?

options.text: The road site test/ saliva test.

text: The police can ask any driver to take a breath test. Is that also the case for a saliva test?

options.text: Yes, a saliva test can be imposed on any driver.
Yes, if there is, based on objective findings, a suspicion of drug use.

explanation: LESSON 28In Belgium, there is zero tolerance for drugs in traffic. The police regularly carry out drug checks to determine whether you have certain prohibited substances in your body.But a saliva test may only be carried out if the police suspect that you are under the influence of drugs, and this suspicion must be based on objective findings.

text: During an alcohol control the police also asks for the car registration.

options.text: You don’t need to have it in the car and therefore you don’t have to show it.
You give the original document or a color copy.

text: At the start of a breath analysis you can ask for 15 minutes waiting time.
explanation: The 15-minute waiting period has been abolished since May 1, 2024

text: A blood test must be done by …

options.text: a designated doctor by the police.
a doctor of choice of the patient.

text: The result of a breath analysis shows 0.28mg/litre alcohol in the exhaled alveolar air. Do you get a temporary driving ban?

options.text: No, because you are below the limit.

text: During a police control you are asked to do a breath test. How much waiting time can you ask for, before the test?
explanation: The 15-minute waiting period has been abolished since May 1, 2024

text: Are you allowed to wait 15 minutes when you have to do a breath analysis?
explanation: The 15-minute waiting period has been abolished since May 1, 2024

text: The test which measures accurately how much the alcohol level is in the exhaled alveolar air, is called …

text: During an alcohol check, you test positive. You can however prove that you did not drink alcohol, but that you are taking medication with the same effect as alcohol. What is the consequence?

options.text: None, because you did not drink alcohol.
Punishable in the same way as if you had consumed alcohol.

explanation: LESSONIf you take medication that has the same effects as alcohol (such as drowsiness or reduced reaction time), this is clearly stated in the leaflet.In that case, you are not allowed to drive a vehicle.Driving anyway is punishable in the same way as driving under the influence of alcohol.

text: The result of a breath analysis is at least 0.22 but less than 0.35 milligram alcohol per litre exhaled alveolar air. What are the consequences?

options.text: An immediate driving ban of six hours.
An immediate driving ban of three hours.

options.text: ... a pedestrian on the public road.
... anyone who is driving a vehicle on the public road.

text: This young man leaves a café and wants to get into the car. What may the police officer ask him to do?

options.text: An alcohol test and a saliva test.

explanation: LESSON 28The police may always require an alcohol test from someone who intends to drive.A saliva test may only be taken if there is an objective suspicion of drug use, based on observable signs.In case of an accident, a saliva test is always allowed.

text: After a breath analysis the result is: 0,39 mg/litre. You immediately get a driving ban of (... ) hours.
When medication is taken together with alcohol, the effect of alcohol can be reinforced.
You are being tough and you refuse an alcohol control. You’ll get an immediate temporary ban of (…) hours.

text: You are involved in an accident. May the police ask you to take a saliva test?

Yes, in the event of an accident, always.

text: From what alcohol level in the breath are you committing an offence?
explanation: LESSON 28- If you have less than 0.22 mg/l, you may continue driving.- If the result is 0.22 mg/l or more, but below 0.35 mg/l, you must hand over your driving licence for 3 hours.It is an offence and you will receive a fine.- If you have 0.35 mg/l or more, you must hand over your driving licence for 6 hours.An immediate withdrawal of your licence is also possible, and you will receive a fine.After those 6 hours, a new breath test or breath analysis will follow.

explanation: LESSON 28 - "Alcohol."That passenger is not a teacher or supervisor of the driver.

options.text: Yes, a doctor can prescribe one.
Yes, it is available in a pharmacy.
No, such a medicine does not exist.

text: The result of a breath analysis shows 0.40mg/litre alcohol in the exhaled alveolar air. Do you get a temporary driving ban?

options.text: No, because you are below the limit.

text: When do you have a ‘positive’ alcohol level?

options.text: Equal to 0,22 mg or more alcohol per litre exhaled alveolar air.
When more than 0,22 mg alcohol per litre exhaled alveolar air.

text: You drank a lot of beer. It’s been said that a few cups of coffee can reduce the alcohol level in your blood. Is this true?

options.text: A breath analysis will be taken.

explanation: LESSON 29The first sign indicates that a tunnel of 500 meters starts 700 meters further.The exact length of the tunnel can be shown on the sign itself. In this case, 700 meters.

You leave the car on the spot.

explanation: LESSON 29 - 'Accident'.If there are injuries, the vehicles will remain in place and the police must come.

text: On regular roads a warning triangle must be placed (...) meters behind the vehicle.

You damaged another car while parking. You don’t know who the owner is. How much time do you have to report it at a police station?
explanation: LESSON 29If you damage someone’s property and the police cannot come to the scene, you must report it as soon as possible at a police station or online via Police-on-Web (for minor damage). The sooner you report it, the more likely it is that the facts will be correctly recorded. Make sure you have all necessary information, such as the location and time of the incident, the license plate of the damaged vehicle, and photos of the damage.

text: The warning triangle must be visible to oncoming traffic from (...) meters.
How many fluorescent jackets must be mandatory in a passenger car?
explanation: LESSON 29

explanation: LESSON 29 - 'Accident'.You are not allowed to change anything more on the situation sketch.

options.text: Completing a European collision form is sufficient.

explanation: LESSON 29 - 'Accident'.Although there are no injuries, call 112, because chemicals can be very dangerous.

text: An accident with only minor damage and no injuries. What are you obliged to show to the other driver if he asks for it?

options.text: The documents of your car, your driver's license and your identity card.
Your driver's license and your identity card.

explanation: LESSON 29 - 'Accident'.You must of course have your driver's license and the original documents with you. But you should not show it or hand it over to the other driver.

text: In your side mirror you see an ambulance with blue flashing lights, but you don’t hear a warning siren.

options.text: You drive to the side and give priority.

text: Who has to fill in the European or International Accident Form?

A young cyclist is involved in an accident. At what age (…) must he show his identity card?
An accident in a tunnel, but there is no smoke or fire. How do you warn the emergency services?

options.text: Preferably by an emergency phone in the tunnel.

text: What do you have to fill in together on a European or International Accident Form?

options.text: The front and the back page.

text: You notice an accident in the other direction of the motorway. What do you do?

options.text: You stop at the first emergency phone.
You stop on the hard shoulder, take your first aid kit and offer assistance.

What do you do when there is a big fire in a tunnel?

options.text: You reverse to exit the tunnel.
You exit the tunnel through an emergency exit.

text: Are you allowed to follow an ambulance with your heavily injured father on board, if it is driving faster than the maximum speed limit?
To whom must I show my ID card in the event of an accident?

options.text: To all persons involved in the accident if they ask, and to the qualified officer.

explanation: LESSON 29In the event of an accident involving only material damage and if you are over 15 years old, you must present your identity card to the other people involved if they request it. In the case of injuries or serious damage, the authorities may also require it.

text: What do you do first when you see a casualty?

options.text: Remove any obstruction from the mouth.
Move him into a safe position.

text: In case of an accident, an injured person may have difficulty breathing. What are you doing?
explanation: LESSON 29 - 'Accident'.You release the respiratory tract and, if necessary, take vomit from the mouth.

text: You are involved in an accident with material damage only on a junction. What do you do first?
In an accident a driver hit his head against the front wind shield and is now unconscious.

options.text: You carefully get him out of the car.
You have to leave him in the car.

text: An injured person asks for a medicine. Should you give it to him?
What is the European emergency number?
When you see these signs in front of a tunnel, you can be sure:

options.text: That the tunnel is at least 500 meters long.
That the tunnel is only 3.5 meters high everywhere.

explanation: LESSON 29The first sign says it is a tunnel that is 500 meters (or longer).The second sign says your vehicle cannot be higher. The tunnel can be higher in some places.

text: A cyclist has been hit at an intersection and is lying unconscious on the ground. Are you allowed to clear the intersection and carefully carry the cyclist to the side of the road?

options.text: Yes, you must clear the intersection.
No, an injured person must remain where they are.

explanation: LESSON 29In an accident with injured persons, you leave the injured where they are and call the emergency services.If there are injured persons, the police must also come to make the official report.

text: What do you write in the big white space of the accident form which is used for the situational sketch. 1. The road and traffic signs (lights, signs, road markings). 2. Vehicles. 3. Direction of the vehicles. 4. 1, 2 and 3.
At what distance (... meters) behind the broken down vehicle do you place a warning triangle on the hard shoulder on the motorway?
You find someone unconscious in a car. You have switched off the engine, turned on the hazard warning lights and placed the warning triangle. What should you do next?

options.text: Carefully remove the person from the vehicle.
Check the breathing and start resuscitation if necessary.

explanation: LESSON 29- First ensure your own safety and that of others.- Check the person and call 112 immediately if there is no response.- Check breathing:.. Look to see if the chest rises and falls... Listen at the mouth and nose for breathing sounds.- Is the person breathing?.. Keep the airway open (tilt the chin upwards)... Continue to monitor breathing until emergency services arrive.- Is the person not breathing or not breathing normally?..Start resuscitation immediately (chest compressions and, if possible, rescue breaths).

text: Exhaust fumes in contact with the sunlight will lead to …
If you have a very environmentally friendly car, are you above or below the Euro standard?
What is the most environmentally friendly fuel?
Which fuel is the MOST polluting or least environmentally friendly?
explanation: LESSON 30 – ‘Environment’. Red diesel contains 200 times more particles sulfur than white diesel.Red diesel you may not use for a car.Low sulfur diesel is environmentally friendly.

text: The fuel of your car is petrol. What is the recommended speed (revs) to change gear?
Driving with open windows consumes less fuel than with closed windows.
When you drive too long in a too low gear …

options.text: ... it has no influence on the fuel consumption.
... it ensures a higher fuel consumption.

text: This sign means ...

options.text: Start of a low emission zone.
Zone where a catalyst is mandatory in the car.

explanation: LES 30 – ‘Environment’.Road authorities have the ability to ban polluting vehicles from certain areas, with a view to improving air quality.

text: You have to transport bicycles. You place them …

options.text: ... at the back of the car.
... on the roof of the car.

text: What is ‘Autodelen’ (Dutch) or ‘Voitures partagées’ (French)?

options.text: With multiple people use the car at the same time to reach a destination.
Occasional use of a car in advance captured moments via reservation.

explanation: LESSON 30 – ‘Environment’. Who shares a car with several people, make use of a car at a different time. You use the car when you need the car. If you don’t need the car, someone else can drive.

text: You drive with a diesel. What is the recommended speed (revs) to change gear?
Are you allowed to re-cut badly worn tyres of a car?

options.text: Yes, when the tread depth can be made deeper than 1.6 mm.

text: You wait for a level crossing with your car motor in freewheel mode. Can you repeatedly give some gas?

options.text: Yes, only in the winter to keep warm the engine.

explanation: LESSON 30 – ‘Environment’. For example, if you wait for a red light with a motor in freewheel mode, repetitive gas (brum brum ... ... broeoemm ...) is not allowed. Not even in the winter to keep warm the engine.

text: You return from your holiday. What do you remove from the rooftop?

options.text: The ski box and the roof rack.

text: The air conditioning is on in the car. The result is …

options.text: ... no influence on the fuel consumption.

text: This sign means: charging place for electric cars on the left and right.
explanation: LESSON 30

text: When must you take this sign into account?

options.text: Only on weekdays, 24 hours a day.
Only on weekdays, including Saturday, from 06:00 to 20:00.
Every day of the week, 24 hours a day.

explanation: LESSON 30These signs indicate the start and end of a low-emission zone (LEZ).A low-emission zone is a defined area where certain vehicles are not allowed because they emit too many harmful substances.A LEZ applies every day of the week, 24 hours a day, unless stated otherwise.Each city or municipality can decide where a LEZ is introduced.

text: Is driving at too high an engine speed also harmful to the environment?
explanation: LESSON 30When you let your engine run unnecessarily at high revs, it consumes more fuel and emits more CO₂ and nitrogen oxides. This is harmful to the environment and increases engine wear, leading to higher maintenance costs.

text: What does E5 refer to?

options.text: The octane content of the petrol.

explanation: Since 2019, fuel is primarily designated by a name that indicates the maximum amount of bioethanol mixed in. Bioethanol is an alcohol made by fermenting sugar, corn or wheat. This is therefore a form of renewable energy.

text: Which diesel is the most environmentally friendly?

options.text: Diesel with a less sulfur level.

text: When is a car the most environmentally friendly?
explanation: LESSON 30 – “Environment”.Eco-score is expressed with a number between 1 and 100.The higher, the more environmentally friendly.

text: A dirty air filter in the engine …

options.text: ... has no influence on the fuel consumption.

text: The catalytic converter in a car …

options.text: ... is the reason for less fuel consumption.

Where can I find the Euro standard (Euronorm / La norme Euro) of my car?

options.text: On the green vehicle inspection card.

explanation: LESSON 30

text: You have to make a long journey.

options.text: You increase the tyre pressure a bit.
You lower the tyre pressure a bit.

explanation: LESSON 31 – ‘Technique’.

text: Which tool ensures the car from slipping and keeps it steerable when you suddenly need to hit the brakes?
explanation: LESSON 31 – ‘Technique’. Learn very well in your book the difference between ABS and ESP.

text: Where do you keep your left foot after changing gear?

options.text: To the left of the pedal.

explanation: LESSON 31 – ‘Technique’. Put your feet to the left of the pedal.

options.text: To where you want to drive.

explanation: LESSON 31 – ‘Technique’.In a built-up area, the maximum permitted speed is 50 km / hour.

text: On a tyre you can see: 165/70 R 14 81 T. The R stands for Radial. What does the 165 stand for?

options.text: The width of the tyre in mm.
The diameter of the rim in inch.

text: On a tyre you can see: 165/70 R 14 81 T. The R stands for Radial. What does the 14 next to the R stand for?
explanation: LESSON 31 – ‘Technique’.Tip exam: learn very well in your book the meaning of the markings on a tyre.

… where you stop in case of bad luck.

explanation: LESSON 31 – ‘Technique’. Always first look if it can turn safely. Then turn on the turn signal. Sufficiently slow down.

The car is worse positioned on the road.

options.text: Together with the radiator discharging the heat from the engine.
Ensure that the air conditioner can cool sufficiently.

explanation: LESSON 31 – ‘Technique’.In cooperation with the radiator, the coolant ensures that the heat is drained.

options.text: Pushing hard on the brake pedal.

explanation: LESSON 31 – ‘Technique’. Learn very well in your book the difference between ABS and ESP.

You don’t change the tyre pressure.

explanation: LESSON 31 – ‘Technique’. At a long drive or if you carry a heavy load should increase the pressure a bit.

text: If there are radial tires on the car at the front, which tires should be at the back?

(because: You may only place radial tires at the front if there are also radial tires at the back.

text: What does the 55 on this tyre mean?

options.text: The width of the tyre in mm.
The diameter of the rim in inches.

explanation: LESSON 31 – ‘Technique’. Tip exam: learn very well in your book the meaning of the markings on a tyre.

text: Your car starts to skid. In which direction should you look?

options.text: Towards the direction you intended to go.

explanation: LESSON 31Although braking is probably your first instinct, you should avoid braking too hard. This can cause the wheels to lock and reduce traction.What should you do instead?Look in the direction you want to go. Unconsciously, you will steer towards where you are looking. You can imagine what happens if you keep looking at the danger.Steer in the opposite direction (counter-steer).Press the clutch and release the accelerator.

text: Badly worn tyres are allowed to be re-cut when they can get a tread depth of 1.6mm.
explanation: LESSON 31 – ‘Technique’.

explanation: LESSON 31 - "Technology".You can check the tire pressure when the tires are cold and the car is horizontal.

explanation: LESSON 31 – ‘Technique’. If your driving gear is too low, then the fuel consumption will be higher.

options.text: You must stop immediately because your brakes no longer work.
You keep driving but have it checked at a garage.
You remove the fuse so the light stops glowing.

explanation: LESSON 31When the ABS warning light is on, it means the anti-lock braking system is not working properly. However, your normal brakes still function. You can continue driving carefully, but you should have the system inspected as soon as possible.

text: What does the 205 on this tyre mean?

options.text: The width of the tyre in mm.
The diameter of the rim in inches.

explanation: LESSON 31 – ‘Technique’. Tip exam: learn very well in your book the meaning of the markings on a tyre.

text: What are the consequences when your tyre pressure is too low?

options.text: Higher fuel consumption and quickly badly worn tyres.

explanation: LESSON 31 – ‘Technique’. You consume more fuel and the tires wear out faster.

text: What's under this blue stop?
explanation: LESSON 31 – ‘Technique’.

text: The minimum tread depth of a tyre must be (...).
explanation: LESSON 31 – ‘Technique’.

text: The windshield washer reservoir is empty. This may negatively affect the driver’s visibility. What should you do?
explanation: LESSON 31If you hear a humming or buzzing sound when you activate the washer but no liquid sprays onto the windshield, the reservoir is empty. You should refill it as soon as possible, because without washer fluid your visibility can be greatly reduced, especially in rain or when dirt splashes up from the road. Just like engine oil, the washer fluid level should be checked regularly.

text: What should you do if you notice an oil leak under your car?

options.text: Continue driving until the next service.
Go to a garage as soon as possible.
Check the oil level before every trip and add oil if needed.

explanation: LESSON 13An oil leak can cause serious engine damage. Even if you top up the oil regularly, the leak remains dangerous. You must have the leak repaired in a garage as soon as possible.

text: The four digits following the word DOT on the sidewall of a tire indicate the tire’s production date.

options.text: The first two digits show the week, and the last two the year.
The first two digits show the year, and the last two the week.
The four digits have nothing to do with the production date.

explanation: LESSON 31The DOT code includes a 4-digit number: the first two digits indicate the week of manufacture, and the last two indicate the year. For example, 3519 means the tire was made in week 35 of 2019.

text: When are snow chains allowed?

options.text: When there is snow or ice on the road.

explanation: LESSON 31 – ‘Technique’.

text: It's April 6th. A snowstorm sweeps across the country. What can you drive with?

options.text: With snow chains or studded tires.

explanation: LESSON 31 – ‘Technique’.

text: When is a car unmanageable because of aquaplaning?

options.text: You do not drive in the tracks of your vehicle ahead.
Sigh strength of a truck before you pull the car along.
The tires of your car have no contact with the road surface.

explanation: LESSON 31 – ‘Technique’.One speaks of aquaplaning when, because of water, the four tires cannot touch the road surface.

text: On a dry road surface the braking distance with ABS can be (…) than without ABS.
explanation: LESSON 31 – ‘Technique’. If you brake with ABS it doesn’t want to say that the braking distance is shorter.

text: ESP is the abbreviation of ‘Electronic Stability Program’.
explanation: LESSON 31 – ‘Technique’. It prevents a vehicle from slipping by braking on one or more wheels separately.(Learn very well in your book the difference between ABS and ESP).

text: Your car starts to skid. Which direction are you looking at?

options.text: The direction you want to go.

explanation: LESSON 31

text: What is the tool called that prevents you from slipping when you suddenly have to change direction?

options.text: Yes, if it is placed in a fixed holder.

explanation: LESSON 31Using a smartphone as a GPS is allowed, as long as the device is placed in a fixed holder.Of course, you may only hold the smartphone in your hand when you are stopped or parked.

text: Your car starts slipping. What do you do?

options.text: You pull the steering wheel shortly to the left and to the right.
You release the gas pedal and declutch.

explanation: LESSON 31 – ‘Technique’. Learn very well in your book the difference between ‘front-wheel-slip’, ‘rear-wheel-slip’ and ‘four-wheel-slip’ and what to do.

text: What should you do when you have to drive up a steep slope?

options.text: You just continue driving more slowly.
You shift to a higher gear.
You shift to a lower gear.

explanation: LESSON 31When driving steep uphill or steep downhill, it is best to shift to a lower gear.This gives the engine more power and improves control of the vehicle.

text: You approach a bend. When do you brake?

options.text: You brake well enough before the bend.

explanation: LESSON 31 – ‘Technique’. When you approach a bend you have to slow down before the bend.

text: Which answer is WRONG? It is March 1st. It is snowing heavily in this built-up area and visibility is only 60 metres.

options.text: The car may use studded tyres.
The car may use snow chains.
The front and rear fog lights must be switched on.

explanation: LESSON 31The question was: “which answer is wrong.”A. Correct. Studded tyres are allowed between 1 November and 31 March.B. Correct. Snow chains may always be used when there is snow on the roadway.C. Wrong. Only the rear fog lights must be switched on.

text: The marks in the grooves indicate when the minimum tread depth is reached. It is then time to change the tyre.
explanation: LESSON 31

text: If the air filter is dirty, does it increase fuel consumption?
explanation: LESSON 31A clogged or dirty air filter reduces the airflow to the engine, which increases the amount of fuel required to maintain vehicle performance.A dirty air filter therefore has a significant impact on fuel consumption, whether the vehicle runs on petrol or diesel.Depending on your vehicle and fuel type, the increase in consumption can range from 10% to 25%.

text: The older the car tyre is, the … it gets.
explanation: LESSON 31 – ‘Technique’. Older tyres are harder.

text: If the pressure is too low, the car drives ...
explanation: LESSON 31 – ‘Technique’.A too low tire pressure causes:. less good road holding,. more wear of the band,. higher fuel consumption.

text: Does the cold winter weather influence the working of the battery of a car?
explanation: LESSON 31 – ‘Technique’. When the weather is very cold, a battery has difficulties to work properly. In winter many batteries are broken.

text: To check the oil level, the car must be on a flat surface. But when should you check the oil level?

options.text: After driving a few kilometres so the oil is warm.

explanation: LESSON 31 – ‘Technique’.Engine oil is one of the most important fluids in your vehicle. It lubricates moving parts, prevents overheating and wear, and helps keep the engine clean.To get a reliable reading, you should check the oil level when the engine is cold and the car is parked on a level surface. If the oil is still warm, it may not have fully drained back into the oil pan, leading to an inaccurate reading.

text: The light of ABS keeps burning while driving, this indicates a malfunction. How do you react? assistance.

options.text: You immediately stop and call the roadside
You can keep on driving without any problems.

explanation: LESSON 31 – ‘Technique’. Learn very well in your book the difference between ABS and ESP.

text: The function of motor oil. 1. Has a cleaning and lubricating function. 2. Ensures that the moving parts don’t touch each other. 3. Prevents the motor from blocking. 4. All above are correct.
explanation: LESSON 31 – ‘Technique’. Motor oil has a lubricating function and prevents overheating and blocking of the engine.The oil protects the internal parts against rust and cleans the engine.

text: What is the function of motor oil?

options.text: Only lubricating and cooling down of the engine.
Lubricating, cooling down and cleaning of the engine.

explanation: LESSON 31 – ‘Technique’. Motor oil has a lubricating function and prevents overheating and blocking of the engine.The oil protects the internal parts against rust and cleans the engine.

text: What is the maximum speed you are allowed to drive on a motorway with studded tyres?
explanation: On a normal road: 60 kph.

text: One speaks of aquaplaning when, because of the water of heavy rain, the four tires cannot touch the road surface.
explanation: LESSON 31 – ‘Technique’.Aquaplaning: suddenly loss of contact with the road in rain. Aqua Planning is the situation that between the tires and the road surface is a thin layer of water. The result is that the car will 'float'. The car will be in effect temporarily unmanageable.

text: The alternator … 1. provides the car with electricity during driving. 2. recharges the battery of the car.
explanation: LESSON 31 – ‘Technique’. If you drive by car, the alternator…… provides the car with electricity during driving;… recharges the battery of the car.

text: It is important to change the tyres every 10.000 or 15.000 km. How do you have to switch them?
explanation: LESSON 31 – ‘Technique’. The screws must be tightened crosswise.

text: When are studded tyres allowed?

options.text: When there is snow or ice on the road.

explanation: LESSON 31 – ‘Technique’. Motorways: 90 km/h.Ordinary roads: 60 km/hour.

text: You have to drive downhill for a long distance. What should you do?

options.text: Let the car roll downhill in neutral.

explanation: LESSON 31Even when driving downhill, you should engage a lower gear.Rule of thumb: descend in the same gear you would use to climb the same hill.This allows engine braking and prevents brake wear.

text: It is 30 November. What is the maximum permitted speed when driving with studded tyres within a built-up area in the Brussels-Capital Region?

options.text: Driving with studded tyres is not allowed.

explanation: LESSON 31Studded tyres may be used between 1 November and 31 March on vehicles with a maximum authorised mass up to 3.5 tonnes.Speed limits with studded tyres:- Motorways and roads with 2×2 lanes separated by a central reservation: maximum 90 km/h.- Ordinary roads: maximum 60 km/h.- Within a built-up area: the maximum speed applicable there.In the Brussels-Capital Region, this is 30 km/h.

text: What should you do if your vehicle starts aquaplaning?

options.text: Brake hard and steer to regain control.
Release the accelerator, do not brake and keep the steering wheel straight.
Accelerate so that the tyres regain grip.

explanation: LESSON 31Aquaplaning is a phenomenon in which the tyres lose contact with the road because of a layer of water.If your vehicle starts aquaplaning, release the accelerator, do not brake and keep the steering wheel as straight as possible.Avoid sudden steering movements. Control will gradually return once the tyres regain contact with the road.

text: What is NOT allowed?

options.text: Radial front and diagonal rear tires.
Front diagonal and rear radial tires.

explanation: LESSON 31 – ‘Technique’. - RADIAL TIRES are authorized at the front and at the rear.- DIAGONAL TIRES are authorized at the front and at the rear.- DIAGONAL at the front and RADIAL at the rear is authorized.- RADIAL at the front and DIAGINAL at the rear are NOT authorized.(because: you can only put radial tires on the front if there are also radial tires on the rear.

text: In what order do you fasten the bolts after changing a wheel?
explanation: LESSON 31 – ‘Technique’.The screws must be tightened crosswise.

text: Two cars will cross each other on a dirt road. How much lateral distance must be kept?
explanation: LESSON 14 – ‘Crossing’.The traffic regulations don’t define 'how much' it must be. There is written: 'sufficient'.

text: The driver of this grey car wants to go to Hasselt. Which lane must he drive on?
explanation: LESSON 4 – ‘The motorway’. It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time.The practice questions for the theory lessons are voiced.

explanation: [Violations of the 3rd and 4th degree on our page Theory B: nr. 32]LESSON 15 +16 – ‘Overtaking’.It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time. The practice questions for the theory lessons are with voice.

text: You have a breakdown on a motorway. When must the driver wear the safety vest?
explanation: LESSON 4The driver must wear a high-visibility vest as soon as he or she leaves the vehicle.That is why the vest must be kept inside the car and within reach (not in the boot).Passengers are not required to wear one, but it is strongly recommended.

text: Which sign do you see before the sign “end of priority road”?
explanation: LESSON 19Sign 1 = priority at the next intersection.Sign 2 = priority road.Sign 3 = one-way street.

text: A minor accident without injuries at an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: You place a warning triangle and leave the cars where they are.
You park the cars in a safe place.

explanation: LESSON 29In case of a minor accident without injuries at an intersection, you should try to clear the intersection.If the vehicles can still move, park them next to the roadway in a place where parking is permitted.

text: A driver has parked his car very badly. But is he allowed to park there?

options.text: Yes, because there is a broken yellow line.
No, because there is a broken yellow line.

explanation: LESSON 26You may not park (but you may stop) next to a broken yellow line painted along the edge of the roadway.

text: This picture is taken from the car you drive and you’re leaving a roundabout. When leaving you have to give priority to the cyclists and mopeds on the cycle lane.
explanation: LESSON 19 – ‘Junction and traffic sign’. It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time. The practice questions for the theory lessons are with voice.

text: The driver of the blue car drives faster than the red one. Is that allowed?
explanation: LESSON 15 +16 – ‘Overtaking’.It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time. The practice questions for the theory lessons are with voice.

text: A driver is checked and has an alcohol level of 0.5 g/l of blood. May he continue driving?
explanation: LESSON 28In Belgium, a driver with an alcohol level of 0.5 g/l of blood (equivalent to 0.22 mg/l of breath alcohol) may not continue driving immediately.He faces:- a driving ban of at least 3 hours,- a fine starting from €179,- and a possible suspension or withdrawal of the driving licence in case of repeat offences or aggravating circumstances.

text: What is the reaction distance when you are driving at 90 km/h?
explanation: LESSON 13Between the moment the driver sees the danger and the moment the brain processes this information and realises that the brake pedal must be pressed, the vehicle has already travelled a certain distance.The higher the speed, the longer the distance covered during the reaction time.• At 50 km/h, the reaction distance is about 15 metres.• At 90 km/h, the reaction distance is about 27 metres.• At 120 km/h, the reaction distance is about 36 metres.- This happens before the brake pedal is pressed.- A drunk driver reacts more slowly, which makes the reaction distance even longer.

text: Are towing services allowed to drive on the hard shoulder while working?
explanation: LESSON 4Police, emergency services and towing services (while working) may drive on the hard shoulder, the peak-hour lane and the emergency corridor.

text: What is the maximum speed limit (… kph) for this car in this street?
explanation: LESSON 12It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time. The practice questions for the theory lessons are with voice.

text: Are you allowed to drive past this sign with a car?
explanation: LESSON 23 – ‘Prohibited direction’.This positive instruction sign means: no through road.

text: How do you react when you drive into a fogbank?
explanation: LESSON 11 – ‘The lights’.It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time. The practice questions for the theory lessons are with voice.

explanation: LESSON 6 - 'Special places'.It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time. The practice questions for the theory lessons are with voice.

text: On a highway, only a towing service that has been called by the police can tow a car. What happens on an express road?

options.text: You may ask a friend to tow your car.
A towing service that you call can tow.
The police will request a towing service.

explanation: LESSON 5 – ‘The express road’.If your car breaks down on a highway or an express road, the police call a towing service they prefer.

text: Is a reflective safety jacket obligatory in the car?
explanation: LESSON 4 – ‘The motorway’. It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time.The practice questions for the theory lessons are voiced.

explanation: LESSON 19 – ‘Junction and traffic sign’. It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time. The practice questions for the theory lessons are with voice.

text: There is a traffic jam. The grey car drives on the left lane on this motorway. A motorcycle wants to overtake between the left and the middle lane. Where should the car driver drive on the lane?

options.text: As far to the left as possible.
As far to the right as possible.

explanation: LESSON 4 – ‘The motorway’. In a queue motorcycles are allowed to ride:. between the two left lanes of traffic.. at a maximum speed of 20 km/hour faster than the other vehicles.. and at a maximum speed of 50 km/hour.So the grey car drives as far as possible to the left, to give place.

text: Are you allowed to drive on an express road with a moped class B?
explanation: LESSON 5 – ‘The express road’.It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time.The practice questions for the theory lessons are voiced.

text: What is the maximum speed allowed in the Flemish Region on an ordinary road when using studded tyres?
explanation: LESSON 4Studded tyres may be used from 1 November to 31 March on vehicles with a maximum authorised mass of up to 3.5 tonnes.The maximum permitted speed is:- on motorways and roads with 2×2 lanes separated by a central strip: 90 km/h;- on ordinary roads in all regions: 60 km/h.

text: At this junction you have to give right of way, except to cyclists and mopeds.
explanation: LESSON 19 – ‘Junction and traffic sign’. It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time. The practice questions for the theory lessons are with voice.

text: Where can I find the Euro standard (Euronorm / La norme Euro) of my car? A / On the green vehicle inspection card. B / On the registration certificate. C / On the insurance document.
explanation: LESSON 30It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time. The practice questions for the theory lessons are with voice.

text: You have a provisional driving license B. Are you allowed to turn right with your car at this intersection?
explanation: LESSON 1

text: The barriers are already open, but the red light is still on. Can I cross the crossing already?
explanation: You are not allowed to drive onto the level crossing as long as the red flashing light is on, even if the barriers are open.

text: Is a pedestrian (orange arrow) allowed to cross the road at that place?

options.text: No, he must use the pedestrian crossing.

explanation: LESSON 7The traffic sign indicates that there is a pedestrian crossing 100 meters ahead.A pedestrian must use it if they are within 20 meters of the crossing.That is not the case here.

text: The driver of a car overtakes a cyclist riding on the roadway on the left side. How much lateral clearance must he keep here?
explanation: LESSON 15This image clearly shows a situation outside a built-up area.- On the roadway:When overtaking a pedestrian walking on the roadway, or a cyclist or moped rider using the roadway, you must keep at least 1.5 metres of lateral clearance.- On a cycle path:If the cyclist or moped rider is on a cycle path, you must also keep this 1.5-metre distance. (This distance also applies when meeting a cyclist coming from the opposite direction.)Inside built-up areas, the required lateral clearance is 1 metre.

text: An accident with only material damage. There is an argument. What do you do?

options.text: Mention it on the accident form.

explanation: Explanation: see lesson 29

text: Are the cars allowed to ride on the rush-hour lane?
explanation: LESSON 4 – ‘The motorway’.If a green arrow hangs above the rush-hour lane, cars may drive on that lane.

explanation: LESSON 15 +16 – ‘Overtaking’.It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time. The practice questions for the theory lessons are with voice.

explanation: [Violations of the 3rd and 4th degree on our page Theory B: nr. 32]LESSON 7 – ‘The pedestrians’.It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time.The practice questions for the theory lessons are voiced.

explanation: LESSON 19 – ‘Junction and traffic sign’. It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time. The practice questions for the theory lessons are with voice.

explanation: LESSON 5It is a normal carriageway divided into two lanes.The maximum permitted speed in the Flemish and Brussels Regions is 70 km/h.In the Walloon Region, it is 90 km/h.

When you need help, you dial the international emergency number (…).

explanation: LESSON 9 – ‘M.A.W. and M.G.W.’.Signs 1, 2 and 3 (since October 1st 2022) relate to the M.A.W.

explanation: LESSON 19The yellow priority sign with the supplementary sign indicates that the priority road ends 100 metres further. At the next junction, you will have to give way.

explanation: Explanation: see lesson 29

options.text: You are approaching a tram stop.
Tram tracks are located on the roadway.

explanation: LESSON 1This is a warning sign.Watch out for trams, which always have priority.

explanation: LESSON 17 – ‘Qualified persons’.It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time. The practice questions for the theory lessons are with voice.

text: An accident without injuries at an intersection within a built-up area. You have already placed a warning triangle. What do you do next?

options.text: You try to park the cars in a safe place.
You leave the cars where they are, and fill in the European accident report.

explanation: LESSON 29In the case of a minor accident without injuries, you should try to clear the intersection.If that is truly impossible and the cars block the intersection, then you notify the police.

text: An intersection without traffic lights or priority signs. Is the blue car allowed to overtake a two-wheeled moped on the left?
explanation: LESSON 16This is an intersection where the priority-to-the-right rule applies.At this type of intersection, the car is only allowed to overtake a cyclist on the left.

text: A one-way street. What is the white car allowed to do at that place?
explanation: LESSON 25The carriageway is divided into traffic lanes.The driver is not allowed to park on the carriageway.He may only stop briefly to pick up or drop off passengers or to load or unload.

text: In this bicycle zone, is the car allowed to overtake a cyclist?
explanation: LESSON 3In a bicycle zone, motor vehicles are not allowed to overtake a cyclist, scooter, or any other means of transport considered equivalent to a bicycle.Other vehicles (for example, a moped) may be overtaken on the left in a bicycle zone, provided that the maximum permitted speed is not exceeded.

text: The cyclist and the truck both want to turn right at this intersection. How does the cyclist react?

options.text: He hurries so that he can turn first.
He turns at the same time as the truck.
He slows down and lets the truck turn first.

explanation: LESSON 10No matter how well the mirrors are adjusted, there are always areas beside or behind the vehicle that the driver of a truck or car cannot see.These areas are called blind spots.Many accidents happen at intersections because a cyclist is in the truck’s blind spot.A smart cyclist slows down and lets the truck turn first.

text: A roadway without road markings within a built-up area. Is this car correctly parked?
explanation: LESSON 25On a one-way street, vehicles may park on both the left and the right side of the roadway.However, this car is incorrectly parked, because it is facing the wrong direction of traffic.

text: Which of these signs applies to both the carriageway and the shoulder?
explanation: LESSON 27

options.text: From here on until the exit maximum 90kph.
From here on 90kph. You have to leave the motorway at the first exit.

explanation: LESSON 4 – ‘The motorway’. It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time.The practice questions for the theory lessons are voiced.

explanation: LESSON 31Studded tyres may be used between 1 November and 31 March on vehicles with a maximum authorised mass up to 3.5 tonnes.Speed limits with studded tyres:- Motorways and roads with 2×2 lanes separated by a central reservation: maximum 90 km/h.- Ordinary roads: maximum 60 km/h.- Within a built-up area: the maximum speed applicable there.In the Brussels-Capital Region, this is 30 km/h.

From mote than 40 kph too fast.

explanation: LESSON 19 – ‘Junction and traffic sign’. It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time. The practice questions for the theory lessons are with voice.

explanation: LESSON 14 – ‘Crossing’.It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time. The practice questions for the theory lessons are with voice.

text: What do you do when a bus stops at this stop?

options.text: Stop and wait until the bus leaves again.

explanation: LESSON 22 - 'Train - tram - bus'.You don't have to stop, but you can drive on carefully.

text: Today is 12 February. What is the car allowed to do at this place?
explanation: LESSON 26This traffic sign means that parking is prohibited on this side of the carriageway from the 1st to the 15th of the month.➡️ Stopping (for example to pick up or drop off passengers) is allowed.➡️ The prohibition applies only to the carriageway.If there is a verge, parking there is allowed.➡️ You must therefore park on the opposite side of the road.

explanation: LESSON 15 +16 – ‘Overtaking’.It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time. The practice questions for the theory lessons are with voice.

text: *** 5 points question *** What is the maximum speed limit in Flanders on a ordinary road? (... km/h)
explanation: [Violations of the 3rd and 4th degree on our page Theory B: nr. 32]LESSON 1 - 'The public road'.It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time.The practice questions for the theory lessons are voiced.

text: Are you allowed to hold your mobile phone in the car while waiting at a red traffic light?
explanation: Even when stopped at a red light, you are still considered a road user and are not allowed to hold or use a mobile phone, unless it is placed in a holder designed for that purpose.

text: Past this sign in Flanders, you are allowed to drive maximum (…) kph with a car.
explanation: LESSON 6 – ‘Special places’.It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time.The practice questions for the theory lessons are voiced.

text: *** 5 points question *** The green filter arrow is lit up. Is the driver of the blue car still allowed to cross at the junction and turn left?
explanation: [Violations of the 3rd and 4th degree on our page Theory B: nr. 32]LESSON 18 – ‘Traffic lights’.It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time. The practice questions for the theory lessons are with voice.

text: What happens if you refuse to take a saliva test?

options.text: You receive a temporary driving ban of 6 hours.
You receive a temporary driving ban of 10 hours.
You receive a temporary driving ban of 12 hours.

explanation: LESSON 28A saliva test may only be administered when the police suspect drug use.Although Belgian law allows you to refuse the test, it is strongly advised to cooperate. If you refuse, the police must call a doctor to evaluate your reasons.If the doctor concludes that you have no legal grounds for refusing, you must pay the doctor’s costs and you will receive a temporary 12-hour driving ban.During a saliva test, a swab is used to collect saliva from your mouth to determine the presence of drugs.If the result exceeds the permitted value:– you must immediately surrender your licence for 12 hours– an immediate withdrawal of the licence is possible– after 12 hours, a new saliva test is requiredOffenders also risk heavy fines and a driving-ban sentence of up to 5 years.

text: What is the maximum permitted speed in an agglomeration of the Brussels-Capital Region?
explanation: LESSON 12 - 'Speed'.It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time. The practice questions for the theory lessons are with voice.

text: Fill in a number. Which traffic sign has the same meaning as a green light?
explanation: LESSON 18(1) An inverted triangle has the same meaning as a green light.(2) A circle has the same meaning as a steady amber light.(3) A horizontal bar has the same meaning as a red light.(4) A diagonal bar pointing left allows driving only in that direction.

text: Who has priority?
explanation: LESSON 21 – ‘Priority and changing directions’.The driver of the white car who wants to drive straight on has priority.The driver who wants to turn left, has to give priority.

text: In the Flemish Region, the minimum speed on a motorway is 70 km/h, if conditions allow. What is the minimum speed on a motorway in the Walloon Region?

options.text: There is no minimum speed on motorways in Wallonia.

explanation: LESSON 4 – Explanation:Throughout Belgium, the minimum speed on a motorway is 70 km/h, when conditions allow.In situations such as snow, heavy rain, roadworks, traffic jams or other hazards, drivers must adjust their speed and may drive more slowly.

text: It is night, outside a built-up area. While the blue car is overtaking, the distracted driver of the white car suddenly swerves to the left. What may the driver of the blue car do?

options.text: He may only use the main beams because it is night.
He may use the horn to avoid an accident.

explanation: LESSON 11When may you use the horn?During the day:Inside and outside built-up areas: to warn others and prevent an accident.Outside built-up areas: to warn a driver you intend to overtake.Between dusk and dawn:Only in case of imminent danger.In all other cases, you must flash your headlights alternately instead of using the horn.

text: Organising a speed race on a public road is an offence …
explanation: LESSON – SERIOUS OFFENCESExcept with special authorisation from the legally competent authority, all speed races and sporting competitions are prohibited on public roads, in particular speed, regularity or skill races.This is considered a fourth-degree offence.

text: Are you allowed to wait for a while past this sign until the school bus arrives?
explanation: Explanation: See Lesson 27

text: A two-way road. The driver of the white car wants to turn left. He positions himself as close as possible to the centre line of the road. Is he acting correctly?

options.text: No, he must position himself on the left-hand side of the road.

explanation: LESSON 21The road on which the white car is driving is not a one-way street.- When turning left, the driver positions himself as close as possible to the centre line of the road.- When turning right, he must position himself as far to the right as possible on the road.➡️ On a one-way street, a driver who wants to turn left must position himself on the far left side.

text: During a roadside check, the police ask for the vehicle registration certificate. In which form must this document be presented?

A copy is sufficient, provided the original is presented later.

explanation: LESSON 9The following documents must be present in the vehicle:- Registration certificate (original)- Certificate of conformity (original)- Insurance certificate (original, copy or digital version on a smartphone)- Roadworthiness inspection certificate (original), once the vehicle is 4 years old

text: May the car overtake the truck on the left?
explanation: LESSON 16The red circular prohibition sign indicates that drivers are forbidden to:- overtake a combination of vehicles, or- overtake any vehicle with more than two wheels.The blue sign indicates that the overtaking prohibition begins 200 metres further ahead.

text: Is the brown car allowed to come out of the street?
explanation: LESSON 23 – ‘Prohibited direction’.This prohibitive sign indicates no entry past this sign to drivers of all vehicles having more than two wheels or motorcycles with a side car.However they are allowed to drive in the opposite direction.

text: What do you do first when you see a casualty?

options.text: Remove any obstruction from the mouth.
Move him into a safe position.

explanation: Explanation: see lesson 29

text: An intersection without traffic signs. The priority-to-the-right rule applies. The truck is moving slowly onto the intersection, ready to turn left. May the grey car overtake it on the right at the intersection?
explanation: LESSON 16What the traffic rules say:Normally, overtaking is done on the left.Exception: overtaking is allowed on the right when the driver to be overtaken has signaled the intention to turn left and has moved to the left side to perform this maneuver.Overtaking on the left at intersections where the priority-to-the-right rule applies is prohibited, except in this specific case.

text: *** 5 points question *** You must switch off the headlights or driving lamps when the driver in front of you is less than (…)m away.
explanation: [Violations of the 3rd and 4th degree on our page Theory B: nr. 32]LESSON 11 – ‘The lights’. It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time. The practice questions for the theory lessons are with voice.

text: At what maximum speed may this car drive past the yellow sign within a built-up area in the Brussels Region?
explanation: LESSON 12It is a roadway within a built-up area.In the Walloon and Flemish Regions, the maximum permitted speed inside built-up areas is 50 km/h.In the Brussels Region, it is 30 km/h.The yellow sign has nothing to do with speed — it is a priority-road sign indicating that you are driving on a priority road.

text: What is the maximum speed limit (… km/hour) a car is allowed to drive on this express road with 2x3 lanes outside a built up area?
