text: *** 5 points question *** What is the hierarchical order?
explanation: [Violations of the 3rd and 4th degree on our page Theory B: nr. 32]LESSON 17 – ‘Qualified persons’.At the top of the commands of an agent.Then the traffic lights.Then the road signs.Then the traffic rules.

text: Are you allowed to overtake a cyclist on the left at this junction?
explanation: LESSON 15 +16 – ‘Overtaking’.It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time. The practice questions for the theory lessons are with voice.

text: The police stop you in a built-up area in Flanders because you were driving at 75 km/h. What are the consequences?

options.text: You receive an immediate temporary withdrawal of your driving licence.
You will have to appear before the court.

explanation: LESSON 12You risk an immediate withdrawal of your licence as soon as you drive more than 30 km/h too fast on motorways, expressways or ordinary roads.But in built-up areas, 30 km/h zones, or residential areas, you already risk this when you drive more than 20 km/h too fast.You risk a driving disqualification as soon as you exceed the speed limit by more than 40 km/h on motorways, expressways or ordinary roads.In built-up areas, 30 km/h zones, or residential areas, you already receive a disqualification once you exceed the limit by more than 30 km/h.This is decided by the judge, not by the police.

text: Where are you allowed to overtake a moped on the left at an intersection?

options.text: On a road with priority from the right.
On a priority road and a road with priority from the right.

explanation: LESSON 16

text: Which arrow indicates that the parking prohibition starts at the arrow?
explanation: Explanation: See lesson 26

text: A driver of a car must not take into account the special traffic lights for the pedestrians.
explanation: LESSON 18 – ‘Traffic lights’.It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time. The practice questions for the theory lessons are with voice.

text: *** 5 points question *** Who is allowed to cross the junction?

options.text: The blue and the green car.
The brown car and the moped.

explanation: [Violations of the 3rd and 4th degree on our page Theory B: nr. 32]LESSON 17 – ‘Qualified persons’.It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time. The practice questions for the theory lessons are with voice.

text: 25 September. It has snowed heavily in Wallonia. Are you allowed to drive with snow chains?
explanation: LESSON 31Snow chains may only be used when there is snow or ice on the roadway.

text: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Take a ferry to the other side.
Deep canal next to the road.

explanation: LESSON 1 – ‘The public road’.It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time.The practice questions for the theory lessons are voiced.

text: This speed limit applies …

options.text: ... until you see an ‘End zone’ sign.

explanation: Explanation: see lesson 12It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time. The practice questions for the theory lessons are with voice.

text: Who won’t be asked to do a breath test?

options.text: Someone on a parking area of a department store who is going to drive a car.
A cyclist who is pushing his bicycle on the public road.

explanation: Explanation: See Lesson 28

text: A driver of a moped has fallen to the ground.

options.text: You leave the helmet on the head.

explanation: Explanation: see lesson 29

text: *** 5 points question *** The driver of this car must stop.
explanation: [Violations of the 3rd and 4th degree on our page Theory B: nr. 32]LESSON 17 – ‘Qualified persons’.It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time. The practice questions for the theory lessons are with voice.

text: Just before entering this tunnel, it suddenly starts to rain heavily. Which lights do you use when driving inside the tunnel?

options.text: The dipped headlights and the rear fog light.
The dipped headlights, the rear fog light, and the front fog lights.

explanation: LESSON 11Inside the tunnel, it is quite dark and visibility is less than 200 meters. Therefore, you must drive with your dipped headlights on.Inside the tunnel it does not rain, so the fog lights are not used.

text: The police stopped you because you were driving at 67 km/h in a built-up area in the Brussels region. What are the consequences?

options.text: You only have to pay a fine.
Your driving licence will be temporarily withdrawn.
You will have to appear in court.

explanation: LESSON 12The maximum speed limit in a built-up area in the Brussels region is 30 km/h.You were therefore driving 36 km/h too fast.A driving disqualification is imposed when you exceed the limit by more than 40 km/h on motorways, expressways or ordinary roads.However, in a built-up area, a 30 km/h zone or a residential area, you already risk disqualification if you exceed the limit by more than 30 km/h.This is not done by the police but by a judge in court.Depending on the verdict, you may lose your right to drive for at least 8 days and up to 5 years, even for vehicles that do not require a driving licence.For novice drivers (with a full driving licence for less than 2 years), the rule is even stricter.

text: This warning sign means that you are approaching a dangerous intersection.
explanation: LESSON 19This is not a warning sign but a priority sign.It means that you have priority at the next intersection.

text: A breath analysis showed an alcohol level in the exhaled alveolar air of at least 0,35 mg/litre and you got a driving ban of six hours. What happens after these six hours?

options.text: The temporary driving ban has passed and you are allowed to leave.
You must do another breath test or a breath analysis.

explanation: Explanation: See Lesson 28

text: An accident with very minor vehicle damage at an intersection. What should you do first?

options.text: Fill in the European accident report form.

explanation: LESSON 29In the event of an accident with very minor damage, you should first move the vehicles to a safe place, if possible.This clears the intersection or roadway and helps prevent further accidents.

text: When you follow the road to the left, you have priority at the next junction.
explanation: LESSON 19 – ‘Junction and traffic sign’. It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time. The practice questions for the theory lessons are with voice.

text: The left and right lane are closed. There must be zip-merge. Car B drives first. Who can drive next?

options.text: Car A on the middle lane.
Car C on the left lane.

explanation: LESSON 2 – ‘The lanes’.The car in the middle lane gives first priority to the car on the right lane and then priority to the car on the left lane. Then car A may drive.

text: There is a bus lane to the right of the carriageway. In the last metres before turning right …

options.text: You must position yourself on the bus lane.
You may position yourself on the bus lane.
You may not position yourself on the bus lane.

explanation: LESSON 22With a car, it is prohibited on a bus lane to:- drive,- stop,- park.You may use the bus lane for the last metres before a junction in order to prepare for a left or right turn.You may also cross a bus lane:- at a junction,- to access a property (garage, shop, petrol station, house …).

text: Who has priority?
explanation: LESSON 20 – ‘Priority form the right’.It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time. The practice questions for the theory lessons are with voice.

text: Is the driver of the brown car allowed to overtake the blue one on the left?
explanation: LESSON 15 +16 – ‘Overtaking’.It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time. The practice questions for the theory lessons are with voice.

text: This blue sign “200 m” belongs …
explanation: LESSON 12It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time. The practice questions for the theory lessons are with voice.

text: At which intersection are you allowed to overtake a moped on the left?
explanation: LESSON 19Sign 1 = priority at the next intersection.Sign 2 = priority road.Sign 3 = priority from the right.At intersections where you have priority, you may overtake a moped.

text: This driver wants to turn right at this junction. Even if there are no other road users, the driver must first come to a complete stop before entering the junction.
explanation: LESSON 19If there is a STOP sign you must come to a complete stop.The give-way sign (inverted triangle) means that you must yield to other drivers and, if necessary, come to a complete stop.

text: An intersection without traffic signs. The driver of the white car stops briefly at the intersection and then wants to drive straight ahead. But the grey car suddenly turns left.

options.text: That is allowed, because the grey car comes from the right.
That is allowed, because the white car stopped.
That is not allowed, because the white car goes straight on.

explanation: LESSON 21Traffic going straight has priority over turning traffic.Even if the driver of the white car stops briefly, he keeps his priority.

text: You are driving your car in a new municipality in Flanders. What is the maximum speed you may drive past this sign on a normal road?
explanation: LESSON 6The yellow sign with a red border only indicates the administrative start of a municipality. It does NOT indicate the start of a built-up area and has no other meaning.

text: *** 5 points question *** A yellow arrow above a lane means …

options.text: ... you must take the first exit.

explanation: [Violations of the 3rd and 4th degree on our page Theory B: nr. 32]LESSON 18 – ‘Traffic lights’.It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time. The practice questions for the theory lessons are with voice.

text: From which speeding offence in a zone 30 may the police immediately withdraw the driving licence?

options.text: Driving more than 20 km/h over the limit.
Driving more than 30 km/h over the limit.
Driving more than 40 km/h over the limit.

explanation: LESSON 12 You risk an immediate withdrawal of your driving licence:- when you exceed the speed limit by more than 30 km/h on motorways, express roads and regular roads;- but in built-up areas, zone 30 areas or residential zones, already when you exceed the limit by more than 20 km/h.This immediate withdrawal is carried out by the police, because it concerns a serious offence.For any serious offence, the driving licence may be withdrawn immediately.

text: The blue car …

options.text: ... is allowed to turn left or drive straight through.

explanation: LESSON 24 – ‘Obligatory direction’. The sign next to the car says that the driver must drive straight through.

text: You approach this junction and you want to cross it. The oncoming car wants to turn left. Do you have to give it priority?
explanation: LESSON 21 – ‘Priority and changing directions’.If the traffic lights work, the board under the lights has no meaning.The traffic light is green, so you're allowed to drive straight through. Your oncoming vehicle (if it also has green light), wants to turn left and must want to give priority.

text: In a van, there is a front seat where the driver and two passengers can sit. What is the minimum required width of that seat?
explanation: LESSON 10The width must be enough for:Driver: 55 cm.Each passenger: 40 cm.Total: 55 + 40 + 40 = 135 cm.

text: What are you allowed to do under this bridge?

options.text: Stop and park on the roadway.
Stop and park on the shoulder.

explanation: LESSON 26Under a bridge, you may not stop (wait) or park on the roadway, but you may on the shoulder if there is one.Before this bridge, however, a sign prohibits stopping and parking on this side, both on the roadway and on the shoulder.

text: The driver of this car has stopped to answer the phone. Is he allowed to do that here?
explanation: LESSON 26Stopping to answer the phone is considered parking.On a road with a broken white line between the lanes, parking is prohibited.Only a brief stop to let someone get in or out is allowed.

text: This road is a short cut to your workplace. Are you allowed to drive on?
explanation: LESSON 23 – ‘Prohibited direction’.This sign means: no entry in both directions to any driver.

text: *** 5 points question *** A level crossing without white lights and no barriers. Is a car allowed to overtake a motorcycle on the left?
explanation: [Violations of the 3rd and 4th degree on our page Theory B: nr. 32]LESSON 15 +16 – ‘Overtaking’.It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time. The practice questions for the theory lessons are with voice.

text: Your car is parked in this street, which suddenly becomes a school street for half an hour. Are you allowed to leave the street with your car?

options.text: No, you must wait for half an hour.
Yes, if you drive at walking speed.

explanation: LESSON 6To reduce traffic at the start and end of the school day, a street near a school can be temporarily closed to motor vehicles. It then becomes a school street.The closure is indicated by sign C3 (no entry) together with an additional sign stating SCHOOL STREET.In principle, a permit is required to drive in a school street. However, leaving a parking space is allowed, provided that you drive at walking speed and proceed with extra caution.

text: Which car is allowed to cross first at the junction?
explanation: LESSON 19 – ‘Junction and traffic sign’. It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time. The practice questions for the theory lessons are with voice.

text: When you place a warning triangle on the breakdown lane, other drivers travelling in your direction must see the triangle from a distance of (…) meters.
explanation: LESSON 4 – ‘The motorway’. It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time.The practice questions for the theory lessons are voiced.

text: Is the driver of the blue car allowed to cross the junction?
explanation: LESSON 24 – ‘Obligatory direction’. The red sign says that it is forbidden to drive past the sign in that direction.

text: Which sign indicates a cycle path?
explanation: LESSON 3Sign 2: mandatory sign indicating that cyclists and also pedestrians must use this part of the public road.Sign 3: bicycle zone.

text: A junction without traffic lights or traffic signs. You are not allowed to park on the road or on the verge within 5 meters of the intersection with the edge of the transverse road. But are you allowed to be stationary there?
explanation: Explanation: See Lesson 25

text: This sign applies …
explanation: LESSON 23 – ‘Prohibited direction’.No entry to vehicles or combination of vehicles which load included, exceed the length shown.(See in your book also lesson 10).

text: *** 5 points question *** What is correct? In a residential area ...

options.text: ... is the maximum speed limit 25 km/hour.
... are cars allowed to park on the left and right of the direction of travel.
... may pedestrians and cyclists use the full lane.

explanation: [Violations of the 3rd and 4th degree on our page Theory B: nr. 32]LESSON 6 – ‘Special places’.The maximum speed limit is 20 km/hour.Only pedestrians may use the full road.

text: A roadway divided into lanes outside a built-up area. May the red truck overtake the white car on the left?
explanation: LESSON 16This prohibition sign indicates that trucks or combinations with a maximum authorised mass exceeding 3500 kg may not overtake:- a combination of vehicles, or- any vehicle with more than two wheels.The no-overtaking rule applies:- up to and including the next intersection, or- ends earlier if you see the “end of overtaking prohibition” sign.A car driver may therefore overtake a truck on the left after this sign.A bus may also overtake, since it is not a truck.

text: The width of a vehicle and its load is maximum …?
explanation: LESSON 10 – ‘The load and the passenger spaces’.A vehicle along with his load should not be wider than 2.55 meters. If wider = "exceptional transport".(Height: up to 4 m).

text: What is ‘autodelen’?

options.text: When multiple people use at the same a car to reach a destination.
Occasionally use a car, on pre-defined moments through reservation system.

explanation: LESSON 9 – ‘M.A.W. and M.G.W.’.People use the same car at a different time. You use the car when you need it. If you do not need the car, someone else can drive.

text: The driver of this car saw no other road users and carefully entered the intersection without stopping. Was he allowed to do that?

options.text: Yes, because there is no stop line on the road.

explanation: LESSON 19A STOP means you must come to a complete stop at the stop line and yield to drivers on the public road you want to enter.If there is no stop line on the pavement, you must stop at the traffic sign.Even if there are no drivers on the crossing road, you must still come to a complete stop before entering the intersection.

text: You are not allowed to park or to be stationary on a cycle lane. Are you allowed to drive on the cycle lane to pass another vehicle more safely?
explanation: Explanation: See Lesson 25

text: What is the maximum permitted speed for a car with studded tyres on a motorway?
explanation: LESSON 4Studded tyres may be used between 1 November and 31 March on vehicles with a maximum authorised mass up to 3.5 tonnes.Speed:– Motorways and roads with 2×2 lanes separated by a median: maximum 90 km/h.– Ordinary roads: maximum 60 km/h.

text: You drive with a diesel. What is the recommended speed (revs) to change gear?
explanation: Explanation: see lesson 30

text: Is the blue car allowed to drive on the lane to the right of him to change direction, the last meters before the junction?
explanation: LESSON 22It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time. The practice questions for the theory lessons are with voice.

text: May this motorcycle also be parked beyond the traffic sign?
explanation: LESSON 26This sign means that parking is allowed for a passenger car, a dual-purpose car, a minibus, and a motorcycle.A light truck is not allowed to park there.

text: Who is allowed to cross first at the junction?
explanation: LESSON 21 – ‘Priority and changing directions’.It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time. The practice questions for the theory lessons are with voice.

text: *** 5 points question *** Is the blue car allowed to overtake the brown lorry on the left?
explanation: [Violations of the 3rd and 4th degree on our page Theory B: nr. 32]LESSON 15 +16 – ‘Overtaking’.It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time. The practice questions for the theory lessons are with voice.

text: The driver of the brown car keeps driving on the left lane. Is the blue car allowed to overtake on the right?
explanation: LESSON 5 – ‘The express road’.It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time.The practice questions for the theory lessons are voiced.

text: Where do you have to drive 50kph?

options.text: As soon as you pass these signs.

explanation: LESSON 22It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time. The practice questions for the theory lessons are with voice.

text: The light is green: you may enter the intersection...

options.text: ... only if the intersection is clear.

explanation: LESSON 18Even with a green light, you may not enter the intersection if traffic from the opposite direction could block you and you risk obstructing the intersection.

text: Your car starts to skid. In which direction should you look?

options.text: Towards the direction you intended to go.

explanation: LESSON 31Although braking is probably your first instinct, you should avoid braking too hard. This can cause the wheels to lock and reduce traction.What should you do instead?Look in the direction you want to go. Unconsciously, you will steer towards where you are looking. You can imagine what happens if you keep looking at the danger.Steer in the opposite direction (counter-steer).Press the clutch and release the accelerator.

text: During a police control you are asked to do a breath test. How much waiting time can you ask for, before the test?
explanation: Explanation: See Lesson 28The 15-minute waiting period has been abolished since May 1, 2024

text: The red cars are parked on the roadway. Can the blue car stand still on the road for a passenger to get out?
explanation: LESSON 25It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time. The practice questions for the theory lessons are with voice.

text: Fill in a number. Beyond which sign are you not allowed to drive a car?
explanation: LESSON 23Sign 3: This prohibition sign means that drivers of motor vehicles with more than two wheels and motorcycles with a sidecar are not allowed to drive past the sign. In the opposite direction, they are allowed.Sign 1: End of motorway.Sign 2: End of expressway.Sign 4: Dead-end street.

text: What is the maximum permitted speed for the motorcycle on this N-road in Flanders?
explanation: LESSON 12An N-road is considered an ordinary road.In Flanders and in the Brussels Region, the maximum permitted speed on an ordinary road is 70 km/h.In Wallonia, it is 90 km/h.

text: A blind person is crossing the road at a place where there is no pedestrian crossing. You stop your car — but are you required to do so?

options.text: No, there is no pedestrian crossing, so you have priority.
You may stop; it is courteous behaviour.
You must give way to the blind person.

explanation: LESSON 7In Belgium, every driver (car, bicycle, etc.) is legally required to give way to a blind or visually impaired pedestrian,recognisable by a white cane, when that person is crossing or clearly intends to cross.This rule applies even if there is no pedestrian crossing.It also applies to other persons with reduced mobility, such as those using a walking frame or rollator.

text: *** 5 points question *** You are allowed to drive maximum (…) kph with a car on this road in Flanders.
explanation: [Violations of the 3rd and 4th degree on our page Theory B: nr. 32]Explanation: see lesson 12.It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time. The practice questions for the theory lessons are with voice.

text: The traffic light is green, but the crossroads are not yet free. May you stay on the zebra crossing while waiting for the intersection to be free?
explanation: LESSON 18 – ‘Traffic lights’. You must not cross the crossroads unless the light is green and the crossroads are free. But you cannot block the crossing point while waiting.

text: If snow chains are fitted around the tires, you can drive a maximum speed of (....) km/h in a built-up area in Flanders.
explanation: LESSON 31 – ‘Technique’.In a built-up area, the maximum permitted speed is 50 km / hour.

text: Must you (the blue car) also give priority to the right, when you drive on a one-way street?
explanation: LESSON 24 – ‘Obligatory direction’. If you're driving on a one-way road, you should also grant priority, except of course when there is a traffic sign indicating you have priority.In this example, the brown car may drive first.

text: You have to transport bicycles. You place them …

options.text: ... at the back of the car.
... on the roof of the car.

explanation: Explanation: see lesson 30

text: Within a built-up area you have two lanes in your driving direction. Can you continue to drive in the left lane?

options.text: Yes, always within a built-up area.
Yes, if you want to turn a little further to the left or park on the left.

explanation: LESSON 2 – ‘The lanes’.It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time. The practice questions for the theory lessons are with voice.

text: A cyclist wants to cross the road using the pedestrian crossing. Does he have priority over the car coming from the left?
explanation: LESSON 7If a cyclist wants to cross the road using a pedestrian crossing, he must get off the bicycle and cross on foot while holding the bike by hand.

text: A level crossing with barriers and lights. But the lights are out. Are you allowed to overtake a vehicle on the left?
explanation: LESSON 22It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time. The practice questions for the theory lessons are with voice.

text: *** 5 points question *** What is the maximum speed limit (… kph) for these cars on this express road within a built up area in Wallonia?
explanation: [Violations of the 3rd and 4th degree on our page Theory B: nr. 32]LESSON 12It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time. The practice questions for the theory lessons are with voice.

text: This girl’s moped has run out of fuel.

options.text: She may walk on the sidewalk.
She must walk on the sidewalk.
She must walk on the roadway.

explanation: LESSON 7A person pushing a broken-down moped is considered a pedestrian and must walk on the sidewalk.If there is no sidewalk, they may walk on the cycle path or on the roadway.

text: An intersection without traffic signs. The white car wants to turn left. The grey car wants to turn right. Who has the right of way?

options.text: Whoever turns first automatically has the right of way.

explanation: LESSON 21The grey car is turning right and taking the shorter turn. It has the right of way.

text: Is the black car allowed to overtake the grey car on the left?
explanation: LESSON 15 +16 – ‘Overtaking’.It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time. The practice questions for the theory lessons are with voice.

text: This traffic sign applies …

options.text: ... until you see a sign: End priority zone.

explanation: LESSON 19 – ‘Junction and traffic sign’. It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time. The practice questions for the theory lessons are with voice.

text: What is the maximum speed limit for a car passing these signs?

options.text: A car isn’t allowed to drive past these signs.

explanation: LESSON 23 – ‘Prohibited direction’.Up to 50 km/hour.

text: This cyclist wants to turn left inside a built-up area. May you overtake him on the right on a raised section of the road?

options.text: Yes, if you leave 1 metre of safe lateral distance.
Yes, if you leave 1.5 metres of safe lateral distance.

explanation: LESSON 16A cyclist who is about to turn left may be overtaken on the right on a raised section of the road.

text: You’re out of gas. Which vehicle are you allowed to push into the street on the right to refuel?

options.text: A two-wheeled moped or a motorcycle.

explanation: LESSON 23 – ‘Prohibited direction’.Someone who pushes a moped is a pedestrian.Someone who pushes a motorcycle is a driver.

text: The driver of this car is waiting for her friend within a built-up area. Is the car parked correctly?

options.text: Yes, because the car is in front of the traffic sign.

explanation: LESSON 26A broken white line divides the roadway into lanes.This means that parking on the roadway is not allowed. You may stop only briefly to let someone get in or out.Waiting for someone counts as parking.

text: What are you allowed to do on the left of this road?
explanation: LESSON 25 – ‘Waiting and parking’.On a road with one-way traffic you may wait and park on both sides.

text: May the red car park at that place inside the built-up area?
explanation: LESSON 26The traffic sign (E1) indicates that parking is prohibited on the roadway and on the verge on this side of the road.The white arrow below the sign shows that the prohibition starts from here.

text: On the motorway you have to drive minimum (…) km/hour in normal circumstances.
explanation: LESSON 4 – ‘The motorway’. It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time.The practice questions for the theory lessons are voiced.

text: A carriageway that is not divided into traffic lanes. The driver of the white car is waiting under this bridge for a colleague who will join the ride. Is this allowed?
explanation: LESSON 25On the carriageway, it is forbidden to stop or to park under a bridge.This rule applies at all times, whether or not the carriageway is divided into traffic lanes.

text: What does this sign mean?
explanation: LESSON 1 – ‘The public road’.It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time.The practice questions for the theory lessons are voiced.

text: What is the maximum speed limit of a car on this express road?
explanation: LESSON 5 – ‘The express road’.It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time.The practice questions for the theory lessons are voiced.

text: *** 5 points question *** The arrow you see here is a green filter arrow which indicates that the drivers who are already on the junction can drive safely to the left.
explanation: [Violations of the 3rd and 4th degree on our page Theory B: nr. 32]LESSON 18 – ‘Traffic lights’.It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time. The practice questions for the theory lessons are with voice.

text: A one-way street in a built-up area. What is the grey car on the left side of the road allowed to do?
explanation: LESSON 25On a one-way roadway, a car may be stopped or parked on either the right or the left side.

text: There are two lanes in your direction on this one way road, at the top of a hill. Are you allowed to overtake another car on the left?
explanation: LESSON 15 +16 – ‘Overtaking’.It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time. The practice questions for the theory lessons are with voice.

text: What does this traffic sign mean?
explanation: LESSON 14 – ‘Crossing’.It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time. The practice questions for the theory lessons are with voice.

text: Breakdown on an express road. May this woman call a friend to have her car towed?
explanation: LESSON 4 + 5Having a vehicle towed by family members or friends on a motorway or an express road is prohibited.In case of a breakdown, you must contact an authorised roadside assistance or towing service.

text: The pink car drives on the merging lane of a motorway. Who has priority?
explanation: LESSON 4 – ‘The motorway’.A driver who drives on the merging lane of a motorway, has to give way.

text: It is no longer snowing. Can the rear fog light stay on for a while?
explanation: Lesson 11 - 'Lights'It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time. The practice questions for the theory lessons are with voice.

text: Which answer is correct? Within a built-up area in the Brussels-Capital Region, you must ...

options.text: ... drive at least 30 kilometers per hour.
... drive at least 50 kilometers per hour.
... adapt your speed to the conditions.

explanation: LESSON 6

text: You approach a dangerous bend. Are you allowed to overtake a cyclist, who rides on the road, on the left?
explanation: LESSON 15 +16 – ‘Overtaking’.It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time. The practice questions for the theory lessons are with voice.

text: A car you can drive with a driving licence B is a car with a M.A.W. of maximum (…) kg.
explanation: LESSON 9 – ‘M.A.W. and M.G.W.’.It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time. The practice questions for the theory lessons are with voice.

text: A driver wants to insert. The driver of the purple car:

options.text: ... must drive for a while in the left lane.
... may drive for a while in the left lane.

explanation: LESSON 4- 'Motorway'.If that lane is clear, he may drive in that lane for a while to make the insertion easier. But it is not an obligation. (courteous driving behavior).

text: You have a temporary driving licence B. Past these signs you drive 73 km/hour. What are the consequences?

options.text: You will only get a fine.
You risk an immediate temporary suspension of your driving licence.
The judge will disqualify you from driving.

explanation: LESSON 6 – ‘Special places’.Exam Tip: read also very well in lesson 12 the difference between a fine and the prohibition of a right for the driving of vehicles.

text: A blind bend to the left. May the white car overtake this cyclist on the left?
explanation: LESSON 16In or before a dangerous bend, it is forbidden to overtake on the left a combination of vehicles, a vehicle with more than two wheels, or a two-wheeled motor vehicle.If visibility is very poor, you are also not allowed to overtake a cyclist.

text: Is this correct? Past these signs you are not allowed to be stationary or to park on the road or on the verge.
explanation: Explanation: See lesson 26

text: It is freezing. Are you allowed to briefly press the accelerator from time to time to keep the engine warm?
explanation: LESSON 30No. You are not allowed to press the accelerator to keep the engine warm. This causes unnecessary noise and air pollution.It is also recommended to switch off the engine if you have to stop for more than 30 seconds (for example at a level crossing or a bridge).Unnecessary idling or revving the engine while stationary is therefore not allowed.

text: Who has priority?
explanation: LESSON 20 – ‘Priority form the right’.It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time. The practice questions for the theory lessons are with voice.

text: Are you allowed to be stationary on the bus stop to let someone in or out?
explanation: Explanation: See lesson 26

text: Both cars are driving on this motorway at the maximum permitted speed. What safe following distance must they keep?
explanation: LESSON 13 – Explanation:The faster you drive, the greater the distance you must keep.You can calculate this distance using a simple formula:the speed divided by two.In this example, the cars are driving at 120 km/h.The safe following distance is therefore: 120 ÷ 2 = 60 metres.At 100 km/h, it becomes 100 ÷ 2 = 50 metres.

text: Which vehicles are you not allowed to overtake with your car after this sign?

options.text: Only a cyclist and a class A moped.
A cyclist, a class A moped and a motorcycle.

explanation: LESSON 3This sign marks the beginning of a bicycle zone.In a bicycle zone, motor vehicles (including mopeds) are not allowed to overtake cyclists, speed pedelecs and bicycles up to 1 m wide.Other vehicles may be overtaken if they are driving too slowly.The maximum permitted speed in a bicycle zone is 30 km/h.

text: Who has priority?
explanation: LESSON 21 – ‘Priority and changing directions’.It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time. The practice questions for the theory lessons are with voice.

text: If your vehicle breaks down on the hard shoulder of a motorway, do you also have to place a warning triangle?

options.text: No, only if the vehicle is on the carriageway.

explanation: LESSON 4 – ExplanationEven when your vehicle has broken down on the hard shoulder, placing a warning triangle is mandatory.On a motorway, it must be placed 100 metres in front of the vehicle.On other roads, the distance is 50 metres (or 30 metres in built-up areas).In built-up areas, the warning triangle may also be placed on the roof of the vehicle.The triangle must be visible from at least 50 metres for approaching drivers.

text: An accident without injuries. What should you do if one of the drivers refuses to sign the European accident report?

options.text: You sign it and inform the insurance company.

explanation: LESSON 29In an accident without injuries, you normally do not need to call the police, but the European accident report must be completed and signed by all drivers involved.By signing, you confirm that you agree with the information written on the form.Once everyone has signed, nothing can be changed.If one of the drivers refuses to sign the report, you call the police.

text: An ambulance with blue flashing lights and a warning siren. What do you do?

options.text: You drive to the side and give priority.

explanation: Explanation: see lesson 29

text: What part of the public road is marked by the yellow line?
explanation: LESSON 2 – ‘The lanes’.It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time.The practice questions for the theory lessons are voiced.

text: May a smartphone be used as a GPS in the car?

options.text: Yes, if it is placed in a fixed holder.

explanation: LESSON 31Using a smartphone as a GPS is allowed, as long as the device is placed in a fixed holder.Of course, you may only hold the smartphone in your hand when you are stopped or parked.

text: At which intersection are you allowed to overtake a cyclist on the left?
explanation: LESSON 19Sign 1 = priority at the next intersection.Sign 2 = priority road.Sign 3 = priority from the right.

text: Beyond which sign can you stop at the place where the word BUS stands (to let someone get out)?
explanation: LESSON 22 - 'Train - tram - bus'.Board 1: special reserved route for buses. Board 2: bus lane. Parking prohibited.

text: Are you allowed to park on the verge in front of this sign?
explanation: Explanation: See lesson 26

text: Which traffic sign can replace the blue mandatory sign to obtain the same result?
explanation: LESSON 241 = Danger sign: succession of dangerous bends.2 = Prohibition sign: no right turn.3 = Danger sign: traffic allowed in both directions after a section of the road with one-way traffic.

text: A tyre has four DOT digits (xxxx). These digits indicate when the tyre was manufactured. What do they mean?

options.text: The first two digits indicate the year and the last two the week.
The first two digits indicate the week and the last two the year.

explanation: LESSON 31The DOT number (Department of Transportation) on a tyre indicates the manufacturing date.It consists of 4 digits:- the first two digits indicate the week of production;- the last two digits indicate the year of production.

text: The judge is obliged to impose a revocation of the right to drive a motor vehicle for speeding in a built-up area by more than …
explanation: LESSON 12If you exceed the maximum speed limit by more than 40 km/h on a motorway, a road for motor vehicles, or an ordinary road, you risk a revocation of the right to drive a motor vehicle. In addition, if you exceed the maximum speed by more than 30 km/h in a built-up area, in a 30-zone, or in a residential area, you also risk a revocation of the right to drive a motor vehicle. This is not a decision taken by the police, but by a judge in court, when your case is examined.

text: Are you allowed to turn around, on the checker-board markings at an intersection?
explanation: LESSON 22 - 'Train - tram- bus'.

text: You drive your car on the right lane of this motorway. What is the maximum speed limit?
explanation: LESSON 22It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time. The practice questions for the theory lessons are with voice.

text: You have hit a cyclist. What do you do after placing the warning triangle and notifying the emergency services?

options.text: You move him off the road.
You apply a pressure bandage on his bleeding arm.
You do nothing and wait for the emergency services.

explanation: LESSON 29An injured person should always be left in place. Do not give them food or drink. If they are bleeding, apply a pressure bandage to the wound.

text: Are you allowed to drive past these signs with a car?
explanation: LESSON 23 – ‘Prohibited direction’.This prohibitive sign indicates no entry to any driver (including cyclists) to drive past this sign in this direction.

text: It is eleven o’clock. Where do you put the arrow on the parking disc?
explanation: Explanation: See Lesson 27

text: Is this car correctly parked in this 30-zone?
explanation: LESSON 25Vehicles must be parked on the right side of the roadway, in the direction of travel.

text: What does this information sign mean?

options.text: End of a built up area.

explanation: LESSON 6 – ‘Special places’.It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time.The practice questions for the theory lessons are voiced.

text: The function of motor oil. 1. Has a cleaning and lubricating function. 2. Ensures that the moving parts don’t touch each other. 3. Prevents the motor from blocking. 4. All above are correct.
explanation: Explanation: See lesson 31

text: You are approaching a red traffic light. You press the clutch pedal.
explanation: It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time. The practice questions for the theory lessons are with voice.

text: Once you are past this traffic sign you are allowed to make a U-turn again.
explanation: LESSON 23 – ‘Prohibited direction’.This sign indicates that form this sign on until the next junction (also there) a U turn is prohibited.

text: When you phone with a hands free kit, you pay less attention to the traffic as well as without a hands free kit.
explanation: Explanation: see lesson 29

text: This picture is taken within a built up area. Are you allowed to park your car on the road just past this sign?
explanation: Explanation: See lesson 26

text: *** 5 points question *** Can you overtake a moped on the left at this level crossing?

options.text: No, overtaking on the left is forbidden,

explanation: LESSON 22 - 'Train, tram, bus'.It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time. The practice questions for the theory lessons are with voice.

text: Are you allowed to follow an ambulance with your heavily injured father on board, if it is driving faster than the maximum speed limit?
explanation: Explanation: see lesson 29

text: Past these signs you leave …
explanation: LESSON 6 – ‘Special places’.It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time.The practice questions for the theory lessons are voiced.

text: The white car is allowed, at that place ...

options.text: Neither to stop nor to park.

explanation: LESSON 26This round traffic sign, with one diagonal stripe, indicates that on the side where the sign is placed, parking is prohibited on both the carriageway and the shoulder, up to the next intersection.

text: When are snow chains allowed?

options.text: When there is snow or ice on the road.
Between the 1st November until the 31st March.

explanation: Explanation: See lesson 31

text: What is the maximum speed allowed for the white car on this road in the Flemish Region?
explanation: LESSON 5It is a normal carriageway divided into two lanes.The maximum permitted speed in the Flemish and Brussels Regions is 70 km/h.In the Walloon Region, it is 90 km/h.

text: You do not live in this house. In front of which garage entrance are you allowed to stop on the carriageway?

options.text: Neither in front of garage 1 nor garage 2.

explanation: LESSON 26Parking in front of a garage entrance or driveway is only allowed if the vehicle’s licence plate is clearly displayed.Stopping (for example to let a passenger get in or out) is generally allowed.

text: May the white car park at that place inside the built-up area?
explanation: LESSON 26The traffic sign (E1) indicates that parking is prohibited on the roadway and on the verge on this side of the road.The white arrow below the sign shows that the prohibition starts from here.

text: What does E5 refer to?

options.text: The octane content of the petrol.

explanation: Since 2019, fuel is primarily designated by a name that indicates the maximum amount of bioethanol mixed in. Bioethanol is an alcohol made by fermenting sugar, corn or wheat. This is therefore a form of renewable energy.

text: You have had your definitive driver's license for two years. Will the police also take a breath test from your passenger?
explanation: LESSON 28 - "Alcohol."It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time. The practice questions for the theory lessons are with voice.

text: Within a built up area. The blue car is … here.

options.text: allowed to be stationary or to park.
not allowed to be stationary or to park

explanation: Explanation: See lesson 26

text: Which driver is not allowed to cross the junction?

options.text: From the car and the moped.

explanation: LESSON 18 – ‘Traffic lights’.It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time. The practice questions for the theory lessons are with voice.

text: Does the ambulance with flashing lights and warning signal have to stop?
explanation: LESSON 17 – ‘Qualified persons’.It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time. The practice questions for the theory lessons are with voice.

text: What is the meaning of this sign?
It’s warm and you’re driving with the window open. Does this affect fuel consumption?
explanation: LESSON 30Driving with the window open affects fuel consumption.When the window is open, the vehicle’s air resistance increases.At low speeds this effect is limited, but at higher speeds the added drag causes a noticeable rise in fuel consumption — up to 5–10% more at highway speed.

text: On this express road In Wallonia with 2x2 lanes, a car is allowed to drive maximum (…) km/hour.
explanation: LESSON 5 – ‘The express road’.In Flanders: 70 kph unless traffic signs or rules impose a different speed limit.In Wallonia and Brussels-capital region: 90 kph.

text: What do you do when there is a big fire in a tunnel?

options.text: You reverse to exit the tunnel.
You exit the tunnel through an emergency exit.

explanation: Explanation: see lesson 29

text: The photo is taken from the car you are driving. You want to enter the motorway. Which statement is correct?

options.text: You must drive to the very end of the acceleration lane.

explanation: LESSON 4When you enter a motorway via an acceleration lane,you must give way to traffic already driving on the motorway.That is why there is a yield (inverted triangle) road sign.You are not required to drive to the end of the acceleration lane.You may merge as soon as you have enough speed and it can be done safely.

text: When is it permitted to drive on this road marking?

options.text: In order to reach your property.
In order to reach your property or to turn at a junction.

explanation: LESSON 23 – ‘Prohibited direction’.This is a traffic displacement area (see rule in your book chapter 2).

text: At home you notice that you forgot to draw something important on the situational sketch.

options.text: You are still allowed to draw extra.
You are not allowed to change anything on the form.

explanation: Explanation: see lesson 29

text: What must drivers do who are on the road that is blocked by the police officer’s horizontally extended arm?
explanation: LESSON 17When a police officer extends one or both arms horizontally, all drivers approaching the officer’s front or back must stop.➡️ Continuing to drive or turning, as this driver intends to do, is a fourth-degree offence.

text: Can someone with epileptic seizures drive a car?

options.text: Never, because they can always have another seizure.
Only after a seizure-free period can a doctor grant permission to drive.

explanation: Explanation:A person with epileptic seizures is generally not allowed to drive.After a first seizure, there is a driving ban of 6 months.Someone with chronic epilepsy who, after treatment, has been seizure-free for 1 year may, with approval from a specialist doctor, be allowed to drive again.After a new seizure, there is again a driving ban of 1 year.

text: Who is allowed to cross first at the junction?
explanation: LESSON 19 – ‘Junction and traffic sign’. It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time. The practice questions for the theory lessons are with voice.

text: Who is the first to cross the intersection?
explanation: LESSON 19 – ‘Junction and traffic sign’. A STOP means that you must stop and give way to the drivers (not the pedestrians) that run on the track you are going to takeA pedestrian is not a driver and there is no pedestrian crossing.

text: What does this traffic sign mean?
explanation: LESSON 19 – ‘Junction and traffic sign’. It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time. The practice questions for the theory lessons are with voice.

text: How tall must a child be to no longer be required to sit in an appropriate safety seat?
explanation: LESSON 10Children under the age of 18 and smaller than 1m35 must be transported in an appropriate safety seat or child restraint system that complies with the prescribed standards. (A child taller than 1m35 may still be transported in a special child seat). Children under 18 years old may not be transported in the front seat in a rear-facing child seat, unless there is no front airbag or the airbag can be deactivated.

text: You are waiting at a drawbridge, while it is freezing outside. May you keep pressing the accelerator to keep the engine warm?
explanation: LESSON 30If you have to wait longer than 30 seconds, you should switch off the engine.Continuously pressing the accelerator to keep the engine warm is not allowed, as it causes unnecessary pollution and noise.

text: *** 5 points question *** What does this sign indicate?
explanation: [Violations of the 3rd and 4th degree on our page Theory B: nr. 32]LESSON 23 – ‘Prohibited direction’.Tip exam: learn very well in your book (chapter 9) the difference between M.A.W. and M.G.W.

text: On a public area, such as a petrol station, you can’t be fined for any offence.
explanation: LESSON 1 – ‘The public road’.It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time.The practice questions for the theory lessons are voiced.

text: The brown car wants to turn left. Is the blue car allowed to overtake the brown one on the right?
explanation: LESSON 15 +16 – ‘Overtaking’.It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time. The practice questions for the theory lessons are with voice.

text: *** 5 points question *** What is the maximum speed limit (… kph) for these cars at that location in Flanders?
explanation: [Violations of the 3rd and 4th degree on our page Theory B: nr. 32]Explanation: see lesson 12.In Wallonia 90 km/h.In Brussels region also 70 km/h.

text: You have a provisional licence B. What time are you not allowed to drive a car anymore on a Friday evening?
explanation: LESSON 1 – ‘The public road’.It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time.The practice questions for the theory lessons are voiced.

text: *** 5 points question *** Which picture is the right one?
explanation: [Violations of the 3rd and 4th degree on our page Theory B: nr. 32]LESSON 14 – ‘Crossing’.It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time. The practice questions for the theory lessons are with voice.

text: What is this part of the public road, with the question mark, called?
explanation: LESSON 2 – ‘The lanes’.It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time.The practice questions for the theory lessons are voiced.

text: May the car stop at that place within a built-up area to let a passenger get in?
explanation: LESSON 7It is forbidden to park or stop on a pedestrian crossing, even to let someone get in or out.It is also forbidden to park or to stop on the roadway within 5 metres before the crossing (parking on the verge is allowed if possible).The same rule applies to crossings for cyclists and two-wheeled mopeds.After the crossing, parking and stopping are allowed, unless prohibited by traffic signs.

text: A passenger sitting in the back seat of a car...

options.text: ... is recommended to wear a seat belt.

explanation: LESSON 10 – ‘The load and the passenger spaces’.

text: Driving onto a level crossing when the red flashing light is operating and the barrier is descending is an offence of the …
explanation: LESSON 4 / OffencesFourth-degree offences are the most serious traffic violations.They directly endanger people’s safety and, in the event of a collision, almost inevitably cause physical injury.Examples include:- ignoring the orders of an authorised person,- not respecting the signalling at a level crossing,- stopping or parking on a level crossing,- encouraging excessive speed,- organising speed races on public roads,- overtaking on the left on a hill or in a bend when this is prohibited,- reversing or driving in the opposite direction on a motorway or expressway.

text: The owner of this car has already been inside the house for several minutes. The car is:
explanation: LESSON 25Stopping/waiting is the time needed to let someone get in or out of the car, or to load/unload goods.The car is therefore parked.

text: Your car is broken down. Is your friend allowed to tow your car on the highway?
*** 5 points question *** In a residential area or estate you are allowed to drive maximum (…) km/hour.
explanation: [Violations of the 3rd and 4th degree on our page Theory B: nr. 32]LESSON 6 – ‘Special places’.It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time.The practice questions for the theory lessons are voiced.

text: The black car (yellow circle) is allowed to drive maximum (…) kph on the motorway on that spot.
explanation: LESSON 4 – ‘The motorway’. It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time.The practice questions for the theory lessons are voiced.

text: A junction with traffic lights. You are not allowed to be stationary or to park on the road or on the verge within (…) meters in front of the traffic lights.
explanation: LESSON 25 – ‘Waiting and parking’.You are not allowed to be stationary or to park on the road and on the verge at a junction with traffic lights within 20 meters of the traffic lights.

text: What does this traffic sign mean?

options.text: Advanced road sign indicating a temporary lane diversion.
Advanced road sign indicating a temporary crossover on the verge.
Advance road sign indicating a temporary lane closure.

explanation: LESSON 2 – ‘The lanes’.It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time.The practice questions for the theory lessons are voiced.

text: What is the maximum speed limit for the blue car on this motorway?
explanation: LESSON 4 – ‘The motorway’. The speed limit only applies to the bus lane.

text: This picture is taken from your car. Are you allowed to overtake the cyclist on the left?
explanation: LESSON 15 +16 – ‘Overtaking’.It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time. The practice questions for the theory lessons are with voice.

text: Who is the last one to cross the junction?
explanation: LESSON 20 – ‘Priority form the right’.It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time. The practice questions for the theory lessons are with voice.

text: This roadway is divided into two lanes. What is the maximum speed allowed in the Brussels Region after passing the yellow sign?
explanation: LESSON 12It is a normal roadway divided into two lanes.In the Walloon Region, the maximum permitted speed is 90 km/h.In the Flemish and Brussels Regions, it is 70 km/h.The yellow sign has nothing to do with speed — it is a priority-road sign indicating that you are driving on a priority road.

text: Past this sign motorcycles and vehicles with a M.A.W. of 3.5 ton are allowed to park.
explanation: Explanation: See Lesson 27

text: The photo is taken from the car you are driving. Who has the right of way?
explanation: LESSON 20There is no police officer, no traffic lights, and no signs regulating priority. Therefore, the right-hand priority rule applies at the intersection.

text: You drive past this sign on a motorway. On the left lane you are allowed to drive maximum (…) kph.
explanation: LESSON 12It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time. The practice questions for the theory lessons are with voice.

text: A charging station in a municipality. When may electric and plug-in hybrid vehicles park there?

options.text: Only if they are connected to the charging station.

explanation: LESSON 27Fully electric vehicles and plug-in hybrid vehicles (PHEV) may park there only if they are actually connected to the charging station.These vehicles may not park there without charging.

text: *** 5 points question *** A suggested/reserved cycle lane. When passing a car …

options.text: ... you are not allowed to drive on it.
... you are allowed to drive on it.

explanation: [Violations of the 3rd and 4th degree on our page Theory B: nr. 32]LESSON 14 – ‘Crossing’.It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time. The practice questions for the theory lessons are with voice.

text: This sign indicates: no entry to drivers of vehicles which, load included, exceed the width shown. What kind of sign is this?
explanation: LESSON 10 – ‘The load and the passenger spaces’.It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time. The practice questions for the theory lessons are with voice.

text: What should you do if your vehicle starts aquaplaning?

options.text: Brake hard and steer to regain control.
Release the accelerator, do not brake and keep the steering wheel straight.
Accelerate so that the tyres regain grip.

explanation: LESSON 31Aquaplaning is a phenomenon in which the tyres lose contact with the road because of a layer of water.If your vehicle starts aquaplaning, release the accelerator, do not brake and keep the steering wheel as straight as possible.Avoid sudden steering movements. Control will gradually return once the tyres regain contact with the road.

text: The red car has stopped to let a passenger get out. Is this allowed?
explanation: LESSON 26This traffic sign means that parking is prohibited on this side of the carriageway and also on the verge.The additional plate with the black downward arrow indicates that the parking prohibition ends at the sign.➡️ However: beyond the sign, the carriageway is divided into two lanes by a broken white line.On such a carriageway, parking is not allowed.➡️ Stopping (for example to allow a passenger to get in or out) is allowed.

text: Where must the reflective safety vest be located?

options.text: Inside the interior of the car.
In the trunk of the car.

explanation: LESSON 4 - 'Motorway'The reflective safety vest, also known as the yellow vest, must be located inside the vehicle’s interior, within easy reach, and not in the trunk. It is recommended to store it in the glove compartment, under the driver’s seat, or in a door pocket so that it is immediately accessible to the driver if they need to exit the vehicle on a motorway or a road for motor vehicles.

text: An intersection without traffic signs. The white car wants to go straight ahead. The grey car wants to turn left. Who has priority?
explanation: LESSON 21Traffic going straight has priority over traffic that is turning.

text: There is an accident without casualties. Are you allowed to leave the four hazard warning lights on?
explanation: LESSON 11 – ‘The lights’.It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time. The practice questions for the theory lessons are with voice.

text: Is oncoming traffic from the other direction possible?
explanation: LESSON 23 – ‘Prohibited direction’.This prohibitive sign indicates no entry to any driver (including cyclists) to drive past this sign in this direction.

text: Does the sign that ends all local prohibitions also put an end to parking signs?
explanation: LESSON 26The sign with a black diagonal stripe informs road users of the end of all regulations previously indicated by signs, except those concerning stopping and parking.

text: You are allowed to be stationary on a priority road …

options.text: ... within or outside a built up area.

explanation: Explanation: See lesson 26

text: What are you allowed to do within 15 meters before and after the sign indicating a bus stop?

options.text: No parking, but stopping is allowed.

explanation: LESSON 26Within 15 meters before and after a bus stop, parking is not allowed. However, you are allowed to stop briefly to let passengers get in or out.

text: After which signs do you have priority?
explanation: LESSON 19- Sign 1 – B21: Narrow passage.You have priority over traffic coming from the opposite direction.- Sign 2 – A39: Two-way traffic after a one-way section.This sign does not grant priority.- Sign 3 – B19: Narrow passage.You must give priority to oncoming traffic — so you do not have priority.

text: When are you required to use your direction indicator?

options.text: When entering and leaving a roundabout.

explanation: LESSON 19When entering a roundabout, you may use your indicator, but it is not mandatory.When leaving a roundabout, you must use the right indicator to show that you are exiting.

text: You are driving at 75 km/h within a built-up area in Flanders. What are the consequences?

options.text: An immediate withdrawal of your driving licence.
You will have to appear in court.

explanation: LESSON 121. If you drive in a built-up area, a 30-zone, or a residential area at more than 20 km/h above the speed limit, you risk an immediate withdrawal of your driving licence. This withdrawal is carried out by the police, because it is considered a serious offence. For any serious offence, your licence can be taken away on the spot.2. In a built-up area, a 30-zone, or a residential area, if you exceed the speed limit by more than 30 km/h, you risk a driving ban pronounced by the judge in court. Depending on the ruling, you may be prohibited from driving any motor vehicle (even those not requiring a licence) for a period ranging from at least 8 days up to 5 years. For novice drivers (< 2 years with a full category B licence), the rules are even stricter.

text: An accident without casualties and material damage only. Is it enough that the people involved fill in a European/International Accident Form?
explanation: Explanation: see lesson 29

text: May the car overtake the truck on the left?
explanation: LESSON 16The red circular prohibition sign indicates that drivers are forbidden to:- overtake a combination of vehicles, or- overtake any vehicle with more than two wheels.The no-overtaking rule applies:- up to and including the next intersection, or- it ends earlier if you see the end-of-prohibition sign.A car driver may therefore overtake a two-wheeled motorcycle.But the motorcyclist may not overtake a car, because a car has more than two wheels.

text: May this car with caravan, with a total length of 12 metres, pass this traffic sign?

options.text: Yes, because the towing vehicle is a car.

explanation: LESSON 10This prohibition sign prohibits access to all vehicles (not only lorries) whose total length, including load and trailer, exceeds the length indicated on the sign.This therefore also applies to drivers of a vehicle combination:when your car is towing a caravan, you are driving a vehicle combination.(Vehicle + trailer = vehicle combination)

text: *** 5 points question *** Is a motorcycle allowed to overtake a car on the left past these signs?
explanation: [Violations of the 3rd and 4th degree on our page Theory B: nr. 32]LESSON 15 +16 – ‘Overtaking’.It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time. The practice questions for the theory lessons are with voice.

text: When you see these two signs together, you know the speed limit only applies during the schooldays.
explanation: LESSON 6 – ‘Special places’.It is very important to read the theory lessons if you want to pass the real exam from the first time.The practice questions for the theory lessons are voiced.

text: Which vehicles are allowed to drive past these signs?
